texts.psa.39.11: When thou with rebukes dost correct man for iniquity, Thou makest his beauty to consume away like a moth: Surely every man is vanity. Selah
texts.psa.39.12: Hear my prayer, O Jehovah, and give ear unto my cry; Hold not thy peace at my tears: For I am a stranger with thee, A sojourner, as all my fathers were.
texts.psa.39.13: Oh spare me, that I may recover strength, Before I go hence, and be no more.
texts.psa.40.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. I waited patiently for Jehovah; And he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
texts.psa.40.2: He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay; And he set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.
texts.psa.40.3: And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: Many shall see it, and fear, And shall trust in Jehovah.
texts.psa.40.4: Blessed is the man that maketh Jehovah his trust, And respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.
texts.psa.40.5: Many, O Jehovah my God, are the wonderful works which thou hast done, And thy thoughts which are to us-ward; They cannot be set in order unto thee; If I would declare and speak of them, They are more than can be numbered.
texts.psa.40.6: Sacrifice and offering thou hast no delight in; Mine ears hast thou opened: Burnt-offering and sin-offering hast thou not required.
texts.psa.40.7: Then said I, Lo, I am come; In the roll of the book it is written of me:
texts.psa.40.8: I delight to do thy will, O my God; Yea, thy law is within my heart.
texts.psa.40.9: I have proclaimed glad tidings of righteousness in the great assembly; Lo, I will not refrain my lips, O Jehovah, thou knowest.
texts.psa.40.10: I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared thy faithfulness and thy salvation; I have not concealed thy lovingkindness and thy truth from the great assembly.
texts.psa.40.11: Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O Jehovah; Let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me.
texts.psa.40.12: For innumerable evils have compassed me about; Mine iniquities have overtaken me, so that I am not able to look up; They are more than the hairs of my head; And my heart hath failed me.
texts.psa.40.13: Be pleased, O Jehovah, to deliver me: Make haste to help me, O Jehovah.
texts.psa.40.14: Let them be put to shame and confounded together That seek after my soul to destroy it: Let them be turned backward and brought to dishonor That delight in my hurt.
texts.psa.40.15: Let them be desolate by reason of their shame That say unto me, Aha, aha.
texts.psa.40.16: Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: Let such as love thy salvation say continually, Jehovah be magnified.
texts.psa.40.17: But I am poor and needy; [Yet] the Lord thinketh upon me: Thou art my help and my deliverer; Make no tarrying, O my God.
texts.psa.41.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. Blessed is he that considereth the poor: Jehovah will deliver him in the day of evil.
texts.psa.41.2: Jehovah will preserve him, and keep him alive, And he shall be blessed upon the earth; And deliver not thou him unto the will of his enemies.
texts.psa.41.3: Jehovah will support him upon the couch of languishing: Thou makest all his bed in his sickness.
texts.psa.41.4: I said, O Jehovah, have mercy upon me: Heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee.
texts.psa.41.5: Mine enemies speak evil against me, [saying], When will he die, and his name perish?
texts.psa.41.6: And if he come to see [me], he speaketh falsehood; His heart gathereth iniquity to itself: When he goeth abroad, he telleth it.
texts.psa.41.7: All that hate me whisper together against me; Against me do they devise my hurt.
texts.psa.41.8: An evil disease, [say they], cleaveth fast unto him; And now that he lieth he shall rise up no more.
texts.psa.41.9: Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, Who did eat of my bread, Hath lifted up his heel against me.
texts.psa.41.10: But thou, O Jehovah, have mercy upon me, and raise me up, That I may requite them.
texts.psa.41.11: By this I know that thou delightest in me, Because mine enemy doth not triumph over me.
texts.psa.41.12: And as for me, thou upholdest me in mine integrity, And settest me before thy face for ever.
texts.psa.41.13: Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, From everlasting and to everlasting. Amen, and Amen. I
texts.psa.42.1: For the Chief Musician. Maschil of the sons of Korah. As the hart panteth after the water brooks, So panteth my soul after thee, O God.
texts.psa.42.2: My soul thirsteth for God, for the living God: When shall I come and appear before God?
texts.psa.42.3: My tears have been my food day and night, While they continually say unto me, Where is thy God?
texts.psa.42.4: These things I remember, and pour out my soul within me, How I went with the throng, and led them to the house of God, With the voice of joy and praise, a multitude keeping holyday.
texts.psa.42.5: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? And [why] art thou disquieted within me? Hope thou in God; for I shall yet praise him [For] the help of his countenance.
texts.psa.42.6: O my God, my soul is cast down within me: Therefore do I remember thee from the land of the Jordan, And the Hermons, from the hill Mizar.
texts.psa.42.7: Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterfalls: All thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.
texts.psa.42.8: [Yet] Jehovah will command his lovingkindness in the day-time; And in the night his song shall be with me, [Even] a prayer unto the God of my life.
texts.psa.42.9: I will say unto God my rock, Why hast thou forgotten me? Why go I mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?
texts.psa.42.10: As with a sword in my bones, mine adversaries reproach me, While they continually say unto me, Where is thy God?
texts.psa.42.11: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? And why art thou disquieted within me? Hope thou in God; for I shall yet praise him, [Who is] the help of my countenance, and my God.
texts.psa.43.1: Judge me, O God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation: Oh deliver me from the deceitful and unjust man.
texts.psa.43.2: For thou art the God of my strength; why hast thou cast me off? Why go I mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?
texts.psa.43.3: Oh send out thy light and thy truth; let them lead me: Let them bring me unto thy holy hill, And to thy tabernacles.
texts.psa.43.4: Then will I go unto the altar of God, Unto God my exceeding joy; And upon the harp will I praise thee, O God, my God.
texts.psa.43.5: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? And why art thou disquieted within me? Hope thou in God; for I shall yet praise him, [Who is] the help of my countenance, and my God.
texts.psa.44.1: For the Chief Musician. [A Psalm] of the sons of Korah. Maschil. We have heard with our ears, O God, Our fathers have told us, What work thou didst in their days, In the days of old.
texts.psa.44.2: Thou didst drive out the nations with thy hand; But them thou didst plant: Thou didst afflict the peoples; But them thou didst spread abroad.
texts.psa.44.3: For they gat not the land in possession by their own sword, Neither did their own arm save them; But thy right hand, and thine arm, and the light of thy countenance, Because thou wast favorable unto them.
texts.psa.44.4: Thou art my King, O God: Command deliverance for Jacob.
texts.psa.44.5: Through thee will we push down our adversaries: Through thy name will we tread them under that rise up against us.
texts.psa.44.6: For I will not trust in my bow, Neither shall my sword save me.
texts.psa.44.7: But thou hast saved us from our adversaries, And hast put them to shame that hate us.
texts.psa.44.8: In God have we made our boast all the day long, And we will give thanks unto thy name for ever. Selah
texts.psa.44.9: But now thou hast cast [us] off, and brought us to dishonor, And goest not forth with our hosts.
texts.psa.44.10: Thou makest us to turn back from the adversary; And they that hate us take spoil for themselves.
texts.psa.44.11: Thou hast made us like sheep [appointed] for food, And hast scattered us among the nations.
texts.psa.44.12: Thou sellest thy people for nought, And hast not increased [thy wealth] by their price.
texts.psa.44.13: Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbors, A scoffing and a derision to them that are round about us.
texts.psa.44.14: Thou makest us a byword among the nations, A shaking of the head among the peoples.
texts.psa.44.15: All the day long is my dishonor before me, And the shame of my face hath covered me,
texts.psa.44.16: For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth, By reason of the enemy and the avenger.
texts.psa.44.17: All this is come upon us; Yet have we not forgotten thee, Neither have we dealt falsely in thy covenant.
texts.psa.44.18: Our heart is not turned back, Neither have our steps declined from thy way,
texts.psa.44.19: That thou hast sore broken us in the place of jackals, And covered us with the shadow of death.
texts.psa.44.20: If we have forgotten the name of our God, Or spread forth our hands to a strange god;
texts.psa.44.21: Will not God search this out? For he knoweth the secrets of the heart.
texts.psa.44.22: Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; We are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.
texts.psa.44.23: Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? Arise, cast [us] not off for ever.
texts.psa.44.24: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, And forgettest our affliction and our oppression?
texts.psa.44.25: For our soul is bowed down to the dust: Our body cleaveth unto the earth.
texts.psa.44.26: Rise up for our help, And redeem us for thy lovingkindness' sake.
texts.psa.45.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Shoshannim. [A Psalm] of the sons of Korah. Maschil. A Song of loves. My heart overfloweth with a goodly matter; I speak the things which I have made touching the king: My tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
texts.psa.45.2: Thou art fairer than the children of men; Grace is poured into thy lips: Therefore God hath blessed thee for ever.
texts.psa.45.3: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O mighty one, Thy glory and thy majesty.
texts.psa.45.4: And in thy majesty ride on prosperously, Because of truth and meekness [and] righteousness: And thy right hand shall teach thee terrible things.
texts.psa.45.5: Thine arrows are sharp; The peoples fall under thee; [They are] in the heart of the king's enemies.
texts.psa.45.6: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: A sceptre of equity is the sceptre of thy kingdom.
texts.psa.45.7: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated wickedness: Therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee With the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
texts.psa.45.8: All thy garments [smell of] myrrh, and aloes, [and] cassia; Out of ivory palaces stringed instruments have made thee glad.
texts.psa.45.9: Kings' daughters are among thy honorable women: At thy right hand doth stand the queen in gold of Ophir.
texts.psa.45.10: Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; Forget also thine own people, and thy father's house:
texts.psa.45.11: So will the king desire thy beauty; For he is thy lord; and reverence thou him.
texts.psa.45.12: And the daughter of Tyre [shall be there] with a gift; The rich among the people shall entreat thy favor.
texts.psa.45.13: The king's daughter within [the palace] is all glorious: Her clothing is inwrought with gold.
texts.psa.45.14: She shall be led unto the king in broidered work: The virgins her companions that follow her Shall be brought unto thee.
texts.psa.45.15: With gladness and rejoicing shall they be led: They shall enter into the king's palace.
texts.psa.45.16: Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, Whom thou shalt make princes in all the earth.
texts.psa.45.17: I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations: Therefore shall the peoples give thee thanks for ever and ever.
texts.psa.46.1: For the Chief Musician. [A Psalm] of the sons of Korah; set to Alamoth. A Song. God is our refuge and strength, A very present help in trouble.
texts.psa.46.2: Therefore will we not fear, though the earth do change, And though the mountains be shaken into the heart of the seas;
texts.psa.46.3: Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, Though the mountains tremble with the swelling thereof. Selah
texts.psa.46.4: There is a river, the streams whereof make glad the city of God, The holy place of the tabernacles of the Most High.
texts.psa.46.5: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God will help her, and that right early.
texts.psa.46.6: The nations raged, the kingdoms were moved: He uttered his voice, the earth melted.
texts.psa.46.7: Jehovah of hosts is with us; The God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah
texts.psa.46.8: Come, behold the works of Jehovah, What desolations he hath made in the earth.
texts.psa.46.9: He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; He breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; He burneth the chariots in the fire.
texts.psa.46.10: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.
texts.psa.46.11: Jehovah of hosts is with us; The God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah
texts.psa.47.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Oh clap your hands, all ye peoples; Shout unto God with the voice of triumph.
texts.psa.47.2: For Jehovah Most High is terrible; He is a great King over all the earth.
texts.psa.47.3: He subdueth peoples under us, And nations under our feet.
texts.psa.47.4: He chooseth our inheritance for us, The glory of Jacob whom he loved. Selah
texts.psa.47.5: God is gone up with a shout, Jehovah with the sound of a trumpet.
texts.psa.47.6: Sing praise to God, sing praises: Sing praises unto our King, sing praises.
texts.psa.47.7: For God is the King of all the earth: Sing ye praises with understanding.
texts.psa.47.8: God reigneth over the nations: God sitteth upon his holy throne.
texts.psa.47.9: The princes of the peoples are gathered together [To be] the people of the God of Abraham: For the shields of the earth belong unto God; He is greatly exalted.
texts.psa.48.1: A Song; a Psalm of the sons of Korah. Great is Jehovah, and greatly to be praised, In the city of our God, in his holy mountain.
texts.psa.48.2: Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth, Is mount Zion, [on] the sides of the north, The city of the great King.
texts.psa.48.3: God hath made himself known in her palaces for a refuge.
texts.psa.48.4: For, lo, the kings assembled themselves, They passed by together.
texts.psa.48.5: They saw it, then were they amazed; They were dismayed, they hasted away.
texts.psa.48.6: Trembling took hold of them there, Pain, as of a woman in travail.
texts.psa.48.7: With the east wind Thou breakest the ships of Tarshish.
texts.psa.48.8: As we have heard, so have we seen In the city of Jehovah of hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish it for ever. Selah
texts.psa.48.9: We have thought on thy lovingkindness, O God, In the midst of thy temple.
texts.psa.48.10: As is thy name, O God, So is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: Thy right hand is full of righteousness.
texts.psa.48.11: Let mount Zion be glad, Let the daughters of Judah rejoice, Because of thy judgments.
texts.psa.48.12: Walk about Zion, and go round about her; Number the towers thereof;
texts.psa.48.13: Mark ye well her bulwarks; Consider her palaces: That ye may tell it to the generation following.
texts.psa.48.14: For this God is our God for ever and ever: He will be our guide [even] unto death.
texts.psa.49.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Hear this, all ye peoples; Give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world,
texts.psa.49.2: Both low and high, Rich and poor together.
texts.psa.49.3: My mouth shall speak wisdom; And the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.
texts.psa.49.4: I will incline mine ear to a parable: I will open my dark saying upon the harp.
texts.psa.49.5: Wherefore should I fear in the days of evil, When iniquity at my heels compasseth me about?
texts.psa.49.6: They that trust in their wealth, And boast themselves in the multitude of their riches;
texts.psa.49.7: None [of them] can by any means redeem his brother, Nor give to God a ransom for him;
texts.psa.49.8: (For the redemption of their life is costly, And it faileth for ever;)
texts.psa.49.9: That he should still live alway, That he should not see corruption.
texts.psa.49.10: For he shall see it. Wise men die; The fool and the brutish alike perish, And leave their wealth to others.
texts.psa.49.11: Their inward thought is, [that] their houses [shall continue] for ever, [And] their dwelling-places to all generations; They call their lands after their own names.
texts.psa.49.12: But man [being] in honor abideth not: He is like the beasts that perish.
texts.psa.49.13: This their way is their folly: Yet after them men approve their sayings. Selah
texts.psa.49.14: They are appointed as a flock for Sheol; Death shall be their shepherd; And the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning; And their beauty shall be for Sheol to consume, That there be no habitation for it.
texts.psa.49.15: But God will redeem my soul from the power of Sheol; For he will receive me. Selah
texts.psa.49.16: Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, When the glory of his house is increased.
texts.psa.49.17: For when he dieth he shall carry nothing away; His glory shall not descend after him.
texts.psa.49.18: Though while he lived he blessed his soul (And men praise thee, when thou doest well to thyself,)
texts.psa.49.19: He shall go to the generation of his fathers; They shall never see the light.
texts.psa.49.20: Man that is in honor, and understandeth not, Is like the beasts that perish.
texts.psa.50.1: A Psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God, Jehovah, hath spoken, And called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.
texts.psa.50.2: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined forth.
texts.psa.50.3: Our God cometh, and doth not keep silence: A fire devoureth before him, And it is very tempestuous round about him.
texts.psa.50.4: He calleth to the heavens above, And to the earth, that he may judge his people:
texts.psa.50.5: Gather my saints together unto me, Those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.
texts.psa.50.6: And the heavens shall declare his righteousness; For God is judge himself. Selah
texts.psa.50.7: Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify unto thee: I am God, [even] thy God.
texts.psa.50.8: I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices; And thy burnt-offerings are continually before me.
texts.psa.50.9: I will take no bullock out of thy house, Nor he-goats out of thy folds.
texts.psa.50.10: For every beast of the forest is mine, And the cattle upon a thousand hills.
texts.psa.50.11: I know all the birds of the mountains; And the wild beasts of the field are mine.
texts.psa.50.12: If I were hungry, I would not tell thee; For the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.
texts.psa.50.13: Will I eat the flesh of bulls, Or drink the blood of goats?
texts.psa.50.14: Offer unto God the sacrifice of thanksgiving; And pay thy vows unto the Most High:
texts.psa.50.15: And call upon me in the day of trouble; I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.
texts.psa.50.16: But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, And that thou hast taken my covenant in thy mouth,
texts.psa.50.17: Seeing thou hatest instruction, And castest my words behind thee?
texts.psa.50.18: When thou sawest a thief, thou consentedst with him, And hast been partaker with adulterers.
texts.psa.50.19: Thou givest thy mouth to evil, And thy tongue frameth deceit.
texts.psa.50.20: Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; Thou slanderest thine own mother's son.
texts.psa.50.21: These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such a one as thyself: [But] I will reprove thee, and set [them] in order before thine eyes.
texts.psa.50.22: Now consider this, ye that forget God, Lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver:
texts.psa.50.23: Whoso offereth the sacrifice of thanksgiving glorifieth me; And to him that ordereth his way [aright] Will I show the salvation of God.
texts.psa.51.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David; when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba. Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: According to the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
texts.psa.51.2: Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, And cleanse me from my sin.
texts.psa.51.3: For I know my transgressions; And my sin is ever before me.
texts.psa.51.4: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, And done that which is evil in thy sight; That thou mayest be justified when thou speakest, And be clear when thou judgest.
texts.psa.51.5: Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity; And in sin did my mother conceive me.
texts.psa.51.6: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts; And in the hidden part thou wilt make me to know wisdom.
texts.psa.51.7: Purify me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
texts.psa.51.8: Make me to hear joy and gladness, That the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
texts.psa.51.9: Hide thy face from my sins, And blot out all mine iniquities.
texts.psa.51.10: Create in me a clean heart, O God; And renew a right spirit within me.
texts.psa.51.11: Cast me not away from thy presence; And take not thy holy Spirit from me.
texts.psa.51.12: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; And uphold me with a willing spirit.
texts.psa.51.13: Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; And sinners shall be converted unto thee.
texts.psa.51.14: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation; [And] my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.
texts.psa.51.15: O Lord, open thou my lips; And my mouth shall show forth thy praise.
texts.psa.51.16: For thou delightest not in sacrifice; else would I give it: Thou hast no pleasure in burnt-offering.
texts.psa.51.17: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: A broken and contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
texts.psa.51.18: Do good in thy good pleasure unto Zion: Build thou the walls of Jerusalem.
texts.psa.51.19: Then will thou delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, In burnt-offering and in whole burnt-offering: Then will they offer bullocks upon thine altar.
texts.psa.52.1: For the Chief Musician. Maschil of David; when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said unto him, David is come to the house of Abimelech. Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? The lovingkindness of God [endureth] continually.
texts.psa.52.2: Thy tongue deviseth very wickedness, Like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.
texts.psa.52.3: Thou lovest evil more than good, And lying rather than to speak righteousness. Selah
texts.psa.52.4: Thou lovest all devouring words, thou deceitful tongue.
texts.psa.52.5: God will likewise destroy thee for ever; He will take thee up, and pluck thee out of thy tent, And root thee out of the land of the living. Selah
texts.psa.52.6: The righteous also shall see [it], and fear, And shall laugh at him, [saying],
texts.psa.52.7: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength, But trusted in the abundance of his riches, And strengthened himself in his wickedness.
texts.psa.52.8: But as for me, I am like a green olive-tree in the house of God: I trust in the lovingkindness of God for ever and ever.
texts.psa.52.9: I will give thee thanks for ever, because thou hast done it; And I will hope in thy name, for it is good, in the presence of thy saints.
texts.psa.53.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Mahalath. Maschil of David. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity; There is none that doeth good.
texts.psa.53.2: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, To see if there were any that did understand, That did seek after God.
texts.psa.53.3: Every one of them is gone back; they are together become filthy; There is none that doeth good, no, not one.
texts.psa.53.4: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge, Who eat up my people [as] they eat bread, And call not upon God?
texts.psa.53.5: There were they in great fear, where no fear was; For God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: Thou hast put them to shame, because of God hath rejected them.
texts.psa.53.6: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Then shall Jacob rejoice, [and] Israel shall be glad.
texts.psa.54.1: For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments. Maschil of David; when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, Doth not David hide himself with us? Save me, O God, by thy name, And judge me in thy might.
texts.psa.54.2: Hear my prayer, O God; Give ear to the words of my mouth.
texts.psa.54.3: For strangers are risen up against me, And violent men have sought after my soul: They have not set God before them. Selah
texts.psa.54.4: Behold, God is my helper: The Lord is of them that uphold my soul.
texts.psa.54.5: He will requite the evil unto mine enemies: Destroy thou them in thy truth.
texts.psa.54.6: With a freewill-offering will I sacrifice unto thee: I will give thanks unto thy name, O Jehovah, for it is good.
texts.psa.54.7: For he hath delivered me out of all trouble; And mine eye hath seen [my desire] upon mine enemies.
texts.psa.55.1: For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments. Maschil of David. Give ear to my prayer, O God; And hide not thyself from my supplication.
texts.psa.55.2: Attend unto me, and answer me: I am restless in my complaint, and moan,
texts.psa.55.3: Because of the voice of the enemy, Because of the oppression of the wicked; For they cast iniquity upon me, And in anger they persecute me.
texts.psa.55.4: My heart is sore pained within me: And the terrors of death are fallen upon me.
texts.psa.55.5: Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me, And horror hath overwhelmed me.
texts.psa.55.6: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then would I fly away, and be at rest.
texts.psa.55.7: Lo, then would I wander far off, I would lodge in the wilderness. Selah
texts.psa.55.8: I would haste me to a shelter From the stormy wind and tempest.
texts.psa.55.9: Destroy, O Lord, [and] divide their tongue; For I have seen violence and strife in the city.
texts.psa.55.10: Day and night they go about it upon the walls thereof: Iniquity also and mischief are in the midst of it.
texts.psa.55.11: Wickedness is in the midst thereof: Oppression and guile depart not from its streets.
texts.psa.55.12: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; Then I could have borne it: Neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; Then I would have hid myself from him:
texts.psa.55.13: But it was thou, a man mine equal, My companion, and my familiar friend.
texts.psa.55.14: We took sweet counsel together; We walked in the house of God with the throng.
texts.psa.55.15: Let death come suddenly upon them, Let them go down alive into Sheol; For wickedness is in their dwelling, in the midst of them.
texts.psa.55.16: As for me, I will call upon God; And Jehovah will save me.
texts.psa.55.17: Evening, and morning, and at noonday, will I complain, and moan; And he will hear my voice.
texts.psa.55.18: He hath redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me; For they were many [that strove] with me.
texts.psa.55.19: God will hear, and answer them, Even he that abideth of old, Selah [The men] who have no changes, And who fear not God.
texts.psa.55.20: He hath put forth his hands against such as were at peace with him: He hath profaned his covenant.
texts.psa.55.21: His mouth was smooth as butter, But his heart was war: His words were softer than oil, Yet were they drawn swords.
texts.psa.55.22: Cast thy burden upon Jehovah, and he will sustain thee: He will never suffer the righteous to be moved.
texts.psa.55.23: But thou, O God, wilt bring them down into the pit of destruction: Bloodthirsty and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; But I will trust in thee.
texts.psa.56.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Jonath elem rehokim. [A Psalm] of David. Michtam: when the Philistines took him in Gath. Be merciful unto me, O God; for man would swallow me up: All the day long he fighting oppresseth me.
texts.psa.56.2: Mine enemies would swallow me up all the day long; For they are many that fight proudly against me.
texts.psa.56.3: What time I am afraid, I will put my trust in thee.
texts.psa.56.4: In God (I will praise his word), In God have I put my trust, I will not be afraid; What can flesh do unto me?
texts.psa.56.5: All the day long they wrest my words: All their thoughts are against me for evil.
texts.psa.56.6: They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, They mark my steps, Even as they have waited for my soul.
texts.psa.56.7: Shall they escape by iniquity? In anger cast down the peoples, O God.
texts.psa.56.8: Thou numberest my wanderings: Put thou my tears into thy bottle; Are they not in thy book?
texts.psa.56.9: Then shall mine enemies turn back in the day that I call: This I know, that God is for me.
texts.psa.56.10: In God (I will praise [his] word), In Jehovah (I will praise [his] word),
texts.psa.56.11: In God have I put my trust, I will not be afraid; What can man do unto me?
texts.psa.56.12: Thy vows are upon me, O God: I will render thank-offerings unto thee.
texts.psa.56.13: For thou hast delivered my soul from death: [Hast thou] not [delivered] my feet from falling, That I may walk before God In the light of the living?
texts.psa.57.1: For the Chief Musician; [set to] Al-tash-heth. [A Psalm] of David. Michtam; when he fled from Saul, in the cave. Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me; For my soul taketh refuge in thee: Yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I take refuge, Until [these] calamities be overpast.
texts.psa.57.2: I will cry unto God Most High, Unto God that performeth [all things] for me.
texts.psa.57.3: He will send from heaven, and save me, [When] he that would swallow me up reproacheth; Selah God will send forth his lovingkindness and his truth.
texts.psa.57.4: My soul is among lions; I lie among them that are set on fire, Even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, And their tongue a sharp sword.
texts.psa.57.5: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; [Let] thy glory [be] above all the earth.
texts.psa.57.6: They have prepared a net for my steps; My soul is bowed down: They have digged a pit before me; They are fallen into the midst thereof themselves. Selah
texts.psa.57.7: My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing, yea, I will sing praises.
texts.psa.57.8: Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake right early.
texts.psa.57.9: I will give thanks unto thee, O Lord, among the peoples: I will sing praises unto thee among the nations.
texts.psa.57.10: For thy lovingkindness is great unto the heavens, And thy truth unto the skies.
texts.psa.57.11: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; [Let] thy glory [be] above all the earth.
texts.psa.58.1: For the Chief Musician; [set to] Al-tashheth. [A Psalm] of David. Michtam. Do ye indeed in silence speak righteousness? Do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?
texts.psa.58.2: Nay, in heart ye work wickedness; Ye weigh out the violence of your hands in the earth.
texts.psa.58.3: The wicked are estranged from the womb: They go astray as soon as they are born, speaking lies.
texts.psa.58.4: Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: [They are] like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear,
texts.psa.58.5: Which hearkeneth not to the voice of charmers, Charming never so wisely.
texts.psa.58.6: Break their teeth, O God, in their mouth: Break out the great teeth of the young lions, O Jehovah.
texts.psa.58.7: Let them melt away as water that runneth apace: When he aimeth his arrows, let them be as though they were cut off.
texts.psa.58.8: [Let them be] as a snail which melteth and passeth away, [Like] the untimely birth of a woman, that hath not seen the sun.
texts.psa.58.9: Before your pots can feel the thorns, He will take them away with a whirlwind, the green and the burning alike.
texts.psa.58.10: The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance: He shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked;
texts.psa.58.11: So that men shall say, Verily there is a reward for the righteous: Verily there is a God that judgeth in the earth.
texts.psa.59.1: For the Chief Musician; [set to] Al-tashheth. [A Psalm] of David. Michtam; when Saul sent, and they watched the house to kill him. Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: Set me on high from them that rise up against me.
texts.psa.59.2: Deliver me from the workers of iniquity, And save me from the bloodthirsty men.
texts.psa.59.3: For, lo, they lie in wait for my soul; The mighty gather themselves together against me: Not for my transgression, nor for my sin, O Jehovah.
texts.psa.59.4: They run and prepare themselves without [my] fault: Awake thou to help me, and behold.
texts.psa.59.5: Even thou, O Jehovah God of hosts, the God of Israel, Arise to visit all the nations: Be not merciful to any wicked transgressors. Selah
texts.psa.59.6: They return at evening, they howl like a dog, And go round about the city.
texts.psa.59.7: Behold, they belch out with their mouth; Swords are in their lips: For who, [say they], doth hear?
texts.psa.59.8: But thou, O Jehovah, wilt laugh at them; Thou wilt have all the nations in derision.
texts.psa.59.9: [Because of] his strength I will give heed unto thee; For God is my high tower.
texts.psa.59.10: My God with his lovingkindness will meet me: God will let me see [my desire] upon mine enemies.
texts.psa.59.11: Slay them not, lest my people forget: Scatter them by thy power, and bring them down, O Lord our shield.
texts.psa.59.12: [For] the sin of their mouth, [and] the words of their lips, Let them even be taken in their pride, And for cursing and lying which they speak.
texts.psa.59.13: Consume them in wrath, consume them, so that they shall be no more: And let them know that God ruleth in Jacob, Unto the ends of the earth. Selah
texts.psa.59.14: And at evening let them return, let them howl like a dog, And go round about the city.
texts.psa.59.15: They shall wander up and down for food, And tarry all night if they be not satisfied.
texts.psa.59.16: But I will sing of thy strength; Yea, I will sing aloud of thy lovingkindness in the morning: For thou hast been my high tower, And a refuge in the day of my distress.
texts.psa.59.17: Unto thee, O my strength, will I sing praises: For God is my high tower, the God of my mercy.
texts.psa.60.1: For the Chief Musician; [set to] Shushan Eduth. Michtam of David, to teach; and when he strove with Aram-naharaim and with Aram-zobah, and Joab returned, and smote of Edom in the Valley of Salt twelve thousand. O God thou hast cast us off, thou hast broken us down; Thou hast been angry; oh restore us again.
texts.psa.60.2: Thou hast made the land to tremble; thou hast rent it: Heal the breaches thereof; for it shaketh.
texts.psa.60.3: Thou hast showed thy people hard things: Thou hast made us to drink the wine of staggering.
texts.psa.60.4: Thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee, That it may be displayed because of the truth. Selah
texts.psa.60.5: That thy beloved may be delivered, Save with thy right hand, and answer us.
texts.psa.60.6: God hath spoken in his holiness: I will exult; I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth.
texts.psa.60.7: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the defence of my head; Judah is my sceptre.
texts.psa.60.8: Moab is my washpot; Upon Edom will I cast my shoe: Philistia, shout thou because of me.
texts.psa.60.9: Who will bring me into the strong city? Who hath led me unto Edom?
texts.psa.60.10: Hast not thou, O God, cast us off? And thou goest not forth, O God, with our hosts.
texts.psa.60.11: Give us help against the adversary; For vain is the help of man.
texts.psa.60.12: Through God we shall do valiantly; For he it is that will tread down our adversaries.
texts.psa.61.1: For the Chief Musician; on a stringed instrument. [A Psalm] of David. Hear my cry, O God; Attend unto my prayer.
texts.psa.61.2: From the end of the earth will I call unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
texts.psa.61.3: For thou hast been a refuge for me, A strong tower from the enemy.
texts.psa.61.4: I will dwell in thy tabernacle for ever: I will take refuge in the covert of thy wings. Selah
texts.psa.61.5: For thou, O God, hast heard my vows: Thou hast given [me] the heritage of those that fear thy name.
texts.psa.61.6: Thou wilt prolong the king's life; His years shall be as many generations.
texts.psa.61.7: He shall abide before God for ever: Oh prepare lovingkindness and truth, that they may preserve him.
texts.psa.61.8: So will I sing praise unto thy name for ever, That I may daily perform my vows.
texts.psa.62.1: For the Chief Musician; after the manner of Jeduthan. A Psalm of David. My soul waiteth in silence for God only: From him [cometh] my salvation.
texts.psa.62.2: He only is my rock and my salvation: [He is] my high tower; I shall not be greatly moved.
texts.psa.62.3: How long will ye set upon a man, That ye may slay [him], all of you, Like a leaning wall, like a tottering fence?
texts.psa.62.4: They only consult to thrust him down from his dignity; They delight in lies; They bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah
texts.psa.62.5: My soul, wait thou in silence for God only; For my expectation is from him.
texts.psa.62.6: He only is my rock and my salvation: [He is] my high tower; I shall not be moved.
texts.psa.62.7: With God is my salvation and my glory: The rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
texts.psa.62.8: Trust in him at all times, ye people; Pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah
texts.psa.62.9: Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: In the balances they will go up; They are together lighter than vanity.
texts.psa.62.10: Trust not in oppression, And become not vain in robbery: If riches increase, set not your heart [thereon].
texts.psa.62.11: God hath spoken once, Twice have I heard this, That power belongeth unto God.
texts.psa.62.12: Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth lovingkindness; For thou renderest to every man according to his work.
texts.psa.63.1: A Psalm of David when he was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, thou art my God; earnestly will I seek thee: My soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee, In a dry and weary land, where no water is.
texts.psa.63.2: So have I looked upon thee in the sanctuary, To see thy power and thy glory.
texts.psa.63.3: Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, My lips shall praise thee.
texts.psa.63.4: So will I bless thee while I live: I will lift up my hands in thy name.
texts.psa.63.5: My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness; And my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips;
texts.psa.63.6: When I remember thee upon my bed, [And] meditate on thee in the night-watches.
texts.psa.63.7: For thou hast been my help, And in the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.
texts.psa.63.8: My soul followeth hard after thee: Thy right hand upholdeth me.
texts.psa.63.9: But those that seek my soul, to destroy it, Shall go into the lower parts of the earth.
texts.psa.63.10: They shall be given over to the power of the sword: They shall be a portion for foxes.
texts.psa.63.11: But the king shall rejoice in God: Every one that sweareth by him shall glory; For the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped.
texts.psa.64.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint: Preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
texts.psa.64.2: Hide me from the secret counsel of evil-doers, From the tumult of the workers of iniquity;
texts.psa.64.3: Who have whet their tongue like a sword, And have aimed their arrows, even bitter words,
texts.psa.64.4: That they may shoot in secret places at the perfect: Suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not.
texts.psa.64.5: They encourage themselves in an evil purpose; They commune of laying snares privily; They say, Who will see them?
texts.psa.64.6: They search out iniquities; We have accomplished, [say they], a diligent search: And the inward thought and the heart of every one is deep.
texts.psa.64.7: But God will shoot at them; With an arrow suddenly shall they be wounded.
texts.psa.64.8: So they shall be made to stumble, their own tongue being against them: All that see them shall wag the head.
texts.psa.64.9: And all men shall fear; And they shall declare the work of God, And shall wisely consider of his doing.
texts.psa.64.10: The righteous shall be glad in Jehovah, and shall take refuge in him; And all the upright in heart shall glory.
texts.psa.65.1: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm. A song of David. Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Zion; And unto thee shall the vow be performed.
texts.psa.65.2: O thou that hearest prayer, Unto thee shall all flesh come.
texts.psa.65.3: Iniquities prevail against me: As for our transgressions, thou wilt forgive them.
texts.psa.65.4: Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach [unto thee], That he may dwell in thy courts: We shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, Thy holy temple.
texts.psa.65.5: By terrible things thou wilt answer us in righteousness, Oh God of our salvation, Thou that art the confidence of all the ends of the earth, And of them that are afar off upon the sea:
texts.psa.65.6: Who by his strength setteth fast the mountains, Being girded about with might;
texts.psa.65.7: Who stilleth the roaring of the seas, The roaring of their waves, And the tumult of the peoples.
texts.psa.65.8: They also that dwell in the uttermost parts are afraid at thy tokens: Thou makest the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice.
texts.psa.65.9: Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it, Thou greatly enrichest it; The river of God is full of water: Thou providest them grain, when thou hast so prepared the earth.
texts.psa.65.10: Thou waterest its furrows abundantly; Thou settlest the ridges thereof: Thou makest it soft with showers; Thou blessest the springing thereof.
texts.psa.65.11: Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; And thy paths drop fatness.
texts.psa.65.12: They drop upon the pastures of the wilderness; And the hills are girded with joy.
texts.psa.65.13: The pastures are clothed with flocks; The valleys also are covered over with grain; They shout for joy, they also sing.
texts.psa.66.1: For the Chief Musician. A song, a Psalm. Make a joyful noise unto God, all the earth:
texts.psa.66.2: Sing forth the glory of his name: Make his praise glorious.
texts.psa.66.3: Say unto God, How terrible are thy works! Through the greatness of thy power shall thine enemies submit themselves unto thee.
texts.psa.66.4: All the earth shall worship thee, And shall sing unto thee; They shall sing to thy name. Selah
texts.psa.66.5: Come, and see the works of God; [He is] terrible in his doing toward the children of men.
texts.psa.66.6: He turned the sea into dry land; They went through the river on foot: There did we rejoice in him.
texts.psa.66.7: He ruleth by his might for ever; His eyes observe the nations: Let not the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah
texts.psa.66.8: Oh bless our God, ye peoples, And make the voice of his praise to be heard;
texts.psa.66.9: Who holdeth our soul in life, And suffereth not our feet to be moved.
texts.psa.66.10: For thou, O God, hast proved us: Thou hast tried us, as silver is tried.
texts.psa.66.11: Thou broughtest us into the net; Thou layedst a sore burden upon our loins.
texts.psa.66.12: Thou didst cause men to ride over our heads; We went through fire and through water; But thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place.
texts.psa.66.13: I will come into thy house with burnt-offerings; I will pay thee my vows,
texts.psa.66.14: Which my lips uttered, And my mouth spake, when I was in distress.
texts.psa.66.15: I will offer unto thee burnt-offerings of fatlings, With the incense of rams; I will offer bullocks with goats. Selah
texts.psa.66.16: Come, and hear, all ye that fear God, And I will declare what he hath done for my soul.
texts.psa.66.17: I cried unto him with my mouth, And he was extolled with my tongue.
texts.psa.66.18: If I regard iniquity in my heart, The Lord will not hear:
texts.psa.66.19: But verily God hath heard; He hath attended to the voice of my prayer.
texts.psa.66.20: Blessed be God, Who hath not turned away my prayer, Nor his lovingkindness from me.
texts.psa.67.1: For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments. A Psalm, a song. God be merciful unto us, and bless us, [And] cause his face to shine upon us; Selah
texts.psa.67.2: That thy way may be known upon earth, Thy salvation among all nations.
texts.psa.67.3: Let the peoples praise thee, O God; Let all the peoples praise thee.
texts.psa.67.4: Oh let the nations be glad and sing for joy; For thou wilt judge the peoples with equity, And govern the nations upon earth. Selah
texts.psa.67.5: Let the peoples praise thee, O God; Let all the peoples praise thee.
texts.psa.67.6: The earth hath yielded its increase: God, even our own God, will bless us.
texts.psa.67.7: God will bless us; And all the ends of the earth shall fear him.
texts.psa.68.1: For the Chief Musician; A Psalm of David, a song. Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered; Let them also that hate him flee before him.
texts.psa.68.2: As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: As wax melteth before the fire, So let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
texts.psa.68.3: But let the righteous be glad; let them exult before God: Yea, let them rejoice with gladness.
texts.psa.68.4: Sing unto God, sing praises to his name: Cast up a highway for him that rideth through the deserts; His name is Jehovah; and exult ye before him.
texts.psa.68.5: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, Is God in his holy habitation.
texts.psa.68.6: God setteth the solitary in families: He bringeth out the prisoners into prosperity; But the rebellious dwell in a parched land.
texts.psa.68.7: O God, when thou wentest forth before thy people, When thou didst march through the wilderness; Selah
texts.psa.68.8: The earth trembled, The heavens also dropped [rain] at the presence of God: Yon Sinai [trembled] at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
texts.psa.68.9: Thou, O God, didst send a plentiful rain, Thou didst confirm thine inheritance, when it was weary.
texts.psa.68.10: Thy congregation dwelt therein: Thou, O God, didst prepare of thy goodness for the poor.
texts.psa.68.11: The Lord giveth the word: The women that publish the tidings are a great host.
texts.psa.68.12: Kings of armies flee, they flee; And she that tarrieth at home divideth the spoil.
texts.psa.68.13: When ye lie among the sheepfolds, [It is as] the wings of a dove covered with silver, And her pinions with yellow gold.
texts.psa.68.14: When the Almighty scattered kings therein, [It was as when] it snoweth in Zalmon.
texts.psa.68.15: A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; A high mountain is the mountain of Bashan.
texts.psa.68.16: Why look ye askance, ye high mountains, At the mountain which God hath desired for his abode? Yea, Jehovah will dwell [in it] for ever.
texts.psa.68.17: The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands upon thousands; The Lord is among them, [as in] Sinai, in the sanctuary.
texts.psa.68.18: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led away captives; Thou hast received gifts among men, Yea, [among] the rebellious also, that Jehovah God might dwell [with them].
texts.psa.68.19: Blessed be the Lord, who daily beareth our burden, Even the God who is our salvation. Selah
texts.psa.68.20: God is unto us a God of deliverances; And unto Jehovah the Lord belongeth escape from death.
texts.psa.68.21: But God will smite through the head of his enemies, The hairy scalp of such a one as goeth on still in his guiltiness.
texts.psa.68.22: The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring [them] again from the depths of the sea;
texts.psa.68.23: That thou mayest crush [them], [dipping] thy foot in blood, That the tongue of thy dogs may have its portion from [thine] enemies.
texts.psa.68.24: They have seen thy goings, O God, Even the goings of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.
texts.psa.68.25: The singers went before, the minstrels followed after, In the midst of the damsels playing with timbrels.
texts.psa.68.26: Bless ye God in the congregations, Even the Lord, [ye that are] of the fountain of Israel.
texts.psa.68.27: There is little Benjamin their ruler, The princes of Judah [and] their council, The princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
texts.psa.68.28: Thy God hath commanded thy strength: Strengthen, O God, that which thou hast wrought for us.
texts.psa.68.29: Because of thy temple at Jerusalem Kings shall bring presents unto thee.
texts.psa.68.30: Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds, The multitude of the bulls, with the calves of the peoples, Trampling under foot the pieces of silver: He hath scattered the peoples that delight in war.
texts.psa.68.31: Princes shall come out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall haste to stretch out her hands unto God.
texts.psa.68.32: Sing unto God, ye kingdoms of the earth; Oh sing praises unto the Lord; Selah
texts.psa.68.33: To him that rideth upon the heaven of heavens, which are of old; Lo, he uttereth his voice, a mighty voice.
texts.psa.68.34: Ascribe ye strength unto God: His excellency is over Israel, And his strength is in the skies.
texts.psa.68.35: O God, [thou art] terrible out of thy holy places: The God of Israel, he giveth strength and power unto [his] people. Blessed be God.
texts.psa.69.1: For the Chief Musician; set to Shoshanim. [A Psalm] of David. Save me, O God; For the waters are come in unto my soul.
texts.psa.69.2: I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
texts.psa.69.3: I am weary with my crying; my throat is dried: Mine eyes fail while I wait for my God.
texts.psa.69.4: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head: They that would cut me off, being mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty: That which I took not away I have to restore.
texts.psa.69.5: O God, thou knowest my foolishness; And my sins are not hid from thee.
texts.psa.69.6: Let not them that wait for thee be put to shame through me, O Lord Jehovah of hosts: Let not those that seek thee be brought to dishonor through me, O God of Israel.
texts.psa.69.7: Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; Shame hath covered my face.
texts.psa.69.8: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, And an alien unto my mother's children.
texts.psa.69.9: For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up; And the reproaches of them that reproach thee are fallen upon me.
texts.psa.69.10: When I wept, [and chastened] my soul with fasting, That was to my reproach.
texts.psa.69.11: When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword unto them.
texts.psa.69.12: They that sit in the gate talk of me; And [I am] the song of the drunkards.
texts.psa.69.13: But as for me, my prayer is unto thee, O Jehovah, in an acceptable time: O God, in the abundance of thy lovingkindness, Answer me in the truth of thy salvation.
texts.psa.69.14: Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink: Let me be delivered from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.
texts.psa.69.15: Let not the waterflood overwhelm me, Neither let the deep shallow me up; And let not the pit shut its mouth upon me.
texts.psa.69.16: Answer me, O Jehovah; for thy lovingkindness is good: According to the multitude of thy tender mercies turn thou unto me.
texts.psa.69.17: And hide not thy face from thy servant; For I am in distress; answer me speedily.
texts.psa.69.18: Draw nigh unto my soul, and redeem it: Ransom me because of mine enemies.
texts.psa.69.19: Thou knowest my reproach, and my shame, and my dishonor: Mine adversaries are all before thee.
texts.psa.69.20: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: And I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; And for comforters, but I found none.
texts.psa.69.21: They gave me also gall for my food; And in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
texts.psa.69.22: Let their table before them become a snare; And when they are in peace, [let it become] a trap.
texts.psa.69.23: Let their eyes be darkened, so that they cannot see; And make their loins continually to shake.
texts.psa.69.24: Pour out thine indignation upon them, And let the fierceness of thine anger overtake them.
texts.psa.69.25: Let their habitation be desolate; Let none dwell in their tents.
texts.psa.69.26: For they persecute him whom thou hast smitten; And they tell of the sorrow of those whom thou hast wounded.
texts.psa.69.27: Add iniquity unto their iniquity; And let them not come into thy righteousness.
texts.psa.69.28: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, And not be written with the righteous.
texts.psa.69.29: But I am poor and sorrowful: Let thy salvation, O God, set me up on high.
texts.psa.69.30: I will praise the name of God with a song, And will magnify him with thanksgiving.
texts.psa.69.31: And it will please Jehovah better than an ox, [Or] a bullock that hath horns and hoofs.
texts.psa.69.32: The meek have seen it, and are glad: Ye that seek after God, let your heart live.
texts.psa.69.33: For Jehovah heareth the needy, And despiseth not his prisoners.
texts.psa.69.34: Let heaven and earth praise him, The seas, and everything that moveth therein.
texts.psa.69.35: For God will save Zion, and build the cities of Judah; And they shall abide there, and have it in possession.
texts.psa.69.36: The seed also of his servants shall inherit it; And they that love his name shall dwell therein.
texts.psa.70.1: For the Chief Musician. [A Psalm] of David; to bring to remembrance. [Make haste], O God, to deliver me; Make haste to help me, O Jehovah.
texts.psa.70.2: Let them be put to shame and confounded That seek after my soul: Let them be turned backward and brought to dishonor That delight in my hurt.
texts.psa.70.3: Let them be turned back by reason of their shame That say, Aha, aha.
texts.psa.70.4: Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; And let such as love thy salvation say continually, Let God be magnified.
texts.psa.70.5: But I am poor and needy; Make haste unto me, O God: Thou art my help and my deliverer; O Jehovah, make no tarrying.
texts.psa.71.1: In thee, O Jehovah, do I take refuge: Let me never be put to shame.
texts.psa.71.2: Deliver me in thy righteousness, and rescue me: Bow down thine ear unto me, and save me.
texts.psa.71.3: Be thou to me a rock of habitation, whereunto I may continually resort: Thou hast given commandment to save me; For thou art my rock and my fortress.
texts.psa.71.4: Rescue me, O my God, out of the hand of the wicked, Out of the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.
texts.psa.71.5: For thou art my hope, O Lord Jehovah: [Thou art] my trust from my youth.
texts.psa.71.6: By thee have I been holden up from the womb; Thou art he that took me out of my mother's bowels: My praise shall be continually of thee.
texts.psa.71.7: I am as a wonder unto many; But thou art my strong refuge.
texts.psa.71.8: My mouth shall be filled with thy praise, And with thy honor all the day.
texts.psa.71.9: Cast me not off in the time of old age; Forsake me not when my strength faileth.
texts.psa.71.10: For mine enemies speak concerning me; And they that watch for my soul take counsel together,
texts.psa.71.11: Saying, God hath forsaken him: Pursue and take him; for there is none to deliver.
texts.psa.71.12: O God, be not far from me; O my God, make haste to help me.
texts.psa.71.13: Let them be put to shame [and] consumed that are adversaries to my soul; Let them be covered with reproach and dishonor that seek my hurt.
texts.psa.71.14: But I will hope continually, And will praise thee yet more and more.
texts.psa.71.15: My mouth shall tell of thy righteousness, [And] of thy salvation all the day; For I know not the numbers [thereof].
texts.psa.71.16: I will come with the mighty acts of the Lord Jehovah: I will make mention of thy righteousness, even of thine only.
texts.psa.71.17: O God, thou hast taught me from my youth; And hitherto have I declared thy wondrous works.
texts.psa.71.18: Yea, even when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not, Until I have declared thy strength unto [the next] generation, Thy might to every one that is to come.
texts.psa.71.19: Thy righteousness also, O God, is very high; Thou who hast done great things, O God, who is like unto thee?
texts.psa.71.20: Thou, who hast showed us many and sore troubles, Wilt quicken us again, And wilt bring us up again from the depths of the earth.
texts.psa.71.21: Increase thou my greatness, And turn again and comfort me.
texts.psa.71.22: I will also praise thee with the psaltery, [Even] thy truth, O my God: Unto thee will I sing praises with the harp, O thou Holy One of Israel.
texts.psa.71.23: My lips shall shout for joy when I sing praises unto thee; And my soul, which thou hast redeemed.
texts.psa.71.24: My tongue also shall talk of thy righteousness all the day long; For they are put to shame, for they are confounded, that seek my hurt.
texts.psa.72.1: [A Psalm] of Solomon. Give the king thy judgments, O God, And thy righteousness unto the king's son.
texts.psa.72.2: He will judge thy people with righteousness, And thy poor with justice.
texts.psa.72.3: The mountains shall bring peace to the people, And the hills, in righteousness.
texts.psa.72.4: He will judge the poor of the people, He will save the children of the needy, And will break in pieces the oppressor.
texts.psa.72.5: They shall fear thee while the sun endureth, And so long as the moon, throughout all generations.
texts.psa.72.6: He will come down like rain upon the mown grass, As showers that water the earth.
texts.psa.72.7: In his days shall the righteous flourish, And abundance of peace, till the moon be no more.
texts.psa.72.8: He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, And from the River unto the ends of the earth.
texts.psa.72.9: They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; And his enemies shall lick the dust.
texts.psa.72.10: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall render tribute: The kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.
texts.psa.72.11: Yea, all kings shall fall down before him; All nations shall serve him.
texts.psa.72.12: For he will deliver the needy when he crieth, And the poor, that hath no helper.
texts.psa.72.13: He will have pity on the poor and needy, And the souls of the needy he will save.
texts.psa.72.14: He will redeem their soul from oppression and violence; And precious will their blood be in his sight:
texts.psa.72.15: And they shall live; and to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba: And men shall pray for him continually; They shall bless him all the day long.
texts.psa.72.16: There shall be abundance of grain in the earth upon the top of the mountains; The fruit thereof shall shake like Lebanon: And they of the city shall flourish like grass of the earth.
texts.psa.72.17: His name shall endure for ever; His name shall be continued as long as the sun: And men shall be blessed in him; All nations shall call him happy.
texts.psa.72.18: Blessed be Jehovah God, the God of Israel, Who only doeth wondrous things:
texts.psa.72.19: And blessed be his glorious name for ever; And let the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen, and Amen.
texts.psa.72.20: The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended. BOOK III
texts.psa.73.1: A Psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, [Even] to such as are pure in heart.
texts.psa.73.2: But as for me, my feet were almost gone; My steps had well nigh slipped.
texts.psa.73.3: For I was envious at the arrogant, When I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
texts.psa.73.4: For there are no pangs in their death; But their strength is firm.
texts.psa.73.5: They are not in trouble as [other] men; Neither are they plagued like [other] men.
texts.psa.73.6: Therefore pride is as a chain about their neck; Violence covereth them as a garment.
texts.psa.73.7: Their eyes stand out with fatness: They have more than heart could wish.
texts.psa.73.8: They scoff, and in wickedness utter oppression: They speak loftily.
texts.psa.73.9: They have set their mouth in the heavens, And their tongue walketh through the earth.
texts.psa.73.10: Therefore his people return hither: And waters of a full [cup] are drained by them.
texts.psa.73.11: And they say, How doth God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?
texts.psa.73.12: Behold, these are the wicked; And, being alway at ease, they increase in riches.
texts.psa.73.13: Surely in vain have I cleansed my heart, And washed my hands in innocency;
texts.psa.73.14: For all the day long have I been plagued, And chastened every morning.
texts.psa.73.15: If I had said, I will speak thus; Behold, I had dealt treacherously with the generation of thy children.
texts.psa.73.16: When I thought how I might know this, It was too painful for me;
texts.psa.73.17: Until I went into the sanctuary of God, And considered their latter end.
texts.psa.73.18: Surely thou settest them in slippery places: Thou castest them down to destruction.
texts.psa.73.19: How are they become a desolation in a moment! They are utterly consumed with terrors.
texts.psa.73.20: As a dream when one awaketh, So, O Lord, when thou awakest, thou wilt despise their image.
texts.psa.73.21: For my soul was grieved, And I was pricked in my heart:
texts.psa.73.22: So brutish was I, and ignorant; I was [as] a beast before thee.
texts.psa.73.23: Nevertheless I am continually with thee: Thou hast holden my right hand.
texts.psa.73.24: Thou wilt guide me with thy counsel, And afterward receive me to glory.
texts.psa.73.25: Whom have I in heaven [but thee]? And there is none upon earth that I desire besides thee.
texts.psa.73.26: My flesh and my heart faileth; [But] God is the strength of my heart and my portion for ever.
texts.psa.73.27: For, lo, they that are far from thee shall perish: Thou hast destroyed all them that play the harlot, [departing] from thee.
texts.psa.73.28: But it is good for me to draw near unto God: I have made the Lord Jehovah my refuge, That I may tell of all thy works.
texts.psa.74.1: Maschil of Asaph. O God, why hast thou cast [us] off for ever? Why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
texts.psa.74.2: Remember thy congregation, which thou hast gotten of old, Which thou hast redeemed to be the tribe of thine inheritance; [And] mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.
texts.psa.74.3: Lift up thy feet unto the perpetual ruins, All the evil that the enemy hath done in the sanctuary.
texts.psa.74.4: Thine adversaries have roared in the midst of thine assembly; They have set up their ensigns for signs.
texts.psa.74.5: They seemed as men that lifted up Axes upon a thicket of trees.
texts.psa.74.6: And now all the carved work thereof They break down with hatchet and hammers.
texts.psa.74.7: They have set thy sanctuary on fire; They have profaned the dwelling-place of thy name [by casting it] to the ground.
texts.psa.74.8: They said in their heart, Let us make havoc of them altogether: They have burned up all the synagogues of God in the land.
texts.psa.74.9: We see not our signs: There is no more any prophet; Neither is there among us any that knoweth how long.
texts.psa.74.10: How long, O God, shall the adversary reproach? Shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?
texts.psa.74.11: Why drawest thou back thy hand, even thy right hand? [Pluck it] out of thy bosom [and] consume [them].
texts.psa.74.12: Yet God is my King of old, Working salvation in the midst of the earth.
texts.psa.74.13: Thou didst divide the sea by thy strength: Thou brakest the heads of the sea-monsters in the waters.
texts.psa.74.14: Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces; Thou gavest him to be food to the people inhabiting the wilderness.
texts.psa.74.15: Thou didst cleave fountain and flood: Thou driedst up mighty rivers.
texts.psa.74.16: The day is thine, the night also is thine: Thou hast prepared the light and the sun.
texts.psa.74.17: Thou hast set all the borders of the earth: Thou hast made summer and winter.
texts.psa.74.18: Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Jehovah, And that a foolish people hath blasphemed thy name.
texts.psa.74.19: Oh deliver not the soul of thy turtle-dove unto the wild beast: Forget not the life of thy poor for ever.
texts.psa.74.20: Have respect unto the covenant; For the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of violence.
texts.psa.74.21: Oh let not the oppressed return ashamed: Let the poor and needy praise thy name.
texts.psa.74.22: Arise, O God, plead thine own cause: Remember how the foolish man reproacheth thee all the day.
texts.psa.74.23: Forget not the voice of thine adversaries: The tumult of those that rise up against thee ascendeth continually.
texts.psa.75.1: For the Chief Musician; [set to] Al-tash-heth. A Psalm of Asaph; a song. We give thanks unto thee, O God; We give thanks, for thy name is near: Men tell of thy wondrous works.
texts.psa.75.2: When I shall find the set time, I will judge uprightly.
texts.psa.75.3: The earth and all the inhabitants thereof are dissolved: I have set up the pillars of it. Selah
texts.psa.75.4: I said unto the arrogant, Deal not arrogantly; And to the wicked, Lift not up the horn:
texts.psa.75.5: Lift not up your horn on high; Speak not with a stiff neck.
texts.psa.75.6: For neither from the east, nor from the west, Nor yet from the south, [cometh] lifting up.
texts.psa.75.7: But God is the judge: He putteth down one, and lifteth up another.
texts.psa.75.8: For in the hand of Jehovah there is a cup, and the wine foameth; It is full of mixture, and he poureth out of the same: Surely the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall drain them, and drink them.
texts.psa.75.9: But I will declare for ever, I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
texts.psa.75.10: All the horns of the wicked also will I cut off; But the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up.
texts.psa.76.1: For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments. A Psalm of Asaph, a song. In Judah is God known: His name is great in Israel.
texts.psa.76.2: In Salem also is his tabernacle, And his dwelling-place in Zion.
texts.psa.76.3: There he brake the arrows of the bow; The shield, and the sword, and the battle. Selah
texts.psa.76.4: Glorious art thou [and] excellent, From the mountains of prey.
texts.psa.76.5: The stouthearted are made a spoil, They have slept their sleep; And none of the men of might have found their hands.
texts.psa.76.6: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, Both chariot and horse are cast into a deep sleep.
texts.psa.76.7: Thou, even thou, art to be feared; And who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?
texts.psa.76.8: Thou didst cause sentence to be heard from heaven; The earth feared, and was still,
texts.psa.76.9: When God arose to judgment, To save all the meek of the earth. Selah
texts.psa.76.10: Surely the wrath of man shall praise thee: The residue of wrath shalt thou gird upon thee.
texts.psa.76.11: Vow, and pay unto Jehovah your God: Let all that are round about him bring presents unto him that ought to be feared.
texts.psa.76.12: He will cut off the spirit of princes: He is terrible to the kings of the earth.
texts.psa.77.1: For the Chief Musician; after the manner of Jeduthan. A Psalm of Asaph. I will cry unto God with my voice, Even unto God with my voice; and he will give ear unto me.
texts.psa.77.2: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord: My hand was stretched out in the night, and slacked not; My soul refused to be comforted.
texts.psa.77.3: I remember God, and am disquieted: I complain, and my spirit is overwhelmed. Selah
texts.psa.77.4: Thou holdest mine eyes watching: I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
texts.psa.77.5: I have considered the days of old, The years of ancient times.
texts.psa.77.6: I call to remembrance my song in the night: I commune with mine own heart; And my spirit maketh diligent search.
texts.psa.77.7: Will the Lord cast off for ever? And will he be favorable no more?
texts.psa.77.8: Is his lovingkindness clean gone for ever? Doth his promise fail for evermore?
texts.psa.77.9: Hath God forgotten to be gracious? Hath he in anger shut up his tender mercies? Selah
texts.psa.77.10: And I said, This is my infirmity; [But I will remember] the years of the right hand of the Most High.
texts.psa.77.11: I will make mention of the deeds of Jehovah; For I will remember thy wonders of old.
texts.psa.77.12: I will meditate also upon all thy work, And muse on thy doings.
texts.psa.77.13: Thy way, O God, is in the sanctuary: Who is a great god like unto God?
texts.psa.77.14: Thou art the God that doest wonders: Thou hast made known thy strength among the peoples.
texts.psa.77.15: Thou hast with thine arm redeemed thy people, The sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
texts.psa.77.16: The waters saw thee, O God; The waters saw thee, they were afraid: The depths also trembled.
texts.psa.77.17: The clouds poured out water; The skies sent out a sound: Thine arrows also went abroad.
texts.psa.77.18: The voice of thy thunder was in the whirlwind; The lightnings lightened the world: The earth trembled and shook.
texts.psa.77.19: Thy way was in the sea, And thy paths in the great waters, And thy footsteps were not known.
texts.psa.77.20: Thou leddest thy people like a flock, By the hand of Moses and Aaron.
texts.psa.78.1: Maschil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my law: Incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
texts.psa.78.2: I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter dark sayings of old,
texts.psa.78.3: Which we have heard and known, And our fathers have told us.
texts.psa.78.4: We will not hide them from their children, Telling to the generation to come the praises of Jehovah, And his strength, and his wondrous works that he hath done.
texts.psa.78.5: For he established a testimony in Jacob, And appointed a law in Israel, Which he commanded our fathers, That they should make them known to their children;
texts.psa.78.6: That the generation to come might know [them], even the children that should be born; Who should arise and tell [them] to their children,
texts.psa.78.7: That they might set their hope in God, And not forget the works of God, But keep his commandments,
texts.psa.78.8: And might not be as their fathers, A stubborn and rebellious generation, A generation that set not their heart aright, And whose spirit was not stedfast with God.
texts.psa.78.9: The children of Ephraim, being armed and carrying bows, Turned back in the day of battle.
texts.psa.78.10: They kept not the covenant of God, And refused to walk in his law;
texts.psa.78.11: And they forgat his doings, And his wondrous works that he had showed them.
texts.psa.78.12: Marvellous things did he in the sight of their fathers, In the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.
texts.psa.78.13: He clave the sea, and caused them to pass through; And he made the waters to stand as a heap.
texts.psa.78.14: In the day-time also he led them with a cloud, And all the night with a light of fire.
texts.psa.78.15: He clave rocks in the wilderness, And gave them drink abundantly as out of the depths.
texts.psa.78.16: He brought streams also out of the rock, And caused waters to run down like rivers.
texts.psa.78.17: Yet went they on still to sin against him, To rebel against the Most High in the desert.
texts.psa.78.18: And they tempted God in their heart By asking food according to their desire.
texts.psa.78.19: Yea, they spake against God; They said, Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
texts.psa.78.20: Behold, he smote the rock, so that waters gushed out, And streams overflowed; Can he give bread also? Will he provide flesh for his people?
texts.psa.78.21: Therefore Jehovah heard, and was wroth; And a fire was kindled against Jacob, And anger also went up against Israel;
texts.psa.78.22: Because they believed not in God, And trusted not in his salvation.
texts.psa.78.23: Yet he commanded the skies above, And opened the doors of heaven;
texts.psa.78.24: And he rained down manna upon them to eat, And gave them food from heaven.
texts.psa.78.25: Man did eat the bread of the mighty: He sent them food to the full.
texts.psa.78.26: He caused the east wind to blow in the heavens; And by his power he guided the south wind.
texts.psa.78.27: He rained flesh also upon them as the dust, And winged birds as the sand of the seas:
texts.psa.78.28: And he let it fall in the midst of their camp, Round about their habitations.
texts.psa.78.29: So they did eat, and were well filled; And he gave them their own desire.
texts.psa.78.30: They were not estranged from that which they desired, Their food was yet in their mouths,
texts.psa.78.31: When the anger of God went up against them, And slew of the fattest of them, And smote down the young men of Israel.
texts.psa.78.32: For all this they sinned still, And believed not in his wondrous works.
texts.psa.78.33: Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, And their years in terror.
texts.psa.78.34: When he slew them, then they inquired after him; And they returned and sought God earnestly.
texts.psa.78.35: And they remembered that God was their rock, And the Most High God their redeemer.
texts.psa.78.36: But they flattered him with their mouth, And lied unto him with their tongue.
texts.psa.78.37: For their heart was not right with him, Neither were they faithful in his covenant.
texts.psa.78.38: But he, being merciful, forgave [their] iniquity, and destroyed [them] not: Yea, many a time turned he his anger away, And did not stir up all his wrath.
texts.psa.78.39: And he remembered that they were but flesh, A wind that passeth away, and cometh not again.
texts.psa.78.40: How oft did they rebel against him in the wilderness, And grieve him in the desert!
texts.psa.78.41: And they turned again and tempted God, And provoked the Holy One of Israel.
texts.psa.78.42: They remember not his hand, Nor the day when he redeemed them from the adversary;
texts.psa.78.43: How he set his signs in Egypt, And his wonders in the field of Zoan,
texts.psa.78.44: And turned their rivers into blood, And their streams, so that they could not drink.
texts.psa.78.45: He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them; And frogs, which destroyed them.
texts.psa.78.46: He gave also their increase unto the caterpillar, And their labor unto the locust.
texts.psa.78.47: He destroyed their vines with hail, And their sycomore-trees with frost.
texts.psa.78.48: He gave over their cattle also to the hail, And their flocks to hot thunderbolts.
texts.psa.78.49: He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, Wrath, and indignation, and trouble, A band of angels of evil.
texts.psa.78.50: He made a path for his anger; He spared not their soul from death, But gave their life over to the pestilence,
texts.psa.78.51: And smote all the first-born in Egypt, The chief of their strength in the tents of Ham.
texts.psa.78.52: But he led forth his own people like sheep, And guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
texts.psa.78.53: And he led them safely, so that they feared not; But the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
texts.psa.78.54: And he brought them to the border of his sanctuary, To this mountain, which his right hand had gotten.
texts.psa.78.55: He drove out the nations also before them, And allotted them for an inheritance by line, And made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.
texts.psa.78.56: Yet they tempted and rebelled against the Most High God, And kept not his testimonies;
texts.psa.78.57: But turned back, and dealt treacherously like their fathers: They were turned aside like a deceitful bow.
texts.psa.78.58: For they provoked him to anger with their high places, And moved him to jealousy with their graven images.
texts.psa.78.59: When God heard [this], he was wroth, And greatly abhorred Israel;
texts.psa.78.60: So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, The tent which he placed among men;
texts.psa.78.61: And delivered his strength into captivity, And his glory into the adversary's hand.
texts.psa.78.62: He gave his people over also unto the sword, And was wroth with his inheritance.
texts.psa.78.63: Fire devoured their young men; And their virgins had no marriage-song.
texts.psa.78.64: Their priests fell by the sword; And their widows made no lamentation.
texts.psa.78.65: Then the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, Like a mighty man that shouteth by reason of wine.
texts.psa.78.66: And he smote his adversaries backward: He put them to a perpetual reproach.
texts.psa.78.67: Moreover he refused the tent of Joseph, And chose not the tribe of Ephraim,
texts.psa.78.68: But chose the tribe of Judah, The mount Zion which he loved.
texts.psa.78.69: And he built his sanctuary like the heights, Like the earth which he hath established for ever.
texts.psa.78.70: He chose David also his servant, And took him from the sheepfolds:
texts.psa.78.71: From following the ewes that have their young he brought him, To be the shepherd of Jacob his people, and Israel his inheritance.
texts.psa.78.72: So he was their shepherd according to the integrity of his heart, And guided them by the skilfulness of his hands.
texts.psa.79.1: A Psalm of Asaph. O God, the nations are come into thine inheritance; Thy holy temple have they defiled; They have laid Jerusalem in heaps.
texts.psa.79.2: The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be food unto the birds of the heavens, The flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.
texts.psa.79.3: Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; And there was none to bury them.
texts.psa.79.4: We are become a reproach to our neighbors, A scoffing and derision to them that are round about us.
texts.psa.79.5: How long, O Jehovah? wilt thou be angry for ever? Shall thy jealousy burn like fire?
texts.psa.79.6: Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that know thee not, And upon the kingdoms that call not upon thy name.
texts.psa.79.7: For they have devoured Jacob, And laid waste his habitation.
texts.psa.79.8: Remember not against us the iniquities of our forefathers: Let thy tender mercies speedily meet us; For we are brought very low.
texts.psa.79.9: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy name; And deliver us, and forgive our sins, for thy name's sake.
texts.psa.79.10: Wherefore should the nations say, Where is their God? Let the avenging of the blood of thy servants which is shed Be known among the nations in our sight.
texts.psa.79.11: Let the sighing of the prisoner come before thee: According to the greatness of thy power preserve thou those that are appointed to death;
texts.psa.79.12: And render unto our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom Their reproach, wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord.
texts.psa.79.13: So we thy people and sheep of thy pasture Will give thee thanks for ever: We will show forth thy praise to all generations.
texts.psa.80.1: For the Chief Musician, set to Shoshanim Eduth.. A Psalm of Asaph. Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; Thou that sittest [above] the cherubim, shine forth.
