texts.psa.37.8: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.
texts.psa.37.9: For evil doers shall be cut off: but those that wait upon the LORD, they shall inherit the earth.
texts.psa.37.10: For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: yes, thou shalt diligently consider his place, and it shall not be.
texts.psa.37.11: But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
texts.psa.37.12: The wicked plotteth against the just, and gnasheth upon him with his teeth.
texts.psa.37.13: The Lord will laugh at him: for he seeth that his day is coming.
texts.psa.37.14: The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, and to slay such as are of upright deportment.
texts.psa.37.15: Their sword shall enter into their own heart, and their bows shall be broken.
texts.psa.37.16: A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked.
texts.psa.37.17: For the arms of the wicked shall be broken: but the LORD upholdeth the righteous.
texts.psa.37.18: The LORD knoweth the days of the upright: and their inheritance shall be for ever.
texts.psa.37.19: They shall not be ashamed in the evil time: and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied.
texts.psa.37.20: But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the LORD shall be as the fat of lambs: they shall consume; into smoke shall they consume away.
texts.psa.37.21: The wicked borroweth, and payeth not again: but the righteous showeth mercy, and giveth.
texts.psa.37.22: For such as are blessed by him shall inherit the earth; and they that are cursed by him shall be cut off.
texts.psa.37.23: The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way.
texts.psa.37.24: Though he should fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand.
texts.psa.37.25: I have been young, and now am old; yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.
texts.psa.37.26: He is ever merciful, and lendeth; and his seed is blessed.
texts.psa.37.27: Depart from evil, and do good; and dwell for evermore.
texts.psa.37.28: For the LORD loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints; they are preserved for ever: but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off.
texts.psa.37.29: The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever.
texts.psa.37.30: The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom, and his tongue talketh of judgment.
texts.psa.37.31: The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide.
texts.psa.37.32: The wicked watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him.
texts.psa.37.33: The LORD will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when he is judged.
texts.psa.37.34: Wait on the LORD, and keep his way, and he will exalt thee to inherit the land: when the wicked are cut off, thou shalt see it.
texts.psa.37.35: I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree.
texts.psa.37.36: Yet he passed away, and lo, he was not: yes, I sought him, but he could not be found.
texts.psa.37.37: Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace.
texts.psa.37.38: But the transgressors shall be destroyed together: the end of the wicked shall be cut off.
texts.psa.37.39: But the salvation of the righteous is of the LORD: he is their strength in the time of trouble.
texts.psa.37.40: And the LORD will help them, and deliver them: he will deliver them from the wicked, and save them, because they trust in him.
texts.psa.38.1: A Psalm of David, to bring to remembrance. O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath: neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
texts.psa.38.2: For thy arrows stick fast in me, and thy hand falleth heavy upon me.
texts.psa.38.3: There is no soundness in my flesh because of thy anger; neither is there any rest in my bones because of my sin.
texts.psa.38.4: For my iniquities have gone over my head: as a heavy burden they are too heavy for me.
texts.psa.38.5: My wounds are offensive, and are corrupt because of my foolishness.
texts.psa.38.6: I am troubled; I am bowed down greatly; I go mourning all the day long.
texts.psa.38.7: For my loins are filled with a lothsome disease: and there is no soundness in my flesh.
texts.psa.38.8: I am feeble and grievously broken: I have roared by reason of the disquietness of my heart.
texts.psa.38.9: Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.
texts.psa.38.10: My heart panteth, my strength faileth me: as for the light of my eyes, that also is gone from me.
texts.psa.38.11: My lovers and my friends stand aloof from my affliction; and my kinsmen stand afar off.
texts.psa.38.12: They also that seek after my life lay snares for me: and they that seek my hurt speak mischievous things, and imagine deceits all the day long.
texts.psa.38.13: But I, as a deaf man, heard not; and I was as a dumb man that openeth not his mouth.
texts.psa.38.14: Thus I was as a man that heareth not, and in whose mouth are no reproofs.
texts.psa.38.15: For in thee, O LORD, do I hope: thou wilt hear, O Lord my God.
texts.psa.38.16: For I said, Hear me, lest otherwise they should rejoice over me: when my foot slippeth, they magnify themselves against me.
texts.psa.38.17: For I am ready to halt, and my sorrow is continually before me.
texts.psa.38.18: For I will declare my iniquity; I will be sorry for my sin.
texts.psa.38.19: But my enemies are lively, and they are strong: and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.
texts.psa.38.20: They also that render evil for good are my adversaries; because I follow the thing that is good.
texts.psa.38.21: Forsake me not, O LORD: O my God, be not far from me.
texts.psa.38.22: Make haste to help me, O Lord my salvation.
texts.psa.39.1: To the chief Musician, even to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David. I said, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue: I will keep my mouth with a bridle, while the wicked is before me.
texts.psa.39.2: I was dumb with silence, I held my peace, even from good; and my sorrow was stirred.
texts.psa.39.3: My heart was hot within me, while I was musing the fire burned: then I spoke with my tongue.
texts.psa.39.4: LORD, make me to know my end, and the measure of my days, what it is; that I may know how frail I am.
texts.psa.39.5: Behold, thou hast made my days as a hand-breadth; and my age is as nothing before thee: verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity. Selah.
texts.psa.39.6: Surely every man walketh in a vain show: surely they are disquieted in vain: he heapeth up riches, and knoweth not who shall gather them.
texts.psa.39.7: And now, Lord, what wait I for? my hope is in thee.
texts.psa.39.8: Deliver me from all my transgressions: make me not the reproach of the foolish.
texts.psa.39.9: I was dumb, I opened not my mouth; because thou didst it.
texts.psa.39.10: Remove thy stroke away from me; I am consumed by the blow of thy hand.
texts.psa.39.11: When thou with rebukes dost correct man for iniquity, thou makest his beauty to consume away like a moth: surely every man is vanity. Selah.
texts.psa.39.12: Hear my prayer, O LORD, and give ear to my cry; hold not thy peace at my tears: for I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner, as all my fathers were.
texts.psa.39.13: O spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go hence, and be no more.
texts.psa.40.1: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined to me, and heard my cry.
texts.psa.40.2: He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.
texts.psa.40.3: And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise to our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD.
texts.psa.40.4: Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.
texts.psa.40.5: Many, O LORD, my God, are thy wonderful works which thou hast done, and thy thoughts which are toward us, they cannot be reckoned up in order to thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered.
texts.psa.40.6: Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; my ears hast thou opened: burnt-offering and sin-offering hast thou not required.
texts.psa.40.7: Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me,
texts.psa.40.8: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.
texts.psa.40.9: I have preached righteousness in the great congregation: lo, I have not refrained my lips, O LORD, thou knowest.
texts.psa.40.10: I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared thy faithfulness and thy salvation: I have not concealed thy loving-kindness and thy truth from the great congregation.
texts.psa.40.11: Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy loving-kindness and thy truth continually preserve me.
texts.psa.40.12: For innumerable evils have encompassed me: my iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of my head: therefore my heart faileth me.
texts.psa.40.13: Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me: O LORD, make haste to help me.
texts.psa.40.14: Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil.
texts.psa.40.15: Let them be desolate for a reward of their shame that say to me, Aha, aha.
texts.psa.40.16: Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, The LORD be magnified.
texts.psa.40.17: But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no delay, O my God.
texts.psa.41.1: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in the time of trouble.
texts.psa.41.2: The LORD will preserve him, and keep him alive; and he shall be blessed upon the earth: and thou wilt not deliver him to the will of his enemies.
texts.psa.41.3: The LORD will strengthen him upon the bed of languishing: thou wilt make all his bed in his sickness.
texts.psa.41.4: I said, LORD, be merciful to me: heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee.
texts.psa.41.5: My enemies speak evil of me, When shall he die, and his name perish?
texts.psa.41.6: And if he cometh to see me, he speaketh vanity: his heart gathereth iniquity to itself; when he goeth abroad, he telleth it.
texts.psa.41.7: All that hate me whisper together against me: against me do they devise my hurt.
texts.psa.41.8: An evil disease, say they, cleaveth fast to him: and now that he lieth he shall rise no more.
texts.psa.41.9: Yes, my own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, who ate of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.
texts.psa.41.10: But thou, O LORD, be merciful to me, and raise me up, that I may requite them.
texts.psa.41.11: By this I know that thou favorest me, because my enemy doth not triumph over me.
texts.psa.41.12: And as for me, thou upholdest me in my integrity, and settest me before thy face for ever.
texts.psa.41.13: Blessed be the LORD God of Israel from everlasting, and to everlasting. Amen, and amen.
texts.psa.42.1: To the chief Musician, Maschil, for the sons of Korah. As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so my soul panteth after thee, O God.
texts.psa.42.2: My soul thirsteth for God, for the living God: when shall I come and appear before God?
texts.psa.42.3: My tears have been my food day and night, while they continually say to me, Where is thy God?
texts.psa.42.4: When I remember these things, I pour out my soul in me: for I had gone with the multitude, I went with them to the house of God, with the voice of joy and praise, with a multitude that kept holy-day.
texts.psa.42.5: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.
texts.psa.42.6: O my God, my soul is cast down within me: therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan, and of the Hermonites, from the hill Mizar.
texts.psa.42.7: Deep calleth to deep at the noise of thy water-spouts: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.
texts.psa.42.8: Yet the LORD will command his loving-kindness in the day-time, and in the night his song shall be with me, and my prayer to the God of my life.
texts.psa.42.9: I will say to God my rock, Why hast thou forgotten me? why go I mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?
texts.psa.42.10: As with a sword in my bones, my enemies reproach me; while they say daily to me, Where is thy God?
texts.psa.42.11: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
texts.psa.43.1: Judge me, O God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation: O deliver me from the deceitful and unjust man.
texts.psa.43.2: For thou art the God of my strength: why dost thou cast me off? why go I mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?
texts.psa.43.3: O send out thy light and thy truth: let them lead me; let them bring me to thy holy hill, and to thy tabernacles.
texts.psa.43.4: Then will I go to the altar of God, to God, my exceeding joy: yes, upon the harp will I praise thee, O God my God.
texts.psa.43.5: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
texts.psa.44.1: To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, Maschil. We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.
texts.psa.44.2: How thou didst drive out the heathen with thy hand, and didst plant them; how thou didst afflict the people, and cast them out.
texts.psa.44.3: For they obtained not the land in possession by their own sword, neither did their own arm save them: but thy right hand, and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance, because thou hadst a favor to them.
texts.psa.44.4: Thou art my King, O God: command deliverances for Jacob.
texts.psa.44.5: Through thee will we push down our enemies: through thy name we will tread them under that rise up against us.
texts.psa.44.6: For I will not trust in my bow, neither shall my sword save me.
texts.psa.44.7: But thou hast saved us from our enemies, and hast put them to shame that hated us.
texts.psa.44.8: In God we boast all the day long, and praise thy name for ever. Selah.
texts.psa.44.9: But thou hast cast off, and put us to shame; and goest not forth with our armies.
texts.psa.44.10: Thou makest us to turn back from the enemy: and they who hate us plunder for themselves.
texts.psa.44.11: Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for food; and hast scattered us among the heathen.
texts.psa.44.12: Thou sellest thy people for naught, and dost not increase thy wealth by their price.
texts.psa.44.13: Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and a derision to them that are around us.
texts.psa.44.14: Thou makest us a by-word among the heathen, a shaking of the head among the people.
texts.psa.44.15: My confusion is continually before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me,
texts.psa.44.16: For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth; by reason of the enemy and avenger.
texts.psa.44.17: All this is come upon us; yet we have not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt falsely in thy covenant.
texts.psa.44.18: Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way;
texts.psa.44.19: Though thou hast severely broke us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shades of death.
texts.psa.44.20: If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a strange god;
texts.psa.44.21: Will not God search out this? for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.
texts.psa.44.22: Yes, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
texts.psa.44.23: Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever.
texts.psa.44.24: Why hidest thou thy face, and forgettest our affliction and our oppression?
texts.psa.44.25: For our soul is bowed down to the dust: our belly cleaveth to the earth.
texts.psa.44.26: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies' sake.
texts.psa.45.1: To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim, for the sons of Korah, Maschil, A Song of loves. My heart is inditing a good matter: I speak of the things which I have made concerning the king: my tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
texts.psa.45.2: Thou art fairer than the children of men: grace is poured into thy lips: therefore God hath blessed thee for ever.
texts.psa.45.3: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O most mighty, with thy glory and thy majesty.
texts.psa.45.4: And in thy majesty ride prosperously because of truth and meekness and righteousness; and thy right hand shall teach thee terrible things.
texts.psa.45.5: Thy arrows are sharp in the heart of the king's enemies; by which the people fall under thee.
texts.psa.45.6: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the scepter of thy kingdom is a scepter of justice.
texts.psa.45.7: Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
texts.psa.45.8: All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, by which they have made thee glad.
texts.psa.45.9: Kings daughters were among thy honorable women: upon thy right hand stood the queen in gold of Ophir.
texts.psa.45.10: Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thy ear; forget also thy own people, and thy father's house;
texts.psa.45.11: So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy lord; and worship thou him.
texts.psa.45.12: And the daughter of Tyre shall be there with a gift; even the rich among the people shall entreat thy favor.
texts.psa.45.13: The king's daughter is all glorious within: her clothing is of wrought gold.
texts.psa.45.14: She shall be brought to the king in raiment of needle-work: the virgins her companions that follow her shall be brought to thee.
texts.psa.45.15: With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the king's palace.
texts.psa.45.16: Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth.
texts.psa.45.17: I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations: therefore shall the people praise thee for ever and ever.
texts.psa.46.1: To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, A Song upon Alamoth. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
texts.psa.46.2: Therefore will we not fear, though the earth shall be removed, and though the mountains shall be carried into the midst of the sea;
texts.psa.46.3: Though its waters shall roar and be disturbed, though the mountains shake with the swelling of it. Selah.
texts.psa.46.4: There is a river, the streams of which shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the Most High.
texts.psa.46.5: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.
texts.psa.46.6: The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved: he uttered his voice, the earth melted.
texts.psa.46.7: The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
texts.psa.46.8: Come, behold the works of the LORD, what desolations he hath made in the earth.
texts.psa.46.9: He maketh wars to cease to the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear asunder; he burneth the chariot in the fire.
texts.psa.46.10: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
texts.psa.46.11: The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
texts.psa.47.1: To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah. O clap your hands, all ye people; shout to God with the voice of triumph.
texts.psa.47.2: For the LORD most high is terrible; he is a great King over all the earth.
texts.psa.47.3: He shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet.
texts.psa.47.4: He shall choose our inheritance for us, the excellence of Jacob whom he loved. Selah.
texts.psa.47.5: God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.
texts.psa.47.6: Sing praises to God, sing praises: sing praises to our King, sing praises.
texts.psa.47.7: For God is the King of all the earth: sing ye praises with understanding.
texts.psa.47.8: God reigneth over the heathen: God sitteth upon the throne of his holiness.
texts.psa.47.9: The princes of the people are assembled, even the people of the God of Abraham: for the shields of the earth belong to God: he is greatly exalted.
texts.psa.48.1: A Song and Psalm for the sons of Korah. Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.
texts.psa.48.2: Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.
texts.psa.48.3: God is known in her palaces for a refuge.
texts.psa.48.4: For lo, the kings were assembled, they passed by together.
texts.psa.48.5: They saw it, and so they wondered; they were troubled, and hasted away.
texts.psa.48.6: Fear took hold upon them there, and pain, as of a woman in travail.
texts.psa.48.7: Thou breakest the ships of Tarshish with an east wind.
texts.psa.48.8: As we have heard, so have we seen in the city of the LORD of hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish it for ever. Selah.
texts.psa.48.9: We have thought of thy loving-kindness, O God, in the midst of thy temple.
texts.psa.48.10: According to thy name, O God, so is thy praise to the ends of the earth: thy right hand is full of righteousness.
texts.psa.48.11: Let mount Zion rejoice, let the daughters of Judah be glad, because of thy judgments.
texts.psa.48.12: Walk about Zion, and go round her: number her towers.
texts.psa.48.13: Mark ye well her bulwarks, consider her palaces; that ye may tell it to the generation following.
texts.psa.48.14: For this God is our God for ever and ever: he will be our guide even to death.
texts.psa.49.1: To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah. Hear this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world:
texts.psa.49.2: Both low and high, rich and poor together.
texts.psa.49.3: My mouth shall speak of wisdom; and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.
texts.psa.49.4: I will incline my ear to a parable: I will open my dark saying upon the harp.
texts.psa.49.5: Why should I fear in the days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels shall encompass me?
texts.psa.49.6: They that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches;
texts.psa.49.7: None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to God a ransom for him:
texts.psa.49.8: (For the redemption of their soul is precious, and it ceaseth for ever:)
texts.psa.49.9: That he should still live for ever, and not see corruption.
texts.psa.49.10: For he seeth that wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others.
texts.psa.49.11: Their inward thought is, that their houses shall continue for ever, and their dwelling places to all generations; they call their lands after their own names.
texts.psa.49.12: Nevertheless man being in honor abideth not: he is like the beasts that perish.
texts.psa.49.13: This their way is their folly: yet their posterity approve their sayings. Selah.
texts.psa.49.14: Like sheep they are laid in the grave; death shall feed on them; and the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning; and their beauty shall consume in the grave from their dwelling.
texts.psa.49.15: But God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave: for he shall receive me. Selah.
texts.psa.49.16: Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;
texts.psa.49.17: For when he dieth he shall carry nothing away: his glory shall not descend after him.
texts.psa.49.18: Though while he lived he blessed his soul: and men will praise thee, when thou doest well to thyself.
texts.psa.49.19: He shall go to the generation of his fathers; they shall never see light.
texts.psa.49.20: Man that is in honor, and understandeth not, is like the beasts that perish.
texts.psa.50.1: A Psalm of Asaph. The mighty God, even the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising to the setting of the sun.
texts.psa.50.2: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined.
texts.psa.50.3: Our God shall come, and shall not keep silence: a fire shall devour before him, and it shall be very tempestuous around him.
texts.psa.50.4: He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.
texts.psa.50.5: Gather my saints together to me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.
texts.psa.50.6: And the heavens shall declare his righteousness: for God is judge himself. Selah.
texts.psa.50.7: Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee: I am God, even thy God.
texts.psa.50.8: I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices or thy burnt-offerings, to have been continually before me.
texts.psa.50.9: I will take no bullock out of thy house, nor he-goats out of thy folds.
texts.psa.50.10: For every beast of the forest is mine, and the cattle upon a thousand hills.
texts.psa.50.11: I know all the fowls of the mountains: and the wild beasts of the field are mine.
texts.psa.50.12: If I were hungry, I would not tell thee: for the world is mine, and the fullness thereof.
texts.psa.50.13: Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
texts.psa.50.14: Offer to God thanksgiving; and pay thy vows to the Most High:
texts.psa.50.15: And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.
texts.psa.50.16: But to the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?
texts.psa.50.17: Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.
texts.psa.50.18: When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him, and hast been partaker with adulterers.
texts.psa.50.19: Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit.
texts.psa.50.20: Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thy own mother's son.
texts.psa.50.21: These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.
texts.psa.50.22: Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.
texts.psa.50.23: Whoever offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his deportment aright will I show the salvation of God.
texts.psa.51.1: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba. Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy loving-kindness: according to the multitude of thy tender mercies, blot out my transgressions.
texts.psa.51.2: Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
texts.psa.51.3: For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.
texts.psa.51.4: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mayest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.
texts.psa.51.5: Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.
texts.psa.51.6: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.
texts.psa.51.7: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
texts.psa.51.8: Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
texts.psa.51.9: Hide thy face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.
texts.psa.51.10: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
texts.psa.51.11: Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.
texts.psa.51.12: Restore to me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.
texts.psa.51.13: Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted to thee.
texts.psa.51.14: Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.
texts.psa.51.15: O Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall show forth thy praise.
texts.psa.51.16: For thou desirest not sacrifice: else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt-offering.
texts.psa.51.17: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
texts.psa.51.18: Do good in thy good pleasure to Zion: build thou the walls of Jerusalem.
texts.psa.51.19: Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt-offering and whole burnt-offering: then shall they offer bullocks upon thy altar.
texts.psa.52.1: To the chief Musician, Maschil, A Psalm of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said to him, David is come to the house of Ahimelech. Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God endureth continually.
texts.psa.52.2: Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.
texts.psa.52.3: Thou lovest evil more than good; and lying rather than to speak righteousness. Selah.
texts.psa.52.4: Thou lovest all devouring words, O thou deceitful tongue.
texts.psa.52.5: God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling-place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah.
texts.psa.52.6: The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him:
texts.psa.52.7: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength; but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness.
texts.psa.52.8: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.
texts.psa.52.9: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: and I will wait on thy name; for it is good before thy saints.
texts.psa.53.1: To the chief Musician upon Mahalath, Maschil, A Psalm of David. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt, and have done abominable iniquity: there is none that doeth good.
texts.psa.53.2: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.
texts.psa.53.3: Every one of them is gone back: they are altogether become filthy; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.
texts.psa.53.4: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people as they eat bread! they have not called upon God.
texts.psa.53.5: There they were in great fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them.
texts.psa.53.6: O that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! when God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
texts.psa.54.1: To the chief Musician on Neginoth, Maschil, A Psalm of David, when the Ziphims came and said to Saul, Doth not David hide himself with us? Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me by thy strength.
texts.psa.54.2: Hear my prayer, O God; give ear to the words of my mouth.
texts.psa.54.3: For strangers have risen up against me, and oppressors seek after my soul: they have not set God before them. Selah.
texts.psa.54.4: Behold, God is my helper: the Lord is with them that uphold my soul.
texts.psa.54.5: He will reward evil to my enemies; cut them off in thy truth.
texts.psa.54.6: I will freely sacrifice to thee: I will praise thy name, O LORD; for it is good.
texts.psa.54.7: For he hath delivered me out of all trouble: and my eye hath seen its desire upon my enemies.
texts.psa.55.1: To the chief Musician on Neginoth, Maschil, A Psalm of David. Give ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.
texts.psa.55.2: Attend to me, and hear me: I mourn in my complaint, and make a noise;
texts.psa.55.3: Because of the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked: for they cast iniquity upon me, and in wrath they hate me.
texts.psa.55.4: My heart is severely pained within me: and the terrors of death have fallen upon me.
texts.psa.55.5: Fearfulness and trembling have come upon me, and horror hath overwhelmed me.
texts.psa.55.6: And I said, O that I had wings like a dove! for then I would fly away, and be at rest.
texts.psa.55.7: Lo, then I would wander far off, and remain in the wilderness. Selah.
texts.psa.55.8: I would hasten my escape from the windy storm and tempest.
texts.psa.55.9: Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongues: for I have seen violence and strife in the city.
texts.psa.55.10: Day and night they go about it upon its walls: mischief also and sorrow are in the midst of it.
texts.psa.55.11: Wickedness is in the midst of it: deceit and guile depart not from her streets.
texts.psa.55.12: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that magnified himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him:
texts.psa.55.13: But it was thou, a man my equal, my guide, and my acquaintance.
texts.psa.55.14: We took sweet counsel together, and walked to the house of God in company.
texts.psa.55.15: Let death seize upon them, and let them go down quick into hell: for wickedness is in their dwellings, and among them.
texts.psa.55.16: As for me, I will call upon God: and the LORD will save me.
texts.psa.55.17: Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he will hear my voice.
texts.psa.55.18: He hath delivered my soul in peace from the battle that was against me: for there were many with me.
texts.psa.55.19: God will hear and afflict them, even he that abideth of old. Selah. Because they have no changes, therefore they fear not God.
texts.psa.55.20: He hath put forth his hands against such as are at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant.
texts.psa.55.21: The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.
texts.psa.55.22: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he will sustain thee: he will never suffer the righteous to be moved.
texts.psa.55.23: But thou, O God, wilt bring them down into the pit of destruction: bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; but I will trust in thee.
texts.psa.56.1: To the chief Musician upon Jonathelem-rechokim, Michtam of David, when the Philistines took him in Gath. Be merciful to me, O God: for man would swallow me up; he fighting daily oppresseth me.
texts.psa.56.2: My enemies would daily swallow me up: for they are many that fight against me, O thou Most High.
texts.psa.56.3: In the time when I am afraid, I will trust in thee.
texts.psa.56.4: In God I will praise his word, in God I have put my trust; I will not fear what flesh can do to me.
texts.psa.56.5: Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts are against me for evil.
texts.psa.56.6: They assemble themselves, they hide themselves, they mark my steps, when they wait for my soul.
texts.psa.56.7: Shall they escape by iniquity; in thy anger cast down the people, O God.
texts.psa.56.8: Thou numberest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
texts.psa.56.9: When I cry to thee, then shall my enemies turn back: this I know; for God is for me.
texts.psa.56.10: In God will I praise his word: in the LORD will I praise his word.
texts.psa.56.11: In God have I put my trust: I will not be afraid what man can do to me.
texts.psa.56.12: Thy vows are upon me, O God: I will render praises to thee.
texts.psa.56.13: For thou hast delivered my soul from death: wilt thou not deliver my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living?
texts.psa.57.1: To the chief Musician, Al-taschith, Michtam of David, when he fled from Saul in the cave. Be merciful to me, O God, be merciful to me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yes, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities are overpast.
texts.psa.57.2: I will cry to God most high; to God that performeth all things for me.
texts.psa.57.3: He shall send from heaven, and save me from the reproach of him that would swallow me up. Selah. God shall send forth his mercy and his truth.
texts.psa.57.4: My soul is among lions: and I lie even among them that are set on fire, even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
texts.psa.57.5: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; let thy glory be above all the earth.
texts.psa.57.6: They have prepared a net for my steps; my soul is bowed down: they have digged a pit before me, into the midst of which they have fallen themselves. Selah.
texts.psa.57.7: My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise.
texts.psa.57.8: Awake, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake early.
texts.psa.57.9: I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: I will sing to thee among the nations.
texts.psa.57.10: For thy mercy is great to the heavens, and thy truth to the clouds.
texts.psa.57.11: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: let thy glory be above all the earth.
texts.psa.58.1: To the chief Musician, Al-taschith, Michtam of David. Do ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?
texts.psa.58.2: Yes, in heart ye work wickedness; ye weigh the violence of your hands in the earth.
texts.psa.58.3: The wicked are estranged from their birth: they go astray as soon as they are born, speaking lies.
texts.psa.58.4: Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: they are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear;
texts.psa.58.5: Which will not hearken to the voice of charmers, charming never so wisely.
texts.psa.58.6: Break their teeth, O God, in their mouth: break out the great teeth of the young lions, O LORD.
texts.psa.58.7: Let them melt away as waters which run continually: when he bendeth his bow to shoot his arrows, let them be as cut in pieces.
texts.psa.58.8: As a snail which melteth, let every one of them pass away: like the untimely birth of a woman, that they may not see the sun.
texts.psa.58.9: Before your pots can feel the thorns, he shall take them away as with a whirlwind, both living, and in his wrath.
texts.psa.58.10: The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance: he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.
texts.psa.58.11: So that a man shall say, Verily there is a reward for the righteous: verily he is a God that judgeth in the earth.
texts.psa.59.1: To the chief Musician, Al-taschith, Michtam of David; when Saul sent, and they watched the house to kill him. Deliver me from my enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.
texts.psa.59.2: Deliver me from the workers of iniquity, and save me from bloody men.
texts.psa.59.3: For lo, they lie in wait for my soul: the mighty are gathered against me; not for my transgression, nor for my sin, O LORD.
texts.psa.59.4: They run and prepare themselves without my fault: awake to help me, and behold.
texts.psa.59.5: Thou therefore, O LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel, awake to visit all the heathen: be not merciful to any wicked transgressors. Selah.
texts.psa.59.6: They return at evening: they make a noise like a dog, and go about the city.
texts.psa.59.7: Behold, they belch out with their mouth: swords are in their lips: for who, say they, doth hear?
texts.psa.59.8: But thou, O LORD, shalt laugh at them; thou shalt have all the heathen in derision.
texts.psa.59.9: Because of his strength will I wait upon thee: for God is my defense.
texts.psa.59.10: The God of my mercy will succor me: God will let me see my desire upon my enemies.
texts.psa.59.11: Slay them not, lest my people forget: scatter them by thy power; and bring them down, O Lord our shield.
texts.psa.59.12: For the sin of their mouth and the words of their lips let them even be taken in their pride: and for cursing and lying which they speak.
texts.psa.59.13: Consume them in wrath, consume them, that they may not be: and let them know that God ruleth in Jacob to the ends of the earth. Selah.
texts.psa.59.14: And at evening let them return; and let them make a noise like a dog, and go about the city.
texts.psa.59.15: Let them wander up and down for food, and grudge if they are not satisfied.
texts.psa.59.16: But I will sing of thy power; yes, I will sing aloud of thy mercy in the morning: for thou hast been my defense and refuge in the day of my trouble.
texts.psa.59.17: To thee, O my strength, will I sing: for God is my defense, and the God of my mercy.
texts.psa.60.1: To the chief Musician upon Shushan-eduth, Michtam of David, to teach; when he strove with Aram-naharaim and with Aram-zobah, when Joab returned, and smote of Edom in the valley of salt twelve thousand. O God, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.
texts.psa.60.2: Thou hast made the earth to tremble; thou hast broken it: heal its breaches; for it shaketh.
texts.psa.60.3: Thou hast shown thy people hard things: thou hast made us to drink the wine of astonishment.
texts.psa.60.4: Thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee, that it may be displayed because of the truth. Selah.
texts.psa.60.5: That thy beloved may be delivered; save with thy right hand, and hear me.
texts.psa.60.6: God hath spoken in his holiness; I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of Succoth.
texts.psa.60.7: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the strength of my head; Judah is my lawgiver;
texts.psa.60.8: Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe: Philistia, triumph thou because of me.
texts.psa.60.9: Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?
texts.psa.60.10: Wilt thou not, O God, who hadst cast us off? and thou, O God, who didst not go out with our armies?
texts.psa.60.11: Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man.
texts.psa.60.12: Through God we shall do valiantly: for he will tread down our enemies.
texts.psa.61.1: To the chief Musician upon Neginah, A Psalm of David. Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.
texts.psa.61.2: From the end of the earth will I cry to thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
texts.psa.61.3: For thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the enemy.
texts.psa.61.4: I will abide in thy tabernacle for ever: I will trust in the covert of thy wings. Selah.
texts.psa.61.5: For thou, O God, hast heard my vows: thou hast given me the heritage of those that fear thy name.
texts.psa.61.6: Thou wilt prolong the king's life: and his years as many generations.
texts.psa.61.7: He shall abide before God for ever: O prepare mercy and truth, which may preserve him.
texts.psa.61.8: So will I sing praise to thy name for ever, that I may daily perform my vows.
texts.psa.62.1: To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David. Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
texts.psa.62.2: He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defense; I shall not be greatly moved.
texts.psa.62.3: How long will ye imagine mischief against a man? ye shall be slain all of you: as a bowing wall shall ye be, and as a tottering fence.
texts.psa.62.4: They only consult to cast him down from his excellence: they delight in lies: they bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah.
texts.psa.62.5: My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.
texts.psa.62.6: He only is my rock and my salvation: he is my defense; I shall not be moved.
texts.psa.62.7: In God is my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
texts.psa.62.8: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.
texts.psa.62.9: Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: to be laid in the balance, they are altogether lighter than vanity.
texts.psa.62.10: Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.
texts.psa.62.11: God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth to God.
texts.psa.62.12: Also to thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work.
texts.psa.63.1: A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
texts.psa.63.2: To see thy power and thy glory, so as I have seen thee in the sanctuary.
texts.psa.63.3: Because thy loving-kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise thee.
texts.psa.63.4: Thus will I bless thee while I live: I will lift up my hands in thy name.
texts.psa.63.5: My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness; and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips:
texts.psa.63.6: When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches.
texts.psa.63.7: Because thou hast been my help, therefore in the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.
texts.psa.63.8: My soul followeth hard after thee: thy right hand upholdeth me.
texts.psa.63.9: But those that seek my soul to destroy it, shall go into the lower parts of the earth.
texts.psa.63.10: They shall fall by the sword: they shall be a portion for foxes.
texts.psa.63.11: But the king shall rejoice in God; every one that sweareth by him shall glory: but the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped.
texts.psa.64.1: To the chief Musician, a Psalm of David. Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
texts.psa.64.2: Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked; from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity:
texts.psa.64.3: Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words:
texts.psa.64.4: That they may shoot in secret at the perfect: suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not.
texts.psa.64.5: They encourage themselves in an evil matter: they commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who will see them?
texts.psa.64.6: They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.
texts.psa.64.7: But God shall shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly shall they be wounded.
texts.psa.64.8: So they shall make their own tongue to fall upon themselves: all that see them shall flee away.
texts.psa.64.9: And all men shall fear, and shall declare the work of God; for they shall wisely consider of his doing.
texts.psa.64.10: The righteous shall be glad in the LORD, and shall trust in him; and all the upright in heart shall glory.
texts.psa.65.1: To the chief Musician, A Psalm and Song of David. Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Zion: and to thee shall the vow be performed.
texts.psa.65.2: O thou that hearest prayer, to thee shall all flesh come.
texts.psa.65.3: Iniquities prevail against me: as for our transgressions, thou shalt purge them away.
texts.psa.65.4: Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach to thee, that he may dwell in thy courts: we shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, even of thy holy temple.
texts.psa.65.5: By terrible things in righteousness wilt thou answer us, O God of our salvation; who art the confidence of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are afar off upon the sea:
texts.psa.65.6: Who by his strength setteth fast the mountains; being girded with power:
texts.psa.65.7: Who stilleth the noise of the seas, the noise of their waves, and the tumult of the people.
texts.psa.65.8: They also that dwell in the uttermost parts are afraid at thy tokens: thou makest the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice.
texts.psa.65.9: Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it: thou greatly enrichest it with the river of God, which is full of water: thou preparest them corn, when thou hast so provided for it.
texts.psa.65.10: Thou waterest the ridges of it abundantly: thou settlest the furrows of it: thou makest it soft with showers: thou blessest the springing of it.
texts.psa.65.11: Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; and thy paths drop fatness.
texts.psa.65.12: They drop upon the pastures of the wilderness: and the little hills rejoice on every side.
texts.psa.65.13: The pastures are clothed with flocks; the valleys also are covered over with corn; they shout for joy, they also sing.
texts.psa.66.1: To the chief Musician, A Song or Psalm. Make a joyful noise to God, all ye lands:
texts.psa.66.2: Sing forth the honor of his name: make his praise glorious.
texts.psa.66.3: Say to God, How terrible art thou in thy works! through the greatness of thy power shall thy enemies submit themselves to thee.
texts.psa.66.4: All the earth shall worship thee, and shall sing to thee; they shall sing to thy name. Selah.
texts.psa.66.5: Come and see the works of God: he is terrible in his doing towards the children of men.
texts.psa.66.6: He turned the sea into dry land: they went through the flood on foot: there we rejoiced in him.
texts.psa.66.7: He ruleth by his power for ever; his eyes behold the nations: let not the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah.
texts.psa.66.8: O bless our God, ye people, and make the voice of his praise to be heard:
texts.psa.66.9: Who holdeth our soul in life, and suffereth not our feet to be moved.
texts.psa.66.10: For thou, O God, hast proved us: thou hast tried us, as silver is tried.
texts.psa.66.11: Thou hast brought us into the net; thou hast laid affliction upon our loins.
texts.psa.66.12: Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place.
texts.psa.66.13: I will go into thy house with burnt-offerings: I will pay thee my vows,
texts.psa.66.14: Which my lips have uttered, and my mouth hath spoken, when I was in trouble.
texts.psa.66.15: I will offer to thee burnt-sacrifices of fatlings, with the incense of rams; I will offer bullocks with goats. Selah.
texts.psa.66.16: Come and hear, all ye that fear God, and I will declare what he hath done for my soul.
texts.psa.66.17: I cried to him with my mouth, and he was extolled with my tongue.
texts.psa.66.18: If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me:
texts.psa.66.19: But verily God hath heard me; he hath attended to the voice of my prayer.
texts.psa.66.20: Blessed be God, who hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.
texts.psa.67.1: To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm or Song. God be merciful to us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us. Selah.
texts.psa.67.2: That thy way may be known upon earth, thy saving health among all nations.
texts.psa.67.3: Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee.
texts.psa.67.4: O let the nations be glad and sing for joy: for thou shalt judge the people righteously, and govern the nations upon earth. Selah.
texts.psa.67.5: Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee.
texts.psa.67.6: Then shall the earth yield her increase; and God, even our own God, will bless us.
texts.psa.67.7: God will bless us, and all the ends of the earth shall fear him.
texts.psa.68.1: To the chief Musician, A Psalm or Song of David. Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.
texts.psa.68.2: As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
texts.psa.68.3: But let the righteous be glad; let them rejoice before God: yes, let them exceedingly rejoice.
texts.psa.68.4: Sing to God, sing praises to his name: extol him that rideth upon the heavens by his name JAH, and rejoice before him.
texts.psa.68.5: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
texts.psa.68.6: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those who are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.
texts.psa.68.7: O God, when thou wentest forth before thy people, when thou didst march through the wilderness; Selah:
texts.psa.68.8: The earth shook, the heavens also dropped at the presence of God: even Sinai itself was moved at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
texts.psa.68.9: Thou, O God, didst send a plentiful rain, by which thou didst confirm thy inheritance, when it was weary.
texts.psa.68.10: Thy congregation hath dwelt therein: thou, O God, hast prepared of thy goodness for the poor.
texts.psa.68.11: The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.
texts.psa.68.12: Kings of armies fled apace: and she that tarried at home divided the spoil.
texts.psa.68.13: Though ye have lain among the pots, yet shall ye be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with yellow gold.
texts.psa.68.14: When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was white as snow in Salmon.
texts.psa.68.15: The hill of God is as the hill of Bashan; a high hill as the hill of Bashan.
texts.psa.68.16: Why leap ye, ye lofty hills? this is the hill which God desireth to dwell in; yes, the LORD will dwell in it for ever.
texts.psa.68.17: The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels: the Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in the holy place.
texts.psa.68.18: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yes, for the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell among them.
texts.psa.68.19: Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. Selah.
texts.psa.68.20: He that is our God is the God of salvation; and to GOD the Lord belong the issues from death.
texts.psa.68.21: But God will wound the head of his enemies, and the hairy scalp of such one as goeth on still in his trespasses.
texts.psa.68.22: The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring my people again from the depths of the sea.
texts.psa.68.23: That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thy enemies, and the tongue of thy dogs in the same.
texts.psa.68.24: They have seen thy goings, O God; even the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.
texts.psa.68.25: The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels.
texts.psa.68.26: Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.
texts.psa.68.27: There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their counsel, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.
texts.psa.68.28: Thy God hath commanded thy strength: strengthen, O God, that which thou hast wrought for us.
texts.psa.68.29: Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents to thee.
texts.psa.68.30: Rebuke the company of spearmen, the multitude of the bulls, with the calves of the people, till every one shall submit himself with pieces of silver: scatter thou the people that delight in war.
texts.psa.68.31: Princes shall come out of Egypt; Cush shall soon stretch out her hands to God.
texts.psa.68.32: Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth; O sing praises to the Lord; Selah:
texts.psa.68.33: To him that rideth upon the heavens of heavens, which were of old; lo, he doth send out his voice, and that a mighty voice.
texts.psa.68.34: Ascribe ye strength to God: his excellence is over Israel, and his strength is in the clouds.
texts.psa.68.35: O God, thou art terrible out of thy holy places: the God of Israel is he that giveth strength and power to his people. Blessed be God.
texts.psa.69.1: To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim, A Psalm of David. Save me, O God; for the waters are come in to my soul.
texts.psa.69.2: I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
texts.psa.69.3: I am weary of my crying: my throat is dried: my eyes fail while I wait for my God.
texts.psa.69.4: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head: they that would destroy me, being my enemies wrongfully, are mighty: then I restored that which I took not away.
texts.psa.69.5: O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my sins are not hid from thee.
texts.psa.69.6: Let not them that wait on thee, O Lord GOD of hosts, be ashamed for my sake: let not those that seek thee be confounded for my sake, O God of Israel.
texts.psa.69.7: Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; shame hath covered my face.
texts.psa.69.8: I am become a stranger to my brethren, and an alien to my mother's children.
texts.psa.69.9: For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee have fallen upon me.
texts.psa.69.10: When I wept, and chastened my soul with fasting, that was to my reproach.
texts.psa.69.11: I made sackcloth also my garment; and I became a proverb to them.
texts.psa.69.12: They that sit in the gate speak against me; and I was the song of the drunkards.
texts.psa.69.13: But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O LORD, in an acceptable time: O God, in the multitude of thy mercy hear me, in the truth of thy salvation.
texts.psa.69.14: Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink: let me be delivered from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.
texts.psa.69.15: Let not the water-flood overflow me, neither let the deep swallow me up, and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.
texts.psa.69.16: Hear me, O LORD; for thy loving-kindness is good: turn to me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.
texts.psa.69.17: And hide not thy face from thy servant; for I am in trouble: hear me speedily.
texts.psa.69.18: Draw nigh to my soul, and redeem it: deliver me because of my enemies.
texts.psa.69.19: Thou hast known my reproach, and my shame, and my dishonor: my adversaries are all before thee.
texts.psa.69.20: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: and I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none.
texts.psa.69.21: They gave me also gall for my food; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
texts.psa.69.22: Let their table become a snare before them: and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap.
texts.psa.69.23: Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not; and make their loins continually to shake.
texts.psa.69.24: Pour out thy indignation upon them, and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.
texts.psa.69.25: Let their habitation be desolate; and let none dwell in their tents.
texts.psa.69.26: For they persecute him whom thou hast smitten; and they talk to the grief of those whom thou hast wounded.
texts.psa.69.27: Add iniquity to their iniquity: and let them not come into thy righteousness.
texts.psa.69.28: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.
texts.psa.69.29: But I am poor and sorrowful: let thy salvation, O God, set me up on high.
texts.psa.69.30: I will praise the name of God with a song, and will magnify him with thanksgiving.
texts.psa.69.31: This also shall please the LORD better than an ox or bullock that hath horns and hoofs.
texts.psa.69.32: The humble shall see this, and be glad: and your heart shall live that seek God.
texts.psa.69.33: For the LORD heareth the poor, and despiseth not his prisoners.
texts.psa.69.34: Let the heaven and earth praise him, the seas, and every thing that moveth therein.
texts.psa.69.35: For God will save Zion, and will build the cities of Judah: that they may dwell there, and have it in possession.
texts.psa.69.36: The seed also of his servants shall inherit it: and they that love his name shall dwell therein.
texts.psa.70.1: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David to bring to remembrance. Make haste, O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, O LORD.
texts.psa.70.2: Let them be ashamed and confounded that seek after my soul: let them be turned backward, and put to confusion, that desire my hurt.
texts.psa.70.3: Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame that say, Aha, aha.
texts.psa.70.4: Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: and let such as love thy salvation say continually, Let God be magnified.
texts.psa.70.5: But I am poor and needy: make haste to me, O God: thou art my help and my deliverer; O LORD, make no delay.
texts.psa.71.1: In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion.
texts.psa.71.2: Deliver me in thy righteousness, and cause me to escape: incline thy ear to me, and save me.
texts.psa.71.3: Be thou my strong habitation, to which I may continually resort: thou hast given commandment to save me; for thou art my rock and my fortress.
texts.psa.71.4: Deliver me, O my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.
texts.psa.71.5: For thou art my hope, O Lord GOD: thou art my trust from my youth.
texts.psa.71.6: By thee have I been sustained from my birth: thou art he that brought me into life: my praise shall be continually of thee.
texts.psa.71.7: I am as a wonder to many; but thou art my strong refuge.
texts.psa.71.8: Let my mouth be filled with thy praise and with thy honor all the day.
texts.psa.71.9: Cast me not off in the time of old age; forsake me not when my strength faileth.
texts.psa.71.10: For my enemies speak against me; and they that lay wait for my soul take counsel together,
texts.psa.71.11: Saying, God hath forsaken him: persecute and take him; for there is none to deliver him.
texts.psa.71.12: O God, be not far from me: O my God, make haste for my help.
texts.psa.71.13: Let them be confounded and consumed that are adversaries to my soul; let them be covered with reproach and dishonor that seek my hurt.
texts.psa.71.14: But I will hope continually, and will yet praise thee more and more.
texts.psa.71.15: My mouth shall show forth thy righteousness and thy salvation all the day; for I know not the numbers thereof.
texts.psa.71.16: I will go in the strength of the Lord GOD: I will make mention of thy righteousness, even of thine only.
texts.psa.71.17: O God, thou hast taught me from my youth: and hitherto have I declared thy wondrous works.
texts.psa.71.18: Now also when I am old and gray-headed, O God, forsake me not; until I have shown thy strength to this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come.
texts.psa.71.19: Thy righteousness also, O God, is very high, who hast done great things: O God, who is like to thee!
texts.psa.71.20: Thou, who hast shown me great and severe troubles, wilt revive me again, and wilt bring me again from the depths of the earth.
texts.psa.71.21: Thou wilt increase my greatness, and comfort me on every side.
texts.psa.71.22: I will also praise thee with the psaltery, even thy truth, O my God: to thee will I sing with the harp, O thou Holy One of Israel.
texts.psa.71.23: My lips shall greatly rejoice when I sing to thee; and my soul, which thou hast redeemed.
texts.psa.71.24: My tongue also shall talk of thy righteousness all the day long: for they are confounded, for they are brought to shame, that seek my hurt.
texts.psa.72.1: A Psalm for Solomon. Give the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness to the king's son.
texts.psa.72.2: He shall judge thy people with righteousness, and thy poor with judgment.
texts.psa.72.3: The mountains shall bring peace to the people, and the little hills, by righteousness.
texts.psa.72.4: He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.
texts.psa.72.5: They shall fear thee as long as the sun and moon endure, throughout all generations.
texts.psa.72.6: He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass: as showers that water the earth.
texts.psa.72.7: In his days shall the righteous flourish; and abundance of peace so long as the moon endureth.
texts.psa.72.8: He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.
texts.psa.72.9: They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust.
texts.psa.72.10: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents: the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.
texts.psa.72.11: Yes, all kings shall fall down before him: all nations shall serve him.
texts.psa.72.12: For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper.
texts.psa.72.13: He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy.
texts.psa.72.14: He shall redeem their soul from deceit and violence: and precious shall be their blood in his sight.
texts.psa.72.15: And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba: prayer also shall be made for him continually; and daily shall he be praised.
texts.psa.72.16: There shall be a handful of corn in the earth upon the top of the mountains; the fruit of it shall shake like Lebanon: and they of the city shall flourish like grass of the earth.
texts.psa.72.17: His name shall endure for ever: his name shall be continued as long as the sun: and men shall be blessed in him: all nations shall call him blessed.
texts.psa.72.18: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who only doeth wondrous things.
texts.psa.72.19: And blessed be his glorious name for ever: and let the whole earth be filled with his glory; Amen, and amen.
texts.psa.72.20: The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended.
texts.psa.73.1: A Psalm of Asaph. Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart.
texts.psa.73.2: But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped.
texts.psa.73.3: For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
texts.psa.73.4: For there are no bands in their death: but their strength is firm.
texts.psa.73.5: They are not in trouble as other men; neither are they afflicted like other men.
texts.psa.73.6: Therefore pride encompasseth them as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment.
texts.psa.73.7: Their eyes stand out with fatness: they have more than heart could wish.
texts.psa.73.8: They are corrupt, and speak wickedly concerning oppression: they speak loftily.
texts.psa.73.9: They set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walketh through the earth.
texts.psa.73.10: Therefore his people return hither: and waters of a full cup are wrung out to them.
texts.psa.73.11: And they say, How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the Most High?
texts.psa.73.12: Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.
texts.psa.73.13: Verily I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocence.
texts.psa.73.14: For all the day long have I been afflicted, and chastened every morning.
texts.psa.73.15: If I say, I will speak thus; behold, I should offend against the generation of thy children.
texts.psa.73.16: When I thought to know this, it was too painful for me;
texts.psa.73.17: Until I went into the sanctuary of God; then I understood their end.
texts.psa.73.18: Surely thou didst set them in slippery places: thou didst cast them down into destruction.
texts.psa.73.19: How are they brought into desolation, as in a moment! they are utterly consumed with terrors.
texts.psa.73.20: As a dream when one awaketh; so, O Lord, when thou awakest, thou wilt despise their image.
texts.psa.73.21: Thus my heart was grieved, and I was pricked in my reins.
texts.psa.73.22: So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.
texts.psa.73.23: Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast held me by my right hand.
texts.psa.73.24: Thou wilt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.
texts.psa.73.25: Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire besides thee.
texts.psa.73.26: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
texts.psa.73.27: For lo, they that are far from thee shall perish: thou hast destroyed all them that go astray from thee.
texts.psa.73.28: But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord GOD, that I may declare all thy works.
texts.psa.74.1: Maschil of Asaph. O God, why hast thou cast us off for ever? why doth thy anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
texts.psa.74.2: Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old: the rod of thy inheritance, which thou hast redeemed; this mount Zion, in which thou hast dwelt.
texts.psa.74.3: Lift up thy feet to the perpetual desolations; even all that the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.
texts.psa.74.4: Thy enemies roar in the midst of thy congregations; they set up their ensigns for signs.
texts.psa.74.5: A man was famous according as he had lifted up axes upon the thick trees.
texts.psa.74.6: But now they break down the carved work of it at once with axes and hammers.
texts.psa.74.7: They have cast fire into thy sanctuary, they have defiled by casting down the dwelling-place of thy name to the ground.
texts.psa.74.8: They said in their hearts, Let us destroy them together: they have burned up all the synagogues of God in the land.
texts.psa.74.9: We see not our signs: there is no more any prophet: neither is there among us any that knoweth how long.
texts.psa.74.10: O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?
texts.psa.74.11: Why withdrawest thou thy hand, even thy right hand? pluck it out of thy bosom.
texts.psa.74.12: For God is my King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
texts.psa.74.13: Thou didst divide the sea by thy strength: thou didst break the heads of the dragons in the waters.
texts.psa.74.14: Thou didst break the head of leviathan in pieces, and didst give him to be food to the people inhabiting the wilderness.
texts.psa.74.15: Thou didst cleave the fountain and the flood: thou didst dry up mighty rivers.
texts.psa.74.16: The day is thine, the night also is thine: thou hast prepared the light and the sun.
texts.psa.74.17: Thou hast set all the borders of the earth: thou hast made summer and winter.
texts.psa.74.18: Remember this, the enemy hath reproached, O LORD, and the foolish people have blasphemed thy name.
texts.psa.74.19: O deliver not the soul of thy turtle dove to the multitude of the wicked: forget not the congregation of thy poor for ever.
texts.psa.74.20: Have respect to the covenant: for the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of cruelty.
texts.psa.74.21: O let not the oppressed return ashamed: let the poor and needy praise thy name.
texts.psa.74.22: Arise, O God, plead thy own cause: remember how the foolish man reproacheth thee daily.
texts.psa.74.23: Forget not the voice of thy enemies: the tumult of those that rise against thee increaseth continually.
texts.psa.75.1: To the chief Musician, Al-taschith, A Psalm or Song of Asaph. To thee, O God, do we give thanks, to thee do we give thanks: for that thy name is near, thy wondrous works declare.
texts.psa.75.2: When I shall receive the congregation I will judge uprightly.
texts.psa.75.3: The earth and all its inhabitants are dissolved: I bear up the pillars of it. Selah.
texts.psa.75.4: I said to the fools, Deal not foolishly; and to the wicked, Lift not up the horn:
texts.psa.75.5: Lift not up your horn on high: speak not with a stiff neck.
texts.psa.75.6: For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south.
texts.psa.75.7: But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another.
texts.psa.75.8: For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture, and he poureth out of the same: but the dregs of it all the wicked of the earth shall wring them out, and drink them.
texts.psa.75.9: But I will declare for ever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
texts.psa.75.10: All the horns of the wicked also will I cut off; but the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.
texts.psa.76.1: To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm or Song of Asaph. In Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel.
texts.psa.76.2: In Salem also is his tabernacle, and his dwelling place in Zion.
texts.psa.76.3: There he broke the arrows of the bow, the shield, and the sword, and the battle. Selah.
texts.psa.76.4: Thou art more glorious and excellent than the mountains of prey.
texts.psa.76.5: The stout-hearted are spoiled, they have slept their sleep: and none of the men of might have found their hands.
texts.psa.76.6: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, both the chariot and horse are cast into a dead sleep.
texts.psa.76.7: Thou, even thou, art to be feared: and who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?
texts.psa.76.8: Thou didst cause judgment to be heard from heaven; the earth feared, and was still,
texts.psa.76.9: When God arose to judgment, to save all the meek of the earth. Selah.
texts.psa.76.10: Surely the wrath of man shall praise thee: the remainder of wrath wilt thou restrain.
texts.psa.76.11: Vow, and pay to the LORD your God: let all that are about him bring presents to him that ought to be feared.
texts.psa.76.12: He shall cut off the spirit of princes: he is terrible to the kings of the earth.
texts.psa.77.1: To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of Asaph. I cried to God with my voice, even to God with my voice; and he gave ear to me.
texts.psa.77.2: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord: my sore ran in the night, and ceased not: my soul refused to be comforted.
texts.psa.77.3: I remembered God, and was troubled: I complained, and my spirit was overwhelmed. Selah.
texts.psa.77.4: Thou holdest my eyes waking: I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
texts.psa.77.5: I have considered the days of old, the years of ancient times.
texts.psa.77.6: I call to remembrance my song in the night: I commune with my own heart: and my spirit made diligent search.
texts.psa.77.7: Will the Lord cast off for ever? and will he be favorable no more?
texts.psa.77.8: Is his mercy wholly gone for ever? doth his promise fail for evermore?
texts.psa.77.9: Hath God forgotten to be gracious? hath he in anger shut up his tender mercies? Selah.
texts.psa.77.10: And I said, This is my infirmity: but I will remember the years of the right hand of the Most High.
texts.psa.77.11: I will remember the works of the LORD: surely I will remember thy wonders of old.
texts.psa.77.12: I will meditate also of all thy work, and talk of thy doings.
texts.psa.77.13: Thy way, O God, is in the sanctuary: who is so great a God as our God!
texts.psa.77.14: Thou art the God that doest wonders: thou hast declared thy strength among the people.
texts.psa.77.15: Thou hast with thy arm redeemed thy people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
texts.psa.77.16: The waters saw thee, O God, the waters saw thee; they were afraid: the depths also were disturbed.
texts.psa.77.17: The clouds poured out water: the skies sent out a sound: thy arrows also went abroad.
texts.psa.77.18: The voice of thy thunder was in the heaven: the lightnings lightened the world: the earth trembled and shook.
texts.psa.77.19: Thy way is in the sea, and thy path in the great waters, and thy footsteps are not known.
texts.psa.77.20: Thou leddest thy people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
texts.psa.78.1: Maschil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my law: incline your ear to the words of my mouth.
texts.psa.78.2: I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old:
texts.psa.78.3: Which we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us.
texts.psa.78.4: We will not hide them from their children, showing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done.
texts.psa.78.5: For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children:
texts.psa.78.6: That the generation to come might know them, even the children who should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children:
texts.psa.78.7: That they might set their hope in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments:
texts.psa.78.8: And might not be as their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not steadfast with God.
texts.psa.78.9: The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle.
texts.psa.78.10: They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law;
texts.psa.78.11: And forgot his works, and his wonders that he had shown them.
texts.psa.78.12: Marvelous things did he in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.
texts.psa.78.13: He divided the sea, and caused them to pass through; and he made the waters to stand as a heap.
texts.psa.78.14: In the day-time also he led them with a cloud, and all the night with a light of fire.
texts.psa.78.15: He cleaved the rocks in the wilderness, and gave them drink as out of the great depths.
texts.psa.78.16: He brought streams also out of the rock, and caused waters to run down like rivers.
texts.psa.78.17: And they sinned yet more against him by provoking the Most High in the wilderness.
texts.psa.78.18: And they tempted God in their heart by asking food for their desire.
texts.psa.78.19: Yes, they spoke against God; they said, Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?
texts.psa.78.20: Behold, he smote the rock, that the waters gushed out, and the streams overflowed; can he give bread also? can he provide flesh for his people?
texts.psa.78.21: Therefore the LORD heard this, and was wroth: so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger also came up against Israel;
texts.psa.78.22: Because they believed not in God, and trusted not in his salvation:
texts.psa.78.23: Though he had commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven,
texts.psa.78.24: And had rained down manna upon them to eat, and had given them of the corn of heaven.
texts.psa.78.25: Man ate angels' food: he sent them food to the full.
texts.psa.78.26: He caused an east wind to blow in the heaven: and by his power he brought in the south wind.
texts.psa.78.27: He rained flesh also upon them as dust, and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea:
texts.psa.78.28: And he let it fall in the midst of their camp, around their habitations.
texts.psa.78.29: So they ate, and were well filled: for he gave them their own desire;
texts.psa.78.30: They were not estranged from their desire: but while their meat was yet in their mouths,
texts.psa.78.31: The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel.
texts.psa.78.32: For all this they sinned still, and believed not for his wondrous works.
texts.psa.78.33: Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, and their years in trouble.
texts.psa.78.34: When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned and inquired early after God.
texts.psa.78.35: And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their redeemer.
texts.psa.78.36: Nevertheless they flattered him with their mouth, and they lied to him with their tongues.
texts.psa.78.37: For their heart was not right with him, neither were they steadfast in his covenant.
texts.psa.78.38: But he, being full of compassion, forgave their iniquity, and destroyed them not: yes, many a time he turned his anger away, and did not stir up all his wrath.
