texts.psa.31.10: For, consumed with sorrow, is my life, and my years with sighing,—My strength hath staggered with my humiliation, and, my bones, are without marrow.
texts.psa.31.11: By reason of all mine adversaries, have I become a reproach. Even to my neighbours, altogether, and a dread to mine acquaintance,—They who have seen me abroad, have fled from me:
texts.psa.31.12: I have been forgotten, like one dead—out of mind, I have been as a missing vessel.
texts.psa.31.13: For I have heard the whispering of many—A terror round about! When they have sat in conclave together against me, to take away my life, have they intrigued.
texts.psa.31.14: I, therefore. in thee, have put my trust, O Yahweh, I have said, My God, thou art!
texts.psa.31.15: In thy hand, are my times, Rescue me from the hand of my foes and from my pursuers!
texts.psa.31.16: Cause thy face to shine upon thy servant, Save me in thy lovingkindness.
texts.psa.31.17: O Yahweh! let me not be ashamed, For I have called upon thee, Let the lawless be ashamed, Go down in silence to hades!
texts.psa.31.18: Let false lips be made dumb,—which are speaking—against a righteous one—arrogantly, with pride and contempt.
texts.psa.31.19: How great is thy goodness, which thou hast hidden away for them who revere thee,—Thou hast wrought for them who seek refuge in thee, in sight of the sons of men.
texts.psa.31.20: Thou wilt conceal them, in the secrecy of thine own presence, from the conspiracies of men,—Thou wilt hide them in a pavilion, from the strife of tongues.
texts.psa.31.21: Blessed be Yahweh, for he hath made wonderful his lovingkindness for me, in a fortified city.
texts.psa.31.22: But, I, had said in mine alarm, I am cut off from before thine eyes,—But, indeed, thou didst hear the voice of my supplication, when I cried for help unto thee.
texts.psa.31.23: Love Yahweh, all ye his men of lovingkindness,—Faithfulness, doth Yahweh observe, but repayeth abundantly him that worketh proudly.
texts.psa.31.24: Be strong, and let your heart be bold, all ye who are waiting for Yahweh.
texts.psa.32.1: How happy is he whose transgression is forgiven! whose sin is pardoned!
texts.psa.32.2: How happy the son of earth, to whom Yahweh will not reckon iniquity! and in whose spirit is no guile!
texts.psa.32.3: When I kept silence, my bones became worn out, Through my groaning all the day;
texts.psa.32.4: For, day and night, heavy upon me, was thy hand,—Changed was my life-sap into the drought of summer. [Selah.]
texts.psa.32.5: My sin, would I own unto thee, and, mine iniquity, not hide, I said, I will confess my transgressions unto Yahweh, And, thou, didst forgive the iniquity of my sin. [Selah.]
texts.psa.32.6: For this cause, will every man of lovingkindness pray unto thee, in time to obtain,—Surely, in the overflow of many waters, unto him, shall they not reach.
texts.psa.32.7: Thou, art a hiding-place for me, From distress, wilt thou preserve me,—With shouts of deliverance, wilt thou compass me about. [Selah.]
texts.psa.32.8: I will make thee discreet, I will point out to thee the way which thou must go, I will fix upon thee mine eye.
texts.psa.32.9: Do not ye become like a horse, like a mule, without discernment,—With the bit and bridle of his mouth, [hast thou] to restrain him,—He will not come near unto thee.
texts.psa.32.10: Many pains, hath the lawless one,—But, he that trusteth in Yahweh, Lovingkindness, shall compass him about.
texts.psa.32.11: Rejoice in Yahweh and exult, O ye righteous, Yea, shout in triumph, all ye upright in heart!
texts.psa.33.1: Shout for joy, ye righteous, in Yahweh, To the upright, seemly is praise.
texts.psa.33.2: Give ye thanks unto Yahweh with the lyre, With a harp of ten strings, make ye music unto him.
texts.psa.33.3: Sing unto him, a song that is new, With skill, sweep the strings, with loud noise.
texts.psa.33.4: For right is the word of Yahweh, and, all his work, is in faithfulness:
texts.psa.33.5: Who loveth righteousness and justice, With the lovingkindness of Yahweh, the earth is full.
texts.psa.33.6: By the word of Yahweh, the heavens were made, and, by the spirit of his mouth, all their host:
texts.psa.33.7: Who gathered as into a skin-bottle the waters of the sea, Delivering, into treasuries, the roaring deeps.
texts.psa.33.8: Let all the earth, stand in awe of Yahweh, Of him, be in dread, all ye inhabitants of the world;
texts.psa.33.9: For, he, spake, and it was, He, commanded, and it stood forth.
texts.psa.33.10: Yahweh, hath frustrated the counsel of nations, hath brought to nothing the devices of peoples.
texts.psa.33.11: The counsel of Yahweh, to times age-abiding, shall stand, The devices of his heart, from generation to generation.
texts.psa.33.12: How happy the nation whose God is, Yahweh, The people he hath chosen as his own inheritance!
texts.psa.33.13: Out of the heavens, hath Yahweh looked, He hath seen all the sons of men:
texts.psa.33.14: Out of his settled place of abode, hath he fixed his gaze on all the inhabitants of the earth:
texts.psa.33.15: Who fashioneth their heart all together, Who understandeth all their doings.
texts.psa.33.16: Not a king, can be saved by greatness of force, nor, hero, deliver himself by greatness of strength:
texts.psa.33.17: A deception, is the horse, for victory, and, by his great strength, shall he not deliver.
texts.psa.33.18: Lo! the eye of Yahweh, is toward them who revere him, unto such as are waiting for his lovingkindness:
texts.psa.33.19: To rescue, from death, their soul, and to keep them alive in famine.
texts.psa.33.20: Our own soul, hath waited for Yahweh, Our help and our shield, is he!
texts.psa.33.21: For, in him, shall our heart rejoice, For, in his holy Name, have we trusted.
texts.psa.33.22: Be thy lovingkindness, O Yahweh, upon us, According as we have waited for thee.
texts.psa.34.1: Let me bless Yahweh at all times, Continually be his praise in my mouth.
texts.psa.34.2: In Yahweh, boasteth my soul, The patient oppressed-ones shall hear and be glad.
texts.psa.34.3: Ascribe ye greatness unto Yahweh with me, and let us exalt his Name together.
texts.psa.34.4: I enquired of Yahweh, and he hath answered me, And, out of all my terrors, hath he rescued me.
texts.psa.34.5: They looked unto him and were radiant, And, as for their faces, let them not be abashed.
texts.psa.34.6: This, oppressed one cried, and, Yahweh, heard—and, out of all his distresses, saved him.
texts.psa.34.7: The messenger of Yahweh encampeth around them who revere him, Thus hath he delivered them.
texts.psa.34.8: Oh taste and see, that good is Yahweh,—How happy the man who seeketh refuge in him!
texts.psa.34.9: Revere Yahweh, ye his holy ones, For there is no want to them who revere him.
texts.psa.34.10: Young lions, have come short, and suffered hunger, but, they who seek Yahweh, shall not lack any good thing.
texts.psa.34.11: Come, ye children! hearken unto me, The reverence of Yahweh, will I teach you.
texts.psa.34.12: Who is the man that desireth life, Loving days, that he may see good?
texts.psa.34.13: Keep thy tongue from wickedness, And thy lips from speaking deceit:
texts.psa.34.14: Depart from wickedness and do good, Aim at well-being, and pursue it.
texts.psa.34.15: The eyes of Yahweh, are towards the righteous, And, his ears, towards their cry for help:
texts.psa.34.16: the face of Yahweh, is against such as do wickedness, To cut off, from the earth, their memory.
texts.psa.34.17: They made outcry, and Yahweh heard, And, out of all their straits, hath he rescued them.
texts.psa.34.18: Near is Yahweh, to the broken in heart, And, the crushed in spirit, will he save.
texts.psa.34.19: Many are the misfortunes of the righteous, But, out of them all, doth Yahweh rescue him.
texts.psa.34.20: Keeping all his bones, Not, one from among them, is broken.
texts.psa.34.21: Misfortune shall be the death of the lawless one, And, the haters of the righteous man, shall be held guilty.
texts.psa.34.22: Yahweh ransometh the soul of his servants, And none shall be held guilty, who seek refuge in him.
texts.psa.35.1: Contend, O Yahweh, with them who contend with me, Make war upon them who make war upon me.
texts.psa.35.2: Grasp buckler and shield, and arise in my help;
texts.psa.35.3: Then draw the spear, and close up against my pursuers, Say to my soul, Thy salvation, I am!
texts.psa.35.4: Let them be ashamed and confounded, who are seeking my life,—Let them turn back and be put to the blush, who are devising my hurt:
texts.psa.35.5: Let them be as chaff before the wind, with, the messenger of Yahweh, pressing them on:
texts.psa.35.6: Let their way become dark and slippery, with, the messenger of Yahweh, pursuing them.
texts.psa.35.7: For, without cause, have they hid for me, in a ditch, their net,—Without cause, have they digged [a pit] for my life.
texts.psa.35.8: There shall reach him a ruin he could not know,—Yea, his own net which he hath hidden, shall capture him, Into that ruin, shall he fall!
texts.psa.35.9: But, my soul, shall exult in Yahweh,—shall be glad in his salvation.
texts.psa.35.10: All my bones, shall say—O Yahweh, who is like unto thee? Rescuing the oppressed from one stronger than he, Yea the oppressed and the needy, from their spoiler.
texts.psa.35.11: There rise up witnesses helping forward violence and wrong, What I know not, they demand of me:
texts.psa.35.12: They repay me evil for good, Bereaving my soul.
texts.psa.35.13: But, as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth, I humbled, with fasting, my soul, though, my prayer, unto mine own bosom, might return:
texts.psa.35.14: Like as for a friend, like as for a brother of mine own, I walked to and fro, As though mourning for a mother, I gloomily bowed myself down.
texts.psa.35.15: But, in mine overthrow, have they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together,—There gathered themselves together against me foolish men, and I knew it not, They have torn in pieces, and not been silent;
texts.psa.35.16: Amidst profane praters of perversion, have they gnashed upon me with their teeth.
texts.psa.35.17: My Lord! how long wilt thou look on? Bring back my soul out of their raging, from among lions, my solitary self.
texts.psa.35.18: I will thank thee, in the midst of a great convocation,—In the midst of a mighty people, will I praise thee.
texts.psa.35.19: Let not them who are falsely my foes rejoice over me, As for them who hate me without cause, let them not wink the eye!
texts.psa.35.20: For, no salvation, will they utter,—But, against the quiet of the land, deceitful things, do they devise;
texts.psa.35.21: Yea they have opened wide against me their mouth, They have said, Aha! Aha! our own eye, hath seen!
texts.psa.35.22: Thou hast seen, O Yahweh, do not keep silence! O My Lord! be not far from me:
texts.psa.35.23: Bestir thyself and wake up, to my vindication, O my God and My Lord!—to my plea:
texts.psa.35.24: Vindicate me according to thy righteousness, O Yahweh, my God! And let them not rejoice over me:
texts.psa.35.25: Let them not say in their heart, Aha! to our mind! Let them not say, We have swallowed him up!
texts.psa.35.26: Let them turn pale, and then at once blush, who are rejoicing at my misfortune,—Let them be clothed with shame and confusion, who are magnifying themselves against me.
texts.psa.35.27: Let them shout in triumph and rejoice, who are desiring my justification; And let them say continually, Yahweh be magnified, Who hath taken pleasure in the prosperity of his servant.
texts.psa.35.28: Mine own tongue also, shall softly utter thy righteousness,—All the day long,—thy praise!
texts.psa.36.1: Declareth the transgression of the lawless one, within my heart, There is, no dread of God, before his eyes;
texts.psa.36.2: For he flattereth himself [too much] in his own eyes, to find his iniquity—to hate [it].
texts.psa.36.3: The words of his mouth, are iniquity and deceit, he hath left off to show discretion by doing well:
texts.psa.36.4: Iniquity, deviseth he upon his bed,—he taketh his stand in a way, not good, Wrong, doth he not abhor!
texts.psa.36.5: O Yahweh! in the heavens, is thy lovingkindness, Thy faithfulness, as far as the fleecy clouds:
texts.psa.36.6: Thy righteousness, is like mighty mountains, and, thy just decrees, are a great resounding deep,—Man and beast, thou savest, O Yahweh!
texts.psa.36.7: How precious thy lovingkindness, O God,—Therefore, the sons of men, under the shadow of thy wings, seek refuge:
texts.psa.36.8: They abundantly relish the fatness of thy house,—And out of the full stream of thine own pleasures, thou givest them to drink.
texts.psa.36.9: For, with thee, is the fountain of life, In thy light, we see light.
texts.psa.36.10: Prolong thy lovingkindness unto them who know thee,—and thy righteousness, to the upright in heart.
texts.psa.36.11: Let not the foot of pride reach me, nor, the hand of the lawless, scare me away.
texts.psa.36.12: There did the workers of iniquity fall,—thrust down and not able to rise!
texts.psa.37.1: Burn not with vexation because of evil-doers, Be not envious of the workers of perversity;
texts.psa.37.2: For, like grass, soon shall they wither, and, like green herbage, shall they fade.
texts.psa.37.3: Trust in Yahweh, and do good, Dwell in the land, and feed on fidelity;
texts.psa.37.4: Yea, rest thy delight on Yahweh, that he may give thee the requests of thy heart.
texts.psa.37.5: Roll on Yahweh thy way, Trust also in him, and, he, will effectually work:
texts.psa.37.6: So will he bring forth, as the light, thy righteousness, and thy vindication as the noonday.
texts.psa.37.7: Be resigned to Yahweh, yea wait with longing for him; Burn not with vexation at him who prospereth in his way,—at the man who doeth wickedness.
texts.psa.37.8: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath, Burn not with vexation—[it would be] only to do evil;
texts.psa.37.9: For, evil doers, shall be cut off, but, as for them who wait for Yahweh, they, shall inherit the earth.
texts.psa.37.10: Yet a little, therefore, and the lawless one shall not be, Yea thou shalt look about, over his place—and he shall have vanished!
texts.psa.37.11: But, the patient oppressed-ones, shall inherit the earth, and shall delight themselves over the abundance of prosperity.
texts.psa.37.12: Plotting is the lawless one, against the just, and gnashing upon him with his teeth.
texts.psa.37.13: My Lord, shall laugh at him, for he seeth, that his day, will come.
texts.psa.37.14: A sword, have the lawless, drawn out, and have trodden their bow,—To bring down the oppressed and the needy, To slaughter the upright in life:
texts.psa.37.15: Their sword, shall enter into their own heart, and, their bow, shall be broken.
texts.psa.37.16: Better the little of the righteous man, than the abundance of the lawless who are mighty;
texts.psa.37.17: For, the arms of the lawless, shall be broken, But Yahweh is upholding the righteous.
texts.psa.37.18: Yahweh knoweth the days of the blameless, that, their inheritance, unto times age-abiding, shall continue.
texts.psa.37.19: They shall not be ashamed in the time of calamity, and, in the days of famine, shall they be filled.
texts.psa.37.20: For, the lawless, shall perish, and, the foes of Yahweh, be like the glory of the meadows, They have vanished! In smoke, have they vanished!
texts.psa.37.21: A lawless man borroweth, and will not repay, But, a righteous man, showeth favour and giveth;
texts.psa.37.22: For, such as are blessed of him, shall inherit the earth, But, the cursed of him, shall be cut off.
texts.psa.37.23: From Yahweh, are the steps of a man made firm, When, with his way, he is well pleased:
texts.psa.37.24: Though he fall, he shall not be hurled headlong, For, Yahweh, is holding his hand.
texts.psa.37.25: Young, have I been, moreover am old,—Yet have I not seen, A righteous man forsaken, Nor his seed begging bread:
texts.psa.37.26: All day long, is he showing favour and lending, his seed, therefore, shall have a blessing.
texts.psa.37.27: Turn from evil, and do good, and so settle down, unto times age-abiding.
texts.psa.37.28: For, Yahweh, loveth justice, and will not forsake his men of lovingkindness, Unto times age-abiding, have the perverse been destroyed,—and the seed of the lawless, been cut off.
texts.psa.37.29: The righteous, shall inherit the earth, that they may settle down, to futurity, thereupon.
texts.psa.37.30: The mouth of a righteous man, softly uttereth wisdom, and, his tongue, speaketh justice:
texts.psa.37.31: The law of his God, is in his heart, his steps shall not swerve.
texts.psa.37.32: The lawless man, lieth in wait, for the just, and seeketh to put him to death:
texts.psa.37.33: Yahweh, will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him, when he is judged.
texts.psa.37.34: Wait for Yahweh, and observe thou his path, that he may exalt thee, to inherit the earth, On the cutting off of the lawless, shalt thou look.
texts.psa.37.35: I have seen a lawless man, a tyrant, and spreading himself out, like a cedar in Lebanon;
texts.psa.37.36: Then I passed by, and lo! he had vanished! Yea I sought him, but he could not be found.
texts.psa.37.37: Mark the blameless man, and behold the upright, for there is a hereafter for the man of peace;
texts.psa.37.38: But, transgressors, are to be destroyed together, the hereafter of lawless men, is to be cut off.
texts.psa.37.39: But, the deliverance of the righteous, is from Yahweh, their refuge in a time of distress.
texts.psa.37.40: Thus hath Yahweh helped them, thus hath he delivered them,—He will deliver them from the lawless, and will save them, because they have sought refuge in him.
texts.psa.38.1: O Yahweh, do not, in thine anger, correct me, nor, in thy wrath, chastise me;
texts.psa.38.2: For, thine arrows, have sunk down into me, and thy hand, presseth heavily upon me.
texts.psa.38.3: There is no soundness in my flesh, By reason of thine indignation, There is no peace in my bones, By reason of my sin;
texts.psa.38.4: For, mine iniquities, have passed over my head, Like a heavy burden, they are too heavy for me:
texts.psa.38.5: My wounds are of bad odour—they have festered, by reason of my folly:
texts.psa.38.6: I am bent, I am bowed down very low. All the day, have I gloomily walked;
texts.psa.38.7: For, my loins, are filled with inflammation, and there is no soundness in my flesh:
texts.psa.38.8: I am benumbed and crushed exceedingly,—I have cried aloud because of the groaning of my heart.
texts.psa.38.9: O My Lord! before thee, is all my longing, and, my sighing, from thee, hath not been hid:
texts.psa.38.10: My heart, fluttereth, my strength hath forsaken me, and, as for the light of mine eyes, even they, are not with me:
texts.psa.38.11: My lovers, and my friends, from before my stroke, stand aloof,—and, my near ones, far away, do stand:
texts.psa.38.12: Yea they who are seeking my life, have laid snares, and they who are asking my harm, have threatened engulfing ruin, And, deceitful things—all day long, do they mutter.
texts.psa.38.13: But, I, as one deaf, will not hear,—and as one dumb, who will not open his mouth:
texts.psa.38.14: Thus have I become as a man who cannot hear, in whose mouth are no arguments:
texts.psa.38.15: Because, for thee, O Yahweh, have I waited, Thou, wilt answer, O Adonay, my God!
texts.psa.38.16: For I said, Lest they rejoice over me! When my feet were tottering, against me, have they magnified themselves:
texts.psa.38.17: For, I, to halt, am ready, and, my pain, is before me continually;
texts.psa.38.18: For, mine iniquity, will I declare, I shall be anxious because of my sin;
texts.psa.38.19: And, my foes, are alive—have become strong,—and multiplied are they who hate me for false cause:
texts.psa.38.20: Even they who are repaying evil for good, accuse me because I pursue the good.
texts.psa.38.21: Do not forsake me, O Yahweh, My God! be not far from me:
texts.psa.38.22: Make haste to help me, My Lord, my deliverance!
texts.psa.39.1: I said, [to myself,] I will take heed to my ways, That I sin not with my tongue,—I will put on my mouth a muzzle, So long as the lawless is before me.
texts.psa.39.2: I was dumb with silence, I held my peace, afar from happiness, But, my pain had been stirred:
texts.psa.39.3: Hot was my heart within me, While I was musing, there was kindled a fire, I spake with my tongue!
texts.psa.39.4: Let me know, O Yahweh, mine end, And the measure of my days—what it is, I would know how short-lived I am.
texts.psa.39.5: Lo! as hand-breadths, hast thou granted my days, and my life-time, is as nothing before thee,—Surely, a mere breath, are all men, [even] such as stand firm. [Selah.]
texts.psa.39.6: Surely as a shadow, doth every man wander, Surely in vain, do they bustle about, he heapeth things up, and knoweth not who shall gather them in.
texts.psa.39.7: Now, therefore, for what have I waited, O My Lord? My hope, is, in thee.
texts.psa.39.8: From all my transgressions, rescue thou me,—The reproach of the base, oh do not make me!
texts.psa.39.9: I am dumb, I cannot open my mouth, for, thou, hast done it.
texts.psa.39.10: Remove from off me thy stroke, Because of the hostility of thy hand, am, I, consumed.
texts.psa.39.11: When, by rebukes for iniquity, thou hast corrected a man, Then hast thou consumed, as a moth, all that was delightful within him, Surely, a breath, are all men. [Selah.]
texts.psa.39.12: Hear my prayer, O Yahweh, And, unto my cry for help, give ear, At my tears, do not be silent,—For, a sojourner, am, I, with thee, A stranger, like all my fathers.
texts.psa.39.13: Look away from me that I may brighten up, Ere yet I depart and am no more.
texts.psa.40.1: I waited patiently for Yahweh,—And he inclined, unto me, and heard my cry for help;
texts.psa.40.2: So he brought me up, Out of the destroying pit, Out of the swampy mire,—And set, upon a cliff, my feet, Making firm my steps:
texts.psa.40.3: Then put he, into my mouth, a new song, Praise to our God,—Many shall see and revere, And shall trust in Yahweh.
texts.psa.40.4: How happy the man, Who hath made Yahweh his confidence, who hath not turned unto the haughty, nor gone aside unto falsehood.
texts.psa.40.5: Mighty things, hast thou done—Thou, Yahweh my God, Thy wonderful doings and thy purposes towards us, There is no setting them in order unto thee—I would tell, and would speak!—They are too great to rehearse.
texts.psa.40.6: Sacrifice and meal-offering, thou didst not delight in, Ears, didst thou pierce for me,—Ascending-sacrifice and sin-bearer, thou didst not ask:
texts.psa.40.7: Then, said I—Lo! I am come, In the written scroll, is it prescribed for me;
texts.psa.40.8: To do thy good-pleasure, O my God, is my delight, And, thy law, is in the midst of mine inward parts:
texts.psa.40.9: I have told the good-tidings of righteousness in a great convocation, Lo! my lips, do I not restrain, O Yahweh, thou, knowest:
texts.psa.40.10: Thy righteousness, have I not hid in the midst of my heart, Thy faithfulness and thy salvation, have I spoken, I have not concealed thy lovingkindness and thy truthfulness from the great convocation.
texts.psa.40.11: Thou, O Yahweh, wilt not restrain thy compassions from me, Thy lovingkindness and thy truthfulness, shall continually watch over me.
texts.psa.40.12: For there have closed in upon me, misfortunes beyond number, Mine iniquities have overtaken me, and I cannot see, They have become more than the hairs of my head, And, my courage, hath forsaken me!
texts.psa.40.13: Be pleased, O Yahweh, to rescue me, O Yahweh! to help me, make haste!
texts.psa.40.14: Let them turn pale and then at once blush, who are seeking my life to snatch it away,—Let them draw back, and be confounded, who are taking pleasure in my calamity;
texts.psa.40.15: Let them be astonished on account of their own shame, who are saying of me, Aha! Aha!
texts.psa.40.16: Let all them be glad and rejoice in thee, who are seekers of thee. Let them say continually—Yahweh be magnified! who are lovers of thy salvation.
texts.psa.40.17: But, I, being oppressed and needy, May My Lord devise for me,—My help and my deliverer, thou art! O my God, do not tarry!
texts.psa.41.1: How happy is he that is attentive to the poor, In the day of calamity, will Yahweh deliver him:
texts.psa.41.2: Yahweh, will preserve him and keep him alive, And he shall be pronounced happy in the land, Do not then give him up at the desire of his enemies!
texts.psa.41.3: Yahweh, will sustain him upon the bed of sickness, All his couch, hast thou transformed in his disease.
texts.psa.41.4: I, said—O Yahweh, show me favour, heal thou my soul, for I have sinned against thee:
texts.psa.41.5: Mine enemies, speak ill of me, When will he die, and his name perish?
texts.psa.41.6: And, if he have come to see me, Falsehood, doth he speak, His own heart, gathereth iniquity to itself, he goeth forth, abroad he telleth it.
texts.psa.41.7: Together—against me, do all who hate me whisper among themselves, Against me, devise they hurt for me.
texts.psa.41.8: An infliction of the Abandoned One hath been fixed upon him, and, now that he hath lien down, he will not again rise.
texts.psa.41.9: Even the man whom I used to salute, in whom I put confidence, who used to eat my bread,—hath magnified his heel against me!
texts.psa.41.10: But, thou, O Yahweh, show me favour and raise me up, That I may repay them.
texts.psa.41.11: Hereby, do I know that thou delightest in me, In that mine enemy shall not raise a shout over me.
texts.psa.41.12: But, as for me, In my blamelessness, hast thou held me fast, And hast caused me to stand before thee unto times age-abiding.
texts.psa.41.13: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, From the age that is past, even unto the age yet to come: Amen and Amen!
texts.psa.42.1: As, the hart, cometh panting up to the channels of water, So my soul, panteth for thee, O God.
texts.psa.42.2: My soul thirsteth for God, for a GOD who liveth,—When shall I enter in, and see the face of God?
texts.psa.42.3: My tears have been my food day and night, While it hath been said unto me all the day, Where is thy God?
texts.psa.42.4: These things, I keep calling to mind, and pouring out, over me, my own soul, For I used to cross over with a crowd, Lead them in procession up to the house of God, With the voice of shouting and praise.—a throng keeping festival.
texts.psa.42.5: Why shouldst thou be cast down, O my soul? And [why] shouldst thou moan over me? Wait thou for God, for yet shall I praise him, As the triumph of my presence.
texts.psa.42.6: My God! over myself, my soul is cast down,—For this cause, will I remember thee from the land of Jordan, And the Hermons, from the hill Mizar.
texts.psa.42.7: Roaring deep unto roaring deep, is calling, at the voice of thy cataracts, All thy breakers and thy rolling waves, over me, have passed.
texts.psa.42.8: By day, will Yahweh command his lovingkindness, And, in the night, shall His song be with me, My prayer be to the GOD of my life.
texts.psa.42.9: I will say onto GOD,—my rock, Wherefore hast thou forgotten me? Wherefore in gloom should I go, because of oppression by the enemy?
texts.psa.42.10: With a crushing of my bones, have my adversaries reproached me,—While they keep saying unto me all the day, Where is thy God?
texts.psa.42.11: Why shouldst thou be sat down, O my soul? And why shouldst thou moan over me? Wait thou for God, for yet shall I praise him, As the triumph of my presence and my God.
texts.psa.43.1: Vindicate me, O God, and plead my cause, Against a nation, without lovingkindness, From the man of deceit and perversity, wilt thou deliver me?
texts.psa.43.2: For, thou, art my defending God—Wherefore hast thou rejected me? Wherefore in gloom should I wander, because of the oppression of an enemy?
texts.psa.43.3: Send forth thy light and thy faithfulness, Let, them, lead me, Let them bring me into thy holy mountain, and into thy habitations:
texts.psa.43.4: That I may go in unto the altar of God, Unto GOD, mine exultant joy,—That I may praise thee with the lyre, O God—mine own God!
texts.psa.43.5: Why shouldst thou be cast down, O my soul? And why shouldst thou moan over me, Wait thou for God, for yet shall I praise him, As the triumph of my presence, and my God.
texts.psa.44.1: O God! with our own ears, have we heard, Our fathers, have recounted to us,—The work thou didst work, In their day, In the days of aforetime:
texts.psa.44.2: Thou thyself, with thine own hand—Didst dispossess, nations, and didst plant them, Didst break peoples in pieces, and didst spread them out:
texts.psa.44.3: For, not by their own sword, gat they possession of the land, Nor did, their own arm, win victory for them,—But thine own right hand, and thine own arm, and the light of thy face, Because thou hadst accepted them.
texts.psa.44.4: Thou thyself, art my king, O God, Command thou the victories of Jacob.
texts.psa.44.5: By thee, will we thrust at, our adversaries, In thy Name, will we tread down our assailants;
texts.psa.44.6: For, not in my bow, will I trust, Nor shall, my sword, give me victory;
texts.psa.44.7: For thou hast saved us from our adversaries, And, them who hated us, hast thou put to shame.
texts.psa.44.8: In God, have we boasted all the day, And, thy Name—unto times age-abiding, will we praise. [Selah.]
texts.psa.44.9: But nay thou hast rejected, and confounded us, And wilt not go forth with our hosts;
texts.psa.44.10: Thou sufferest us to turn back from the adversary, And, they who hate us, have plundered at will:
texts.psa.44.11: Thou dost give us up like sheep to be devoured, And, amongst the nations, hast thou scattered us.
texts.psa.44.12: Thou dost sell thy people for, no-value, And hast not made increase by their price.
texts.psa.44.13: Thou dost make us, A reproach to our neighbours, A mockery and a derision to them who are round about us:
texts.psa.44.14: Thou dost make us, A by-word among the nations,—A shaking of the head among the peoples.
texts.psa.44.15: All the day, is my confusion before me, And, the shame of my face, hath covered me:
texts.psa.44.16: At the voice of him who reproacheth and revileth, At the face of the foe and avenger.
texts.psa.44.17: All this, hath come upon us, Yet had we not forgotten thee, Neither had we dealt falsely with thy covenant;
texts.psa.44.18: Our heart had not drawn back, Nor had our goings swerved from thy path;
texts.psa.44.19: That thou shouldst have crushed us down in the place of wild dogs, And covered us over with a deadly shadow.
texts.psa.44.20: If we had forgotten the Name of our God, And had spread forth our hands unto the GOD of the foreigner,
texts.psa.44.21: Would not, God, have searched into this, Seeing that, he, knoweth the secrets of the heart?
texts.psa.44.22: Surely, for thy sake, have we been slain all the day, We have been accounted as sheep for slaughter.
texts.psa.44.23: Awake thou! wherefore shouldst thou sleep, O Lord? Bestir thee! do not reject us altogether!
texts.psa.44.24: Wherefore shouldst thou hide, thy face? Shouldst forget our humiliation and our oppression?
texts.psa.44.25: For our soul, sinketh down to the dust, Our body, cleaveth to the earth.
texts.psa.44.26: Arise to our help, And ransom us, because of thine own lovingkindness.
texts.psa.45.1: Overflowed hath my heart, with an excellent theme, I will recite my poem concerning the king, Be, my tongue, [like] the pen of a scribe who is skilled.
texts.psa.45.2: Most beautiful thou art, beyond the sons of men, Graciousness hath been poured forth by thy lips, For this cause, hath God blessed thee, to times age-abiding.
texts.psa.45.3: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O mighty one, [’Tis] thine honour and thy majesty;
texts.psa.45.4: And, [in] thy majesty, be successful! ride forth! on behalf of faithfulness, and humility—righteousness, And let thine own right hand show thee wonderful things.
texts.psa.45.5: Thine arrows, are sharp—Peoples, under thee, fall! In the heart of the foes of the king.
texts.psa.45.6: Thy throne, O God, is to times age-abiding and beyond, A sceptre of equity, is the sceptre of thy kingdom.
texts.psa.45.7: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated lawlessness,—For this cause, hath God, thine own God, anointed thee, With the oil of gladness, beyond thy partners.
texts.psa.45.8: Myrrh and aloes, cassias, all thy garments,—Out of the palaces of ivory, the tones of strings, have rejoiced thee.
texts.psa.45.9: Daughters of kings, are among thine honourable women, Stationed is the bride at thy right hand, in gold of Ophir.
texts.psa.45.10: Hearken, O daughter, and observe, Incline also thine ear, Forget, then, thine own people, And the house of thy father;
texts.psa.45.11: When the king shall desire thy beauty, Surely, he, is thy lord, then bow down to him.
texts.psa.45.12: Also, the daughter of Tyre, [cometh in] with a present! Thy face, shall the rich of the people appease.
texts.psa.45.13: All glorious—the daughter of a king [sitteth] within, Brocades, wrought with gold, [are] her clothing!
texts.psa.45.14: In embroidered raiment, shall she be brought unto the king—The virgins that follow her, her companions, are to be conducted unto thee:
texts.psa.45.15: They shall be brought, with rejoicings and exultation,—They shall enter into the palace of the king!
texts.psa.45.16: Instead of thy fathers, be thy sons, Thou shalt make them rulers in all the earth.
texts.psa.45.17: I will keep in remembrance thy Name, through each succeeding generation, For this cause, peoples, shall praise thee, to times age-abiding and beyond.
texts.psa.46.1: God—for us, is a refuge and strength, A help in distresses, soon found.
texts.psa.46.2: For this cause, will we not fear, Though the earth showeth change, Or the mountains slip into the heart of the seas:
texts.psa.46.3: The waters thereof roar and foam, The mountains tremble with the swelling thereof [Selah.]
texts.psa.46.4: A river! whose channels, shall gladden the city of God, The Most High, hath hallowed his habitation.
texts.psa.46.5: God, is in the midst of her, she shall not be shaken, God will help her, by the turnings of the morning.
texts.psa.46.6: Nations have roared, Kingdoms have tottered, He hath uttered his voice, Earth melteth.
texts.psa.46.7: Yahweh of hosts, is with us, A high tower for us, is the God of Jacob. [Selah.]
texts.psa.46.8: Come! view the doings of Yahweh,—Who hath set desolations in the earth;
texts.psa.46.9: Causing wars to cease unto the end of the earth,—The bow, he shivereth, And breaketh in pieces the spear, war-chariots, burneth he up with fire.
texts.psa.46.10: Let be! and know that, I, am God, I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.
texts.psa.46.11: Yahweh of hosts, is with us, A high tower for us, is the God of Jacob. [Selah.]
texts.psa.47.1: All ye peoples, clap your hands, Shout unto God, with the voice of triumph;
texts.psa.47.2: For, Yahweh—as Most High, is to be revered, A great king, over all the earth,
texts.psa.47.3: He will subjugate, Peoples under us, and, Tribes of men beneath our feet.
texts.psa.47.4: He chooseth for us our inheritance, The excellence of Jacob, which he hath loved. [Selah.]
texts.psa.47.5: God hath ascended with a shout, Yahweh, with the sound of a horn.
texts.psa.47.6: Sing praises unto God, sing praises, Sing praises to our King, sing praises;
texts.psa.47.7: For God is king of all the earth, Sing praises with understanding.
texts.psa.47.8: God, hath become king, over the nations, God, hath taken his seat upon his holy throne.
texts.psa.47.9: The willing-hearted of the peoples, have gathered themselves together, The people of the God of Abraham; For, to God, belong the shields of the earth, Greatly is he exalted.
texts.psa.48.1: Great is Yahweh, and worthy to be mightily praised, In the city of our God, His holy mountain.
texts.psa.48.2: Beautiful in elevation, the joy of all the land, Is Mount Zion, in the recesses of the north,—The city of a great king.
texts.psa.48.3: God, in her palaces, is to be known as a high tower.
texts.psa.48.4: For lo! Kings—Met as appointed, Passed by together;
texts.psa.48.5: They themselves, saw, So, were they amazed, Dismayed—they hurried way!
texts.psa.48.6: Trembling, seized them, there, Pangs. like hers who is in travail.
texts.psa.48.7: With an east wind, wilt thou shatter the ships of Tarshish.
texts.psa.48.8: Just as we have heard, So, have we seen, In the city of Yahweh of hosts, In the city of our God, God himself, will establish her, unto times age-abiding. [Selah.]
texts.psa.48.9: We have thought, O God, upon thy lovingkindness, In the midst of thy temple:
texts.psa.48.10: According to thy Name, O God, So, be thy praise, unto the ends of the earth, With righteousness, is, thy right hand, filled.
texts.psa.48.11: Let Mount Zion rejoice, Let the daughters of Judah exult, Because of thy judgments.
texts.psa.48.12: Go round Zion, and compass her about, Reckon up her towers;
texts.psa.48.13: Apply your mind to her rampart, Pass between her palaces, That ye may recount them to an after generation;
texts.psa.48.14: For, this God, is our God, to times age-abiding and beyond, He himself, will conduct us till death.
texts.psa.49.1: Hear ye, this all ye peoples, Give ear, all ye inhabitants of this passing world;
texts.psa.49.2: Both sons of the low, And sons of the high,—Together both rich and needy:—
texts.psa.49.3: My mouth, shall speak forth Wisdom, And the soft utterance of my heart be Understanding:
texts.psa.49.4: I will bend, to a by-word, mine ear, I will open, on the lyre, mine enigma.
texts.psa.49.5: Wherefore should I fear in the days of calamity, Though the iniquity of them who lie in wait for me should enclose me?
texts.psa.49.6: As for them who are trusting in their wealth,—And, in the abundance of their riches, do boast themselves,
texts.psa.49.7: A brother, can none of them, redeem, he cannot give unto God a ransom for himself:
texts.psa.49.8: So costly, is the redemption of their soul, That it faileth unto times age-abiding;
texts.psa.49.9: That he should, yet, live on, continually, Should not see corruption.
texts.psa.49.10: For it is seen that, the wise, die, Together with the dullard, and the brutish, do they perish, And leave, to others, their wealth:
texts.psa.49.11: Their, inward thought, is that their houses are for times age-abiding, Their habitations, for generation after generation,—They give their own names unto lands!
texts.psa.49.12: But, a son of earth, though wealthy, cannot tarry, He hath made himself a by-word—Beasts, they resemble:
texts.psa.49.13: This, their way, is a folly to them, And yet, their followers, with their mouth, approve. [Selah.]
texts.psa.49.14: Like sheep—into hades, are they driven, Death shall shepherd them,—And the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning, Even their form, is to decay, Hades, is all that remaineth of a habitation for him.
texts.psa.49.15: But, God, will redeem my soul, out of the hand of hades, For he will take me. [Selah.]
texts.psa.49.16: Do not fear, When a man becometh rich, When the glory of his house increaseth;
texts.psa.49.17: For, when he dieth, he shall take, nothing, his glory shall not descend after him;
texts.psa.49.18: For, though, his own self—while he lived, he used to bless, And they will praise thee, when thou doest well to thyself,
texts.psa.49.19: He shall enter as far as the circle of his fathers, Nevermore, shall they see the light.
texts.psa.49.20: A son of earth though wealthy, who discerneth not, Hath made himself a by-word, Beasts, they resemble.
texts.psa.50.1: El, Elohim, Yahweh, hath spoken, and culled the earth, From the rising of the sun, unto the going in thereof:
texts.psa.50.2: Out of Zion the perfection of beauty, God, hath shone forth.
texts.psa.50.3: Let our God come, and let him not keep silence! A fire—before him, shall devour, And, around him, hath it become exceeding tempestuous:
texts.psa.50.4: He calleth, Unto the heavens above, And unto the earth, That he may judge his people.
texts.psa.50.5: Gather yourselves unto me—ye my men of lovingkindness, Who have solemnised my covenant over sacrifice.
texts.psa.50.6: Now have the heavens declared his righteousness, Because, God, is, about to judge. [Selah.]
texts.psa.50.7: Hear, O my people, and I will speak, O Israel, and I will adjure thee, God, thine own God, I am:—
texts.psa.50.8: Not, for thy sacrifices, will I reprove thee, Nor for thine ascending-offerings, before me continually:
texts.psa.50.9: I will not take out of thy house—a bullock, Nor out of thy folds—he-goats;
texts.psa.50.10: For, mine, is every wild-beast of the forest, The cattle on the mountains, in their thousands;
texts.psa.50.11: I know every bird of the mountains, And, the moving things of the plain, are with me:
texts.psa.50.12: If I were hungry, I would not tell thee, For, mine, is the world, and the fulness thereof.
texts.psa.50.13: Will I eat the flesh of mighty oxen? Or, the blood of he-goats, will I drink?
texts.psa.50.14: Sacrifice to God a thankoffering, And pay to the Most High thy vows;
texts.psa.50.15: Call upon me, then, in the day of distress, I will deliver thee, that thou mayest glorify me.
texts.psa.50.16: But, to the lawless one, God saith, What hast, thou, to do, to recount my statutes? Or that thou hast taken up my covenant upon thy mouth?
texts.psa.50.17: Seeing that, thou, hast hated correction, And hast cast my words behind thee;
texts.psa.50.18: If thou sawest a thief, then didst thou run with him,—And, with adulterers, hath been thy chosen life;
texts.psa.50.19: Thy mouth, hast thou thrust into wickedness, And, thy tongue, kept weaving deceit;
texts.psa.50.20: Thou wouldst sit down—Against thine own brother, wouldst thou speak, Against thine own mother’s son, wouldst thou expose a fault:—
texts.psa.50.21: These things, hast thou done, and I have kept silence, Thou thoughtest that I should really be like thyself, I will convict thee, yea I will set [thine offences] in order before thine eyes.
texts.psa.50.22: Understand this, I pray you, ye forgetters of GOD, Lest I tear in pieces, and there be none to deliver:—
texts.psa.50.23: He that sacrificeth a thankoffering, will glorify me,—And will prepare a way by which I may show him the salvation of God.
texts.psa.51.1: Be favorable unto me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness, And, in the multitude of thy compassions, blot out my transgressions;
texts.psa.51.2: Thoroughly wash me from mine iniquity, And, from my sin, make me pure;
texts.psa.51.3: For, my transgressions, do, I, acknowledge, And, my sin, is before me continually:
texts.psa.51.4: Against thee—against thee alone, have I sinned, And, wickedness—in thine eyes, have I done,—That thou mayest, Be justified when thou speakest,—Be clear when thou judgest.
texts.psa.51.5: Lo! in iniquity, was I brought forth, And, in sin, did my mother conceive me.
texts.psa.51.6: Lo! faithfulness, hast thou desired in the inward parts, Yea, in the hidden part, wilt thou cause me to know, wisdom.
texts.psa.51.7: Wilt thou cleanse me from sin with hyssop, That I may be pure? Wilt thou wash me, That I may be whiter, than snow?
texts.psa.51.8: Wilt thou cause me to hear joy and gladness? The bones thou hast crushed would exult.
texts.psa.51.9: Hide thy face from my sins,—And, all mine iniquities, blot out;
texts.psa.51.10: A pure heart, create for me, O God, And, a steadfast spirit, renew within me.
texts.psa.51.11: Do not cast me away from thy presence, And, thy Holy Spirit, do not take from me:
texts.psa.51.12: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, And, with a willing spirit, wilt thou uphold me:—
texts.psa.51.13: I would teach transgressors thy ways, And, sinners, unto thee, should return.
texts.psa.51.14: Rescue me from shed-blood, O God, the God of my salvation, My tongue should shout thy righteousness;
texts.psa.51.15: O My Lord! my lips, wilt thou open, And, my mouth, shall declare thy praise.
texts.psa.51.16: For thou wilt not desire sacrifice—that I should give it, Ascending-offering, will not please:
texts.psa.51.17: The sacrifices of God, are a spirit that is broken,—A heart—broken and crushed, O God, thou wilt not despise.
texts.psa.51.18: Do good, in thy good-pleasure, unto Zion, Wilt thou build the walls of Jerusalem!
texts.psa.51.19: Then, shalt thou desire the sacrifices of righteousness, Ascending-sacrifice and whole burnt-offering, Then, shall ascend upon thine altar, young bulls.
texts.psa.52.1: Why dost thou boast thyself of wickedness, O mighty man? The lovingkindness of GOD, [lasteth] all the day.
texts.psa.52.2: Engulfing ruin, doth thy tongue devise, Like a whetted razor, working deceit;
texts.psa.52.3: Thou lovest Evil more than good, Falsehood, more than speaking righteousness. [Selah.]
texts.psa.52.4: Thou lovest all devouring words, O deceitful tongue!
texts.psa.52.5: GOD also, will break thee down utterly, He will snatch thee up and tear thee away tentless, And uproot thee, out of the land of the living. [Selah.]
texts.psa.52.6: The righteous shall both see and fear, And, over him, shall laugh:
texts.psa.52.7: Lo! the man who made not God his refuge,—But trusted in the abundance of his riches, Emboldened himself in his wealth!
texts.psa.52.8: But, I, am like a flourishing olive-tree, in the house of God, I have put confidence in the lovingkindness of God, for times age-abiding and beyond.
texts.psa.52.9: I will praise thee to times age-abiding, Because thou didst effectually work,—And I will wait on thy Name, Because it is good, In the presence of thy men of lovingkindness.
texts.psa.53.1: The impious hath said in his heart, There is no God! They have acted corruptly, They have wrought abominable perversity, There is none that doeth good:—
texts.psa.53.2: God, out of the heavens, looked down upon the sons of men,—To see whether there was one that showed wisdom, Enquiring after God.
texts.psa.53.3: They all, have turned back, together have they become tainted,—There is none that doeth good, Not so much as, one!
texts.psa.53.4: Are the workers of iniquity, without knowledge? Devouring my people, [as] they devour food? Upon God, have they not called.
texts.psa.53.5: There have they been in great dread where no dread was, Because, God, hath scattered the bones of thy besieger,—Thou hast put [him] to shame, Because, God, had, rejected, them.
texts.psa.53.6: Oh that, out of Zion, were granted the salvations of Israel! When God bringeth back the captives of his people, Jacob, shall exult, Israel, shall be glad.
texts.psa.54.1: O God! by thine own Name, save me, And, by thine own strength, wilt thou vindicate me?
texts.psa.54.2: O God! Hear my prayer, Give ear to the sayings of my mouth;
texts.psa.54.3: For, aliens, have risen up against me, And, men of violence, have sought my life, They have not set God before them. [Selah.]
texts.psa.54.4: Lo! God, is bringing me help, My Lord, is with the upholders of my life;
texts.psa.54.5: Let him turn back the mischief upon mine adversaries, In thy faithfulness, destroy them!
texts.psa.54.6: With a freewill-offering, will I sacrifice unto thee, I will praise thy Name, O Yahweh, for it is good;
texts.psa.54.7: For, out of all distress, hath he rescued me,—And, upon my foes, hath, mine own eye, looked.
texts.psa.55.1: Give ear, O God, to my prayer, And do not hide thyself from my supplication:
texts.psa.55.2: Attend unto me, and answer me, I may ramble in my complaining, And be driven to and fro—
texts.psa.55.3: Because of the noise of the enemy, By reason of the oppression of the lawless one, For they would let trouble drop upon me, And, in anger, would they entrap me.
texts.psa.55.4: My heart, would writhe within me, And, the terrors of Death, have fallen upon me:
texts.psa.55.5: Fear and trembling, would enter me, And there would have overwhelmed me—a horror!
texts.psa.55.6: Then I said—Oh that there were given me a pinion, like a dove, I would fly away and be at rest:
texts.psa.55.7: Lo! I would take a distant flight, I would tarry in the wilderness. [Selah.]
texts.psa.55.8: I would hasten mine escape, From rushing wind, from storm.
texts.psa.55.9: Confuse, O My Lord, divide their speech, For I have seen violence and contention in the city;
texts.psa.55.10: Day and night, they go round her, upon her walls, And, trouble and misery, are in her midst;
texts.psa.55.11: Engulfing ruin, is in her midst, And there depart not from her broadway, oppression and deceit.
texts.psa.55.12: For it is, not an enemy, that reproacheth me, Or I could bear it,—Not one that hath hated me, who, against me, hath magnified himself, Or I might hide myself from him;
texts.psa.55.13: But it is, thou, a man esteemed as mine equal, mine associate, and mine acquaintance;
texts.psa.55.14: So that together have we been wont to find sweetness in counsel, In the house of God, used we to walk in the throng.
texts.psa.55.15: Desolations on them! Let them go down into hades alive, For, wicked doings, are at home within them.
texts.psa.55.16: I, unto God, will cry,—And, Yahweh, will save me.
texts.psa.55.17: At evening and morning and high noon, have I been wont to lament and complain, And he hath heard my voice!
texts.psa.55.18: He hath completely redeemed my soul, out of the attack upon me, For, in multitudes, were they [in conflict] with me.
texts.psa.55.19: GOD will hear, Yea He will humble them who aforetime sat [enthroned]. [Selah.] With whom are no changings, Neither have they revered God.
texts.psa.55.20: He hath thrust forth his hands, against them he was wont to salute, he hath violated his covenant;
texts.psa.55.21: Smoother than curds, were [the words of] his mouth, But, war, was [in] his heart,—Softer his words than oil, Yet, they, were drawn swords!
texts.psa.55.22: Cast upon Yahweh thy lot, and, he, will sustain thee: He will not suffer, to times age-abiding, the righteous one to be shaken.
texts.psa.55.23: But, thou, O God, wilt bring them down to the pit of destruction, Men of bloodshed and deceit, shall not live out half their days; But, I, will trust in thee.
texts.psa.56.1: Show me favour, O God, For weak man hath panted for me, All the day, a fighter oppresseth me:
texts.psa.56.2: Mine adversaries have panted all the day, For, many, are fighting with me, loftily.
texts.psa.56.3: What day I am afraid, I, unto thee will direct my confidence.
texts.psa.56.4: In God, I will praise his cause,—In God, have I trusted, I will not fear, What can flesh do unto me?
texts.psa.56.5: All the day, they wrest, my words, Against me, all their devices are for mischief;
texts.psa.56.6: They stir up strife—they lie hid, They, mark my steps,—Seeing they have waited for my life.
texts.psa.56.7: Because of iniquity, recompense thou them,—In anger, bring thou down, the peoples, O God.
texts.psa.56.8: My wandering, hast, thou, recorded,—Put thou my tears in thy bottle, Are they not in thy record?
texts.psa.56.9: Then, shall my foes turn back, in the day I cry, This, I know, for God is mine!
texts.psa.56.10: In God, will I praise with good cause: In Yahweh, will I praise with good cause;
texts.psa.56.11: In God, have I trusted, I will not fear, What can a son of earth do unto me!
texts.psa.56.12: Upon me, O God, are thy vows, I will pay back praises unto thee.
texts.psa.56.13: For thou hast rescued my soul from death, Wilt thou not [rescue] my feet from stumbling? That I may walk to and fro, before God, In the light of life.
texts.psa.57.1: Show me favour, O God, Show me favour, For, in thee, hath my soul sought refuge,—And, in the shadow of thy wings, will I seek refuge, Until the storm of ruin pass by.
texts.psa.57.2: I will cry unto God Most High, Unto GOD, who accomplisheth on my behalf:
texts.psa.57.3: He will send out of heaven, that he may save me, He who is panting for me, hath reproached. [Selah.] God will send out his lovingkindness and his faithfulness.
texts.psa.57.4: My soul, is in the midst of lions, I lie down amidst flames, As for the sons of men, Their teeth, are spear and arrows, And, their tongue, is a sharp sword.
texts.psa.57.5: Be exalted Above the Heavens, O God, Above all the earth, thy glory!
texts.psa.57.6: A net, did they fix for my steps, My soul was bowed down,—They digged before me a pit, They fell into the midst thereof! [Selah.]
texts.psa.57.7: Fixed is my heart, O God, Fixed is my heart, I will sing, and touch the strings.
texts.psa.57.8: Awake, mine honour, Awake, harp and lyre, I will awaken the dawn;
texts.psa.57.9: I will thank thee, among the peoples, O My Lord, I will praise thee in song, among the races of men.
texts.psa.57.10: For, great, unto the heavens, is thy lovingkindness, And, unto the skies, thy faithfulness.
texts.psa.57.11: Be exalted Above the heavens, O God, Above all the earth, thy glory!
texts.psa.58.1: Are ye, indeed, silent [when] righteousness, ye should speak? When, with equity, ye should judge, O ye sons of men?
texts.psa.58.2: Aye! ye all do work, perversity,—Throughout the land, your hands, weigh out, violence!
texts.psa.58.3: Lawless men have been estranged from birth, They have gone astray from their nativity, speaking falsehood;
texts.psa.58.4: Their poison, is like unto the poison of a serpent, Like the deaf adder, that stoppeth his ear;
texts.psa.58.5: That will not hearken to the voice of whisperers, Though the wise one try to bind him with spells.
texts.psa.58.6: O God! break away their teeth in their mouth, The biters of the young lions, knock thou out, O Yahweh!
texts.psa.58.7: Let such men flow away like waters that disperse themselves: He prepareth his arrow, Like [grass] let them be cut down:
texts.psa.58.8: Like a snail, which melteth away as it goeth, An untimely birth of a woman, which hath not seen the sun:
texts.psa.58.9: Before your kettles can perceive the [kindled] bramble, Be he green or be he withered, he shall be swept away.
texts.psa.58.10: The righteous man will rejoice when he hath seen an avenging, His feet, will he bathe in the blood of the lawless one:—
texts.psa.58.11: So that a son of earth may say—Surely there is fruit for the righteous man! Surely there are gods who judge in the earth!
texts.psa.59.1: Rescue me from my foes, O my God, From them who lift themselves up against me, wilt thou set me on high:
texts.psa.59.2: Rescue me, from the workers of iniquity, And, from the men of bloodshed, save me.
texts.psa.59.3: For lo! they have lain in wait for my life, Mighty ones stir up strife against me, Without transgression of mine, and without sin of mine, O Yahweh;
texts.psa.59.4: For no iniquity, do they run that they may take their stand, Rouse thyself to meet me, and see.
texts.psa.59.5: Thou, therefore, O Yahweh, God of hosts, God of Israel, Awake, to visit all the nations, Do not show favour to any iniquitous traitors. [Selah.]
texts.psa.59.6: They return at evening, They grow like a dog, And go round the city.
texts.psa.59.7: Lo! they belch forth with their mouth, Swords, are in their lips, For [say they], Who doth hear?
texts.psa.59.8: Thou, therefore, O Yahweh, wilt laugh at them, Thou wilt mock at all nations.
texts.psa.59.9: O my Strength, unto thee, will I make melody, For, God, is my high tower.
texts.psa.59.10: My God of lovingkindness, will come to meet me, God, will let me look on mine adversaries.
texts.psa.59.11: Do not slay them, lest my people forget, Cause them to wander by thy strength, and prostrate them, [Thou] our shield, O Lord!
texts.psa.59.12: The sin of their mouth, The word of their lips, Let them then be captured in their pride, Both for the oath and for the deception they record.
texts.psa.59.13: Bring to a full end in wrath, Bring to a full end, that they be no more,—That men may know that, God, is ruling in Jacob, Unto the ends of the earth. [Selah.]
texts.psa.59.14: Let them return, then, at evening, Let them growl like a dog, And go round the city.
texts.psa.59.15: They, may prowl about for food,—And, if they are not satisfied, then let them whine!
texts.psa.59.16: But, I, will sing thy power, And will shout aloud, in the morning, thy lovingkindness,—For thou has become a refuge for me, And a place to flee to in the day of my distress.
texts.psa.59.17: O my Strength, unto thee, will I make melody, For, God, is my high tower, my God of lovingkindness.
texts.psa.60.1: O God, thou hast rejected us—hast scattered us, Thou hast been angry, Wilt thou restore us?
texts.psa.60.2: Thou hast shaken the land—hast rent it, Heal thou the fractures thereof—for it hath tottered:
texts.psa.60.3: Thou hast suffered thy people to see hardship, Thou hast let them drink the wine of confusion.
texts.psa.60.4: Thou hadst given—to them that revere thee—a banner, to float aloft, Because of [thy] faithfulness. [Selah.]
texts.psa.60.5: That thy beloved ones may be delivered, Save thou with thine own right hand—and answer us.
texts.psa.60.6: God, hath spoken in his holiness—I will exult! I will apportion Shechem, And, the Vale of Succoth, will I measure out;
texts.psa.60.7: Mine, is Gilead—and mine, Manasseh, But, Ephraim, is the defence, of my head, Judah, is my commander’s staff;
texts.psa.60.8: Moab, is my wash-bowl, Upon Edom, will I throw my shoe, Over Philistia! raise shout of triumph.
texts.psa.60.9: Who will conduct me to a fortified city? Who will lead me as far as Edom!
texts.psa.60.10: Is it not, thou, O God?—thou hast rejected us! And wilt thou not go forth, O God, with our hosts?
texts.psa.60.11: Grant us help out of distress, For, vain, is the deliverance of man:
texts.psa.60.12: In God, we shall do valiantly, He himself, therefore, will tread down our adversaries.
texts.psa.61.1: Hear, O God, my loud cry, Attend unto my prayer:
texts.psa.61.2: From the end of the earth, unto thee do I cry, When my heart fainteth away, Unto a rock that is higher than I, wilt thou lead me.
texts.psa.61.3: For thou hast been, A Refuge to me, A Tower of Strength, from the face of the foe.
texts.psa.61.4: I would be a guest in thy tent to the ages, I would seek refuge in the concealment of thy wings. [Selah.]
texts.psa.61.5: For, thou, O God, hast hearkened to my vows, Thou hast granted a possession, unto them who revere thy Name.
texts.psa.61.6: Days—unto the days of the king, wilt thou add. His years, as of generation after generation:
texts.psa.61.7: Let him retain his seat age-abidingly before God, Appoint that, lovingkindness and faithfulness, my watch over him!
texts.psa.61.8: So, will I sing thy Name unto futurity, Paying my vows, day by day.
texts.psa.62.1: Surely, towards God, silence [becometh] my soul, From him, is my salvation:
texts.psa.62.2: Surely, he, is my rock and my salvation, My high tower—I shall not be greatly shaken!
texts.psa.62.3: How long will ye shout at a man? Ye shall be crushed all of you,—Like a wall that bulgeth,—a fence pushed in!
texts.psa.62.4: Surely, from his elevation, they have taken counsel to thrust him down, They accept falsehood,—With his mouth, they each of them bless, But, inwardly, they revile. [Selah.]
texts.psa.62.5: Surely, towards God, be thou silent, my soul, For, from him, is mine expectation:
texts.psa.62.6: Surely, he, is my rock, and my salvation, My high tower—I shall not be shaken!
texts.psa.62.7: Upon God, [depend] my salvation and mine honour, My rock of strength, my refuge, are in God.
texts.psa.62.8: Trust ye in him all ye assembly of the people, Pour out, before him, your heart, God, is a refuge for us. [Selah.]
texts.psa.62.9: Surely, vanity, are men of low degree, Deception, men of high degree,—In the balances, they go up, They, are [made] of vanity, altogether.
texts.psa.62.10: Do not trust in extortion, Nor, with robbery, become vain, As for wealth, when it beareth fruit, Do not set [thereon your] heart.
texts.psa.62.11: One thing, hath God spoken, Two things, [there are] which I have heard, That, power, belongeth unto God;
texts.psa.62.12: And, thine, O My Lord, is lovingkindness,—For, thou, wilt pay back unto every man—according to his deed.
texts.psa.63.1: O God, my GOD, thou art, Earnestly do I desire thee,—My soul thirsteth for thee, My flesh fainteth for thee, In a land—dry, and weary for want of water,—
texts.psa.63.2: In like manner as, in the sanctuary, I have had vision of thee, To behold thy power and thy glory.
texts.psa.63.3: Because better is thy lovingkindness than life, My lips, aloud shall praise thee!
texts.psa.63.4: Thus, will I bless thee while I live, In thy Name, will I lift up mine outspread hands:
texts.psa.63.5: As with fatness and richness, shall my soul be satisfied, And, with joyfully shouting lips, shall my mouth utter praise.
texts.psa.63.6: Should I call thee to mind upon my couch, In the watches of the night, would I breathe soft speech of thee.
texts.psa.63.7: For thou hast become a help unto me,—And, in the shadow of thy wings, will I shout for joy.
texts.psa.63.8: My soul hath run clinging to thee, On me, hath thy right hand laid hold.
texts.psa.63.9: When, they, to crush it, would seek my life, They shall go into the lower parts of the earth:
texts.psa.63.10: Every one shall be given up into the power of the sword, The portion of jackals, shall they become.
texts.psa.63.11: But, the king, shall rejoice in God,—Every one shall glory who sweareth by him, For the mouth of them who speak falsehood, shall be stopped.
texts.psa.64.1: Hear, O God, my voice when I complain, From dread peril by the foe, wilt thou guard my life.
texts.psa.64.2: Wilt thou hide me, From the conclave of evil-doers, From the crowd of workers of iniquity.
texts.psa.64.3: Who have sharpened, like a sword, their tongue, Have made ready their arrow—a bitter word;
texts.psa.64.4: To shoot, in secret places, at the blameless one, Suddenly they shoot at him, and fear not.
texts.psa.64.5: They strengthen for them a wicked word, They talk of hiding snares, They have said, Who can see them?
texts.psa.64.6: They devise perverse things, They have completed the device well devised, Both the intent of each one, and the mind, are unsearchable.
texts.psa.64.7: Once let God have shot at them an arrow, Suddenly have appeared their own wounds!
texts.psa.64.8: When they were to have ruined another, their tongue smote themselves, All who observe them take flight.
texts.psa.64.9: Therefore have all men feared,—And have told the doing of God, And, his work, have considered.
texts.psa.64.10: The righteous man shall rejoice in Yahweh, and seek refuge in him, Then shall glory—all who are upright in heart.
texts.psa.65.1: Thine, are silence [and] praise, O God, in Zion,—And, to thee, shall be paid the vow.
texts.psa.65.2: Thou hearer of prayer! Unto thee, shall all flesh come.
texts.psa.65.3: Iniquitous things, have been too strong for me, As for our transgressions, wilt, thou, by propitiation remove them.
texts.psa.65.4: How happy the man thou shalt choose and bring near! He shall abide in thy courts,—We shall be satisfied with, The blessing of thy house, The holiness of thy temple.
texts.psa.65.5: By things reverend in righteousness, wilt thou answer us, O God of our salvation, The confidence of all the ends of the earth, And of the sea far away;
texts.psa.65.6: Who setteth fast the mountains by his strength, Being girded with might;
texts.psa.65.7: Who stilleth, The noise of the seas, The noise of their rolling waves, and The tumult of races of men?
texts.psa.65.8: Yea the dwellers in the uttermost parts have feared at thy tokens, The goings forth of morning and evening, thou causest to shout for joy.
texts.psa.65.9: Thou hast visited the earth, and made it abound, Abundantly, dost thou enrich it—The channel of God, is full of waters, Thou preparest their corn, Yea, thus, dost thou prepare it:
texts.psa.65.10: The ridges thereof, drenching, Settling the furrows thereof, With myriad drops, dost thou soften it, The sprouting thereof, doth thou bless.
texts.psa.65.11: Thou hast set a crown upon thy year of bounty, And, thy tracks, drop fatness;
texts.psa.65.12: Fruitful are the pastures of the wilderness, And, with exultation, the hills do gird themselves.
texts.psa.65.13: Clothed are the pastures with flocks, The valleys also, cover themselves with corn, They shout for joy, yea they sing.
texts.psa.66.1: Make a joyful noise unto God, all the earth;
texts.psa.66.2: Praise ye in song the glory of his Name, Celebrate the glory of his praise:
texts.psa.66.3: Say unto God—How fearful in thy doings, Through the abounding of thy power, shall thy foes come cringing unto thee;
texts.psa.66.4: All the earth, shall bow themselves down to thee, And sing praises unto thee,. Shall praise in song thy Name. [Selah.]
texts.psa.66.5: Come and see the doings of God,—Fearful in deed toward the sons of men:
texts.psa.66.6: He turned the sea into dry land, Through the stream, crossed they over on foot, There did we rejoice in him:
texts.psa.66.7: Who ruleth, in his might, unto times age abiding, His eyes, over the nations, keep watch, The rebellious, let them not exalt themselves. [Selah.]
texts.psa.66.8: Bless our God, O ye peoples, And cause to be heard, the sound of his praise;—
texts.psa.66.9: Who hath set our soul among the living, And hath not suffered, our foot, to slip.
texts.psa.66.10: For thou didst prove us, O God, Thou didst refine us, according to the refining of silver:
texts.psa.66.11: Thou didst bring us into the hunter’s net, Thou didst lay a load upon our loins;
texts.psa.66.12: Thou didst let men ride at our head; We went into fire and into water, But thou didst bring us forth into freedom.
texts.psa.66.13: I will enter thy house with ascending-sacrifices, I will pay unto thee my vows,
texts.psa.66.14: Which my lips uttered, And my mouth spake, in my distress.
texts.psa.66.15: Ascending-sacrifices of fatlings, will I cause to ascend unto thee, With the perfume of rams, I will offer bulls, with he-goats. [Selah.]
texts.psa.66.16: Come! hearken—that I may recount, all ye reverers of God, What he hath done for my soul:—
texts.psa.66.17: Unto him—with my mouth, did I cry, And high praise was under my tongue.
texts.psa.66.18: If, iniquity, I had cared for in my heart, My Lord, had not heard me!
texts.psa.66.19: But in truth, God hath heard, He hath attended to the voice of my prayer.
texts.psa.66.20: Blessed be God, Who hath not turned away my prayer, Nor his own lovingkindness from me.
texts.psa.67.1: God, be favorable to us and bless us, Cause his face to shine upon us. [Selah.]
texts.psa.67.2: That thy way may be known throughout the earth, Throughout all nations, thy saving help!
texts.psa.67.3: Peoples will praise thee, O God, Peoples will, all of them, praise thee,
texts.psa.67.4: Races of men, will be glad and shout for joy, Because thou wilt judge peoples with equity, And, races of men throughout the earth, thou wilt lead. [Selah.]
texts.psa.67.5: Peoples will praise thee, O God,—Peoples will, all of them, praise thee.
texts.psa.67.6: Earth, will have given her increase, God, our own God, will bless us:
texts.psa.67.7: God, will bless us, That all the ends of the earth, may revere him.
texts.psa.68.1: Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered, Yea let them that hate him flee before him:
texts.psa.68.2: As smoke is driven about, Let them be driven about,—As wax is melted before a fire, Let the lawless perish before God.
texts.psa.68.3: But let, the righteous, be glad, let them exult before God, Yea let them rejoice with gladness.
texts.psa.68.4: Sing ye to God, Make music of his Name,—Lift up (a song), to him that rideth through the waste plains,—Since Yah is his name, exult ye before him.
texts.psa.68.5: The father of the fatherless, And the advocate of widows, Is God, in his holy habitation.
texts.psa.68.6: God, is he that causeth the solitary to dwell in a home, That bringeth out prisoners into prosperity, But, the rebellious, have made their habitation in a sunburnt land.
texts.psa.68.7: O God! When thou camest forth before thy people, When thou didst stride through the wilderness, [Selah.]
texts.psa.68.8: Earth, trembled, Yea, the heavens, dripped at the presence of God,—This Sinai—at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
texts.psa.68.9: A bounteous rain, dost thou shed abroad, O God, upon thine inheritance, When exhausted, thou thyself, hast supported it:
texts.psa.68.10: Thy living host, have remained therein, Thou dost provide, in thy bounty, for the humbled ones—O God!
texts.psa.68.11: Let, My Lord, but give the word, The herald bands, will be a mighty host:
texts.psa.68.12: Kings of armies, they flee! they flee! And, she that stayeth at home, shall share the spoil.
texts.psa.68.13: Though ye rest between the folds, The wings of the dove, shall be covered with silver, And, her pinions, with green-shimmering gold.
texts.psa.68.14: When the Almighty scattereth kings therein, It will gleam like snow in the gloom:
texts.psa.68.15: A mighty mountain, is the mountain of Bashan, A mountain of peaks, is the mountain of Bashan!—
texts.psa.68.16: Wherefore start ye up, ye mountains, ye peaks? The mountain God hath coveted for his habitation, Surely, Yahweh will inhabit it ever!
texts.psa.68.17: The chariots of God, are two myriads—thousands repeated, My Lord, is among them Sinai, is in the sanctuary!
texts.psa.68.18: Thou hast ascended on high, Thou hast led in procession a body of captives, Thou hast received gifts consisting of men, Yea even the rebellious, That, Yah, Elohim, might settle down to rest.
texts.psa.68.19: Blessed be My Lord! Day by day, he beareth our burden for us, GOD himself, is our salvation. [Selah.]
texts.psa.68.20: The GOD we have, is a GOD of saving deeds, And, due to Yahweh, My Lord, are escapes from death.
texts.psa.68.21: Yea, God himself, will smite through the head of his foes,—The hairy crown of him that is marching on in his guilty deeds.
texts.psa.68.22: Said My Lord, From Bashan, will I bring back,—I will bring back from the depths of the sea:
texts.psa.68.23: That thou mayest bathe thy foot in blood,—The tongue of thy dogs, from the foes, hath its portion.
texts.psa.68.24: They have seen thy progress O God, The progress of my GOD, my king into the sanctuary:
texts.psa.68.25: In front are the singers, Behind are the harpers, In the midst of damsels playing on timbrels:
texts.psa.68.26: In the congregations, bless ye God, My Lord, from among the called of Israel:
texts.psa.68.27: There, is Benjamin, the Diminutive—ruling them, The princes of Judah—their throng, The princes of Zebulun, The princes of Naphtali.
texts.psa.68.28: Thy God hath commanded thy strength,—The strength, O God, which thou hast wrought for us.
texts.psa.68.29: Because of thy temple above Jerusalem, Unto thee, shall kings bear along a gift—
texts.psa.68.30: Rebuke thou, The wild beast of the reeds, The herd of mighty oxen among the calves of the peoples—Each one bowing down with bars of silver,—Scatter thou the peoples, who in wars take delight.
texts.psa.68.31: Ambassadors come out of Egypt, The Ethiopian, eagerly stretcheth out his hands, unto God.
texts.psa.68.32: Ye kingdoms of the earth, sing unto God, Praise in song Adonay. [Selah.]
texts.psa.68.33: Unto him that rideth upon the most ancient heavens, Lo! he uttereth his voice, a voice of strength.
texts.psa.68.34: Ascribe ye strength unto God,—Over Israel, is his majesty, And his strength, in the skies. To be revered is God, for his sanctuary,—
texts.psa.68.35: As for the GOD of Israel, he, is giving strength and abundant might to the people. Blessed be God!
texts.psa.69.1: Save me, O God, For waters have entered as far as the life;
texts.psa.69.2: I have sunk in deep swamp, Where there is no place to stand, I have come into abysses of waters, Where a flood hath overflowed me;
texts.psa.69.3: I am weary with mine outcry, Parched is my throat,—Mine eyes have become dim, through waiting for my God.
texts.psa.69.4: More than the hairs of my head, Are they who hate me without cause,—Firmer than my bones, Are they who are my foes for false cause,—What I had not plundered, then, had I to restore.
texts.psa.69.5: O God, thou, hast known my folly, And, my wrong-doings, from thee, have not been hid.
texts.psa.69.6: Let them not be ashamed, through me, Who have waited for thee, O My Lord, Yahweh of hosts,—Let them not be confounded, through me, Who are seeking thee, O God of Israel!
texts.psa.69.7: Because, for thy sake, have I borne reproach, Confusion hath covered my face;
texts.psa.69.8: One estranged, have I become, to my own brethren, Yea, an alien, to the sons of my own mother;
texts.psa.69.9: Because, zeal for thy house, hath eaten me up, And, the reproaches of them who have reproached thee, have fallen upon me.
texts.psa.69.10: When I have humbled my soul with fasting, Then hath it turned to my reproach;
texts.psa.69.11: When I have made my clothing of sackcloth, Then have I served them for a by-word;
texts.psa.69.12: They who sit in the gate talk against me,—And [against me are] the songs of them who imbibe strong drink.
texts.psa.69.13: But, as for me, my prayer shall be unto thee, O Yahweh, in a time of acceptance, O God, in the abounding of thy lovingkindness, answer me with thy saving faithfulness.
texts.psa.69.14: Rescue me out of the mire, lest I sink, Let me be rescued, From my haters, and, From abysses of waters:
texts.psa.69.15: Let not a flood of waters overflow me, And let not the depth swallow me up, Neither let the well close, over me, her mouth.
texts.psa.69.16: Answer me, O Yahweh, for good is thy lovingkindness, According to the abounding of thy compassions, turn thou towards me:
texts.psa.69.17: Then do not hide thy face from thy servant, Because I am in distress, haste thou—answer me!
texts.psa.69.18: Oh draw near unto my soul—redeem it, Because of mine enemies, ransom me.
texts.psa.69.19: Thou, knowest my reproach, and my shame, and my confusion, Before thee, are all mine adversaries.
texts.psa.69.20: Reproach hath broken my heart, and I am weak,—Though I waited for one to pity me, yet there was none, And for comforters, yet I found not any.
texts.psa.69.21: But they put in my food—poison! And, for my thirst, they gave for my drink—vinegar!
texts.psa.69.22: Let their table, before them, become a snare, And unto their friends, a lure;
texts.psa.69.23: Let their eyes become too dim to see, And, their loins, continually cause thou to shake;
texts.psa.69.24: Pour out over them thine indignation, And let, the glow of thine anger, overtake them:
texts.psa.69.25: Let their encampment become desolate, In their tents, be there none to dwell:
texts.psa.69.26: For, whom, thou thyself, hadst smitten, they pursued, And, unto the pain of thy wounded ones, they must needs add.
texts.psa.69.27: Lay punishment on their iniquity, And let them not enter into thy righteousness;
texts.psa.69.28: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, And, with the righteous, let them not be enrolled.
texts.psa.69.29: I, then, am humbled and in pain, Thy salvation, O God, may it set me on high.
texts.psa.69.30: I will praise the Name of God with a song, And will magnify him with thanksgiving;
texts.psa.69.31: So shall it be more pleasing to Yahweh than a bullock of the herd, Showing horn [and] divided hoof.
texts.psa.69.32: The humbled have seen—they rejoice! Ye seekers of God, let your heart, then, revive;
texts.psa.69.33: For, a Hearkener to the needy, is Yahweh, And, his prisoners, hath he not despised.
texts.psa.69.34: Let the heavens and the earth, praise him, The seas, and everything that creepeth therein.
texts.psa.69.35: For, God, will save Zion, And build the cities of Judah, So shall men dwell there, and possess it:
texts.psa.69.36: Yea, the seed of his servants, shall inherit it, And, the lovers of his Name, shall settle down therein.
texts.psa.70.1: [Be pleased] O God, to rescue me, O Yahweh, to help me—make haste.
texts.psa.70.2: Let them turn pale and then at once blush, Who are seeking my life,—Let them draw back, and be confounded, Who are taking pleasure in my misfortune;
texts.psa.70.3: Let them turn back, on account of their own shame, Who are saying, Aha! Aha!
texts.psa.70.4: Let all them be glad and rejoice in thee, Yea, let them, who are seekers of thee,—say continually, God be magnified! Who are lovers of thy salvation.
texts.psa.70.5: But, I, being humbled and needy, O God, haste to me,—My help and my deliverer, art thou, O Yahweh do not tarry.
texts.psa.71.1: In thee, O Yahweh, have I sought refuge, May I not be ashamed unto times age-abiding:
texts.psa.71.2: In thy righteousness, wilt thou rescue me, and deliver me, Incline unto me thine ear, and save me:
texts.psa.71.3: Be thou unto me, a Rock to dwell in, a Place of Security, To save me, For, my mountain crag and my stronghold, thou art.
texts.psa.71.4: Oh my God, deliver me, From the hand of the lawless one, From the clutch of the perverse and ruthless one;
texts.psa.71.5: For, thou, art my hope, My Lord, Yahweh, My confidence from my youthful days:
texts.psa.71.6: Upon thee, have I stayed myself from birth, Thou art he that severed me, from the body of my mother, Of thee, shall be my praise—continually.
texts.psa.71.7: A very wonder, have I been unto many, Seeing that, thou, hast been my strong refuge,
texts.psa.71.8: My mouth shall be filled with, thy praise, All the day, with thy splendour.
texts.psa.71.9: Do not cast me off in the time of old age, When my vigour faileth, do not forsake me;
texts.psa.71.10: For mine enemies have spoken of me, And, they who watch for my life, have taken counsel together;
texts.psa.71.11: Saying, God, hath forsaken him, Pursue and take him, For there is none to rescue.
texts.psa.71.12: O God, be not far from me, O my God, to help me, make haste!
texts.psa.71.13: Let them be ashamed—be consumed, Who are assailing my life,—Let them be covered with reproach and confusion, Who are seeking my hurt.
texts.psa.71.14: But, I, continually will hope, And will add to all thy praise;
texts.psa.71.15: My mouth, shall relate thy righteousness, All the day, thy deliverance, For I know not the numbers.
texts.psa.71.16: I will enter into the mighty doings of My Lord—Yahweh, I will make mention of thy righteousness—thine alone.
texts.psa.71.17: O God, thou hast taught me from my youthful days, And, hitherto, have I been wont to tell of thy wonders;
texts.psa.71.18: Even now, therefore, that I am old and grayheaded, O God, do not forsake me,—Until I tell of thine arm unto a [new] generation, Unto every one that is to come, thy might;
texts.psa.71.19: And, as for thy righteousness, O God, up on high, Wherein thou hast wrought great things, O God! who is like unto thee?
texts.psa.71.20: Thou who hast let us see many distresses and misfortunes, Wilt again bring us to life, And, out of the resounding depths of the earth, wilt again raise us up;
texts.psa.71.21: Thou wilt increase my greatness, And, on every side, wilt comfort me.
texts.psa.71.22: I also, will praise thee by the aid of a harp, Thy faithfulness, O my God,—I will make music unto thee with a lyre, Thou holy one of Israel;
texts.psa.71.23: My lips shall make a joyful noise, When I make music unto thee, And my soul which thou hast ransomed;
texts.psa.71.24: Even my tongue, all the day, shall softly utter thy righteousness, For they have turned pale—for they have blushed, Who were seeking my hurt.
texts.psa.72.1: O God! thy justice, give, unto the king, And thy righteousness, unto the son of a king;
texts.psa.72.2: May he judge, Thy people with righteousness; And thine oppressed ones with justice;
texts.psa.72.3: May the mountains bring peace to the people, And the hills [be laden] with righteousness;
texts.psa.72.4: May he, Vindicate the oppressed of the people, Bring deliverance to the children of the needy, and, Crush the oppressor.
texts.psa.72.5: Let men revere thee, With the sun, And in presence of the moon, Unto the remotest generation.
texts.psa.72.6: Let him come down, Like rain on fields to be mown, Like myriad drops on land to be reaped.
