texts.psa.72.7: May righteousness, in his days, blossom forth, And abundance of peace, till there be no moon.
texts.psa.72.8: So let him have dominion, From sea to sea, And from the River [="Euphrates"] unto the ends of the earth;
texts.psa.72.9: Before him, let the men of the desert kneel, But, as for his foes, the dust, let them lick;
texts.psa.72.10: The kings of Tarshish and of the Coastlands, A gift, let them render, The kings of Sheba and Seba, A present, let them bring;
texts.psa.72.11: Yea let all kings, bow down unto him, Let, all nations, serve him;
texts.psa.72.12: Because he Rescueth, The needy from the rich, The oppressed, who hath no helper;
texts.psa.72.13: He Pitieth the weak and the needy, And, the lives of the needy, he Saveth:
texts.psa.72.14: From extortion, and, violence, he Redeemeth their life, And precious is their blood in his sight.
texts.psa.72.15: Let him live, then! And be there given unto him of the gold of Sheba,—Let prayer also be offered for him continually, All the day, let him be blessed.
texts.psa.72.16: May there be an abundance of corn in the earth, in the top of the mountains,—Let the fruit thereof, wave like Lebanon, And they of the city bloom like the fresh shoots of the earth.
texts.psa.72.17: May his Name be age-abiding, In the presence of the sun, let his Name flourish,—And may all the families of the ground bless themselves in him, All nations, pronounce him happy!
texts.psa.72.18: Blessed be Yahweh God, the God of Israel,—Who doeth wondrous things by himself alone;
texts.psa.72.19: And blessed be his glorious Name, unto times age-abiding,—And filled with his glory be all the earth, Amen and Amen!
texts.psa.72.20: Ended are the prayers of David, son of Jesse.
texts.psa.73.1: Nothing but good, is God, Unto Israel, Unto the pure in heart.
texts.psa.73.2: But, as for me,—My feet had, almost stumbled, My steps had, well-nigh slipped;
texts.psa.73.3: For I was envious of the boasters, At the prosperity of the lawless, used I to look.
texts.psa.73.4: For they have no pangs in their death, And vigorous is their body;
texts.psa.73.5: Of the toil of weak mortals, have they none, Nor, with the sons of earth, are they hard smitten.
texts.psa.73.6: For this cause, doth arrogance deck them as a neck-chain, And a garment of wrong is their attire;
texts.psa.73.7: Their iniquity, hath proceeded from fatness, They have surpassed the imaginations of the heart;
texts.psa.73.8: They mock, and wickedly command oppression, From on high, they command;
texts.psa.73.9: They have set, in the heavens, their mouth, And, their tongue, marcheth through the earth.
texts.psa.73.10: Therefore must his people return thither, And, the waters of abundance, are drained by them;
texts.psa.73.11: And they say—How doth GOD know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?
texts.psa.73.12: Lo! these, are the lawless, Who are secure for an age, They have attained unto wealth.
texts.psa.73.13: Altogether in vain, Have I cleansed my heart, And bathed in pureness, my hands;
texts.psa.73.14: And yet been smitten all the day, And been rebuked morning by morning!
texts.psa.73.15: If I had thought, I will relate it thus, Lo! the circle of thy sons, had I betrayed.
texts.psa.73.16: When I reasoned, that I might understand this, A vexation, it was in mine eyes:
texts.psa.73.17: Until I could enter the holy places of God,—Could give heed to their hereafter:—
texts.psa.73.18: Surely, in slippery places, dost thou set them,—Thou hast suffered them to fall into places of danger.
texts.psa.73.19: How have they become desolate, as in a moment! They have ceased—come to an end, by reason of calamities.
texts.psa.73.20: As the dream of him that waketh, O my Lord! when rousing thyself up, their shadowy being, wilt thou despise.
texts.psa.73.21: But my heart had grown embittered, And, in my reins, had I received wounds;
texts.psa.73.22: But, I, was brutish, and could not perceive, Like the beasts, had I become before thee.
texts.psa.73.23: Nevertheless, I, am continually before thee, Thou hast taken hold of my right hand;
texts.psa.73.24: By thy counsel, wilt thou guide me, And, afterwards, unto glory, wilt thou take me.
texts.psa.73.25: Whom have I in the heavens? And, compared with thee, there is nothing I desire on earth.
texts.psa.73.26: Failed have my flesh and my heart, The rock of my heart—and my portion, is God unto times age-abiding.
texts.psa.73.27: For lo! they who are far from thee, shall perish, Thou hast put an end to every one who wandered unchastely from thee.
texts.psa.73.28: But, as for me, the drawing near of God, is my blessedness,—I have made, of My Lord Yahweh, my refuge,—That I may recount all thy works.
texts.psa.74.1: Wherefore, O God, hast thou cast off utterly? Shall thine anger smoke against the flock of thine own pasturing?
texts.psa.74.2: Remember thine own assembly thou didst acquire aforetime, Thou didst redeem the tribe of thine own inheritance, Mount Zion, wherein thou didst take up thy habitation.
texts.psa.74.3: Lift up thy steps unto the places utterly unsafe, All the mischief!—the foe in the sanctuary!
texts.psa.74.4: Thine adversaries have roared in the midst of thine appointed meeting, They have set their ensigns as tokens!
texts.psa.74.5: One used to be known according as he carried up high—into the thicket of trees—the axes;
texts.psa.74.6: But, now, the doors thereof all together, with axes and hammers, they batter down.
texts.psa.74.7: They have cast, into the fire, thy sanctuary, To the ground, have they profaned the habitation of thy Name.
texts.psa.74.8: They have said in their heart, Let us suppress them altogether, They have burned up all the meeting-places of GOD in the land.
texts.psa.74.9: Our own signs, have we not seen,—There is no longer a prophet,—Neither is there with us, one who knoweth—How long!
texts.psa.74.10: How long, O God, shall the adversary, reproach? Shall the enemy revile thy Name perpetually?
texts.psa.74.11: Wherefore shouldst thou withdraw thy hand—thy right hand? [Bring it] out of the midst of thy bosom! [Selah.]
texts.psa.74.12: But, God, hath been my king from aforetime, Working Deliverances in the midst of the earth.
texts.psa.74.13: Thou, didst cleave asunder, in thy might, the sea, Thou didst break in pieces the heads of the Crocodiles, [till they floated] on the waters;
texts.psa.74.14: Thou, didst crush the heads of the Sea-Monster, Thou didst give him to be food, for the people of the deserts;
texts.psa.74.15: Thou, didst cleave open fountain and torrent, Thou, didst dry up rivers of steady flow:
texts.psa.74.16: Thine, is the day, Yea, thine, the night, Thou, didst establish moon and sun;
texts.psa.74.17: Thou, didst set up all the bounds of the earth, As for summer and winter, thou, didst form them!
texts.psa.74.18: Remember this, An enemy, hath reproached Yahweh, Yea, an impious people, have reviled thy Name.
texts.psa.74.19: Do not deliver up, to a wild beast, the life of thy turtle-dove, The living host of thine oppressed ones, do not forget perpetually.
texts.psa.74.20: Have respect to thy covenant, For the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of violence.
texts.psa.74.21: May the crushed one not again be confounded, As for the oppressed and the needy, let them praise thy Name.
texts.psa.74.22: Arise! O God, plead thine own cause, Remember the reproach of thee, from the impious one, all the day:
texts.psa.74.23: Do not forget the voice of thine adversaries, The noise of thine assailants, ascending continually.
texts.psa.75.1: We have given thanks unto thee, O God, we have given thanks, And, in calling upon thy Name, men have recounted thy wonders.
texts.psa.75.2: Surely I will take a set time,—I, with equity, will judge:
texts.psa.75.3: Earth was melting away with all its inhabitants, I, have fixed the pillars thereof. [Selah.]
texts.psa.75.4: I have said to the boasters, Do not boast, And to the lawless, Do not lift up a horn;
texts.psa.75.5: Do not lift up on high your horn, Nor speak of the Rock, with arrogance;
texts.psa.75.6: For neither from east nor west, Nor from the wilderness of the mountains [cometh exaltation];
texts.psa.75.7: For, God himself, is about to judge, One, he will cast down, Another, he will lift up;
texts.psa.75.8: For, a cup, is in the hand of Yahweh, Whose wine is foaming, It is full of spiced wine, Which he hath caused to flow from one to another,—Surely, the dregs thereof, they shall drain out—they shall drink, Even all the lawless ones of the earth.
texts.psa.75.9: But, I, will exult unto times age-abiding, I will sing praises unto the God of Jacob;
texts.psa.75.10: But, all the horns of the lawless, will I hew off,—Exalted shall be the horns of the Righteous One.
texts.psa.76.1: God is, known in Judah, In Israel, great is his Name;
texts.psa.76.2: Now hath come into Salem, his pavilion, And his dwelling-place into Zion.
texts.psa.76.3: There, hath he broken in pieces the arrows of the bow, shield and sword, and battle. [Selah.]
texts.psa.76.4: Enveloped in light, thou, art more majestic than the mountains of prey.
texts.psa.76.5: The valiant of heart have become a spoil, They have slumbered their sleep, And none of the men of might have found their hands.
texts.psa.76.6: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, Stunned are the horsemen.
texts.psa.76.7: As for thee, to be feared thou art! Who then shall stand before thee, because of the power of thine anger?
texts.psa.76.8: Out of the heavens, didst thou cause judgment to be heard, Earth, feared and was still:
texts.psa.76.9: When God rose up to judgment, To save all the oppressed of the earth. [Selah.]
texts.psa.76.10: For the multitude of mankind shall give thanks unto thee, The remainder of the multitude, shall keep holy festival unto thee.
texts.psa.76.11: Vow and pay, unto Yahweh your God,—Let, all who are round about him, bear along a gift unto him who is to be revered.
texts.psa.76.12: He cutteth off the spirit of nobles, he is of reverend majesty to the kings of the earth.
texts.psa.77.1: With my voice—unto God, will I make outcry, With my voice unto God, and he will give ear unto me;
texts.psa.77.2: In the day of my distress—unto My Lord, will I seek, My hand, by night, hath been outstretched and never once became slack, My soul, hath refused to be consoled;
texts.psa.77.3: I remember God and I murmur, I muse, and my spirit swooneth. [Selah.]
texts.psa.77.4: Thou hast held, watching, mine eyes, I was driven to and fro, and could not speak;
texts.psa.77.5: I reasoned, Of the days of aforetime, Of the years of by-gone ages;
texts.psa.77.6: I remember my song in the night,—With my own heart, I commune, And my spirit, maketh search:—
texts.psa.77.7: For ages, will My Lord reject? And, not again, grant acceptance any more?
texts.psa.77.8: Hath his lovingkindness, come to a perpetual end? Hath his word failed to generation after generation?
texts.psa.77.9: Hath GOD, forgotten to show favour? Or hath he shut up, in anger, his compassions? [Selah.]
texts.psa.77.10: Then said I—An affliction to me, it is, The changing of the right hand of the Most High.
texts.psa.77.11: I will remember the doings of Yah, Surely I will remember, out of aforetime, thy wonderful way;
texts.psa.77.12: And will talk to myself of all thy work, And, of thy doings, will I muse:—
texts.psa.77.13: O God, in the sanctuary, is thy way,—Who is a great GOD like Elohim?
texts.psa.77.14: Thou, art GOD, doing wonderfully,—Thou hast made known, among the peoples, thy might;
texts.psa.77.15: Thou didst redeem, with thine arm—Thy people, Thy sons of Jacob and Joseph. [Selah.]
texts.psa.77.16: The waters saw thee, O God, The waters saw thee, They were in birth-throes, Yea the resounding deeps were stirred;
texts.psa.77.17: The clouds, poured down waters, The skies uttered, a voice, Yea, thine arrows, flew hither and thither;
texts.psa.77.18: The, voice of thy thunder, was in the whirlwind, Thy lightnings illumined the world, The earth, trembled and quaked;
texts.psa.77.19: In the sea, was thy way, And, thy path, in the mighty waters, And, thy footprints, could not be known:
texts.psa.77.20: Thou didst lead, like a flock, thy people, By the hand of Moses and Aaron.
texts.psa.78.1: Give ear, O my people, to mine instruction, Bend your ear to the sayings of my mouth;
texts.psa.78.2: I will open, in a parable, my mouth, I will pour forth enigmas out of antiquity;—
texts.psa.78.3: Which we have heard, and come to know, And, our fathers, have recounted to us;
texts.psa.78.4: We will not withhold [them] from their children, To a later generation, recounting the praises of Yahweh, Even his might and his wonders which he wrought;
texts.psa.78.5: When he set up a testimony in Jacob, And, a law, appointed in Israel,—Which he commanded our fathers, That they might make them known to their children;
texts.psa.78.6: To the end, A later generation, might come to know, Children who should be born, Who should arise, and recount [them] to their children;
texts.psa.78.7: That they might set, in Elohim, their confidence,—And not forget the doings of El, But, his commandments, might observe;
texts.psa.78.8: And not become, like their fathers, a generation stubborn and rebellious,—A generation that fixed not their heart, Neither was their spirit, faithful with GOD.
texts.psa.78.9: The sons of Ephraim—armed bowmen, Turned in the day of battle;
texts.psa.78.10: They kept not the covenant of God, And, in his law, refused to walk;
texts.psa.78.11: And forgat His doings, And his wonders which he had showed them:
texts.psa.78.12: In presence of their fathers, wrought he, wondrously,—In the land of Egypt—the field of Zoan:
texts.psa.78.13: He clave the sea, and caused them to pass through, And reared up the waters like a mound;
texts.psa.78.14: And led them, by a cloud, in the daytime, And all the night, by a light of fire;
texts.psa.78.15: He used to cleave rocks in the desert, And let them drink as out of mighty deeps;
texts.psa.78.16: And he brought forth streams out of the cliff, And caused waters to flow down, like rivers.
texts.psa.78.17: But again, once more sinned they against him, Resisting the Most High in a land of drought:
texts.psa.78.18: They put GOD to the proof in their heart, By asking food to their mind:
texts.psa.78.19: Yea they spake against Elohim,—They said, Can GOD prepare a table in the desert?
texts.psa.78.20: Lo! he hath smitten a rock, And waters, have gushed out, Yea, torrents, have rushed along,—Food also, can he give? Or provide flesh for his people?
texts.psa.78.21: Therefore, Yahweh hearkened, and became wroth,—And, a fire, was kindled against Jacob, Moreover also, anger, mounted against Israel;
texts.psa.78.22: Because, They believed not in God, Nor trusted in his salvation;
texts.psa.78.23: Though he had commanded the skies above, And, the doors of the heavens, had opened;
texts.psa.78.24: And had rained on them manna to eat, And, the corn of the heavens, had given to them:
texts.psa.78.25: The food of the mighty, each one did eat, Nourishment, sent he them to the full;
texts.psa.78.26: He let loose an east wind in the heavens, Then guided he, in his might, a south wind;
texts.psa.78.27: And rained upon them flesh as the dust, And, like the sand of the seas, birds of wing;
texts.psa.78.28: And let them fall in the midst of their camp,—Round about their habitations.
texts.psa.78.29: So they did eat and were abundantly filled, When, what they longed for, he had brought them:—
texts.psa.78.30: They had not turned away from what they had longed for, Yet was their food in their mouth,
texts.psa.78.31: When, the anger of God, mounted against them, And he slew of their vigorous youths, And, the choice young men of Israel, caused he to bow down in death.
texts.psa.78.32: For all this, sinned they still, And believed not in his wonders;
texts.psa.78.33: So he ended, in a breath, their days, And their years, in a sudden terror!
texts.psa.78.34: If he slew [of] them, then they sought him, Yea they turned, and did earnestly seek GOD;
texts.psa.78.35: And remembered that, Elohim, was their rock, Yea, EL Most High, their Redeemer:
texts.psa.78.36: So they spake him fair with their mouth, And, with their tongue, did promise him falsely;
texts.psa.78.37: But, their heart, was not fixed with him, Nor were they trusty in his covenant:
texts.psa.78.38: Yet, he, full of compassion, would put a propitiatory-covering over iniquity, and not destroy,—Yea, many a time, turned he back his anger, And would not stir up all his wrath.
texts.psa.78.39: So then he remembered, That, Flesh, they were, A Wind departing, that returneth not.
texts.psa.78.40: How often they, Resisted him in the desert, Vexed him, in the waste:
texts.psa.78.41: Yea they again put GOD to the test, And, to the Holy One of Israel, caused they sorrow:
texts.psa.78.42: They remembered not his hand—The day, When he ransomed them from the adversary;
texts.psa.78.43: When he set, in Egypt, his signs, And his wonders, in the plain of Zoan;
texts.psa.78.44: When he turned, into blood, their Nile-streams, And, their own rivers, could they not drink;
texts.psa.78.45: He sent among them, The gad-fly, and it devoured them, And the frog, and it despoiled them;
texts.psa.78.46: When he gave to the corn-locust their produce, And their toil, to the swarming locust;
texts.psa.78.47: He killed, with hail, their vine, And their sycomores, with frost:
texts.psa.78.48: When he gave up, to hail-storms, their beasts, And their cattle, to pestilent fevers;
texts.psa.78.49: He sent among them the heat of his anger, Wrath and indignation and distress,—A mission of messengers of misfortune:
texts.psa.78.50: He leveled a path for his anger, Withheld not, from death, their soul, But, their life—to the pestilence, he delivered:
texts.psa.78.51: So he smote, Every first-born in Egypt, The beginning of their strength, in the tents of Ham;
texts.psa.78.52: And he set forth, like sheep, his people, And guided them, like a flock in the desert;
texts.psa.78.53: Yea he led them securely, and they dreaded not, And, their enemies, the sea did cover.
texts.psa.78.54: Then brought he them within his own holy bounds, The mountain-range, which his right hand made his own:
texts.psa.78.55: So he drave out, before them, [whole] nations, And allotted them, by line, an inheritance, And caused to dwell, in their own homes, the tribes of Israel.
texts.psa.78.56: But they tested and resisted God Most High, And, his testimonies, did not observe;
texts.psa.78.57: But drew back and dealt treacherously, like their fathers, They turned aside, like deceitful bowmen;
texts.psa.78.58: And provoked him to anger with their high places, And, with their images, used to move him to jealousy.
texts.psa.78.59: God heard and was wroth, And greatly abhorred Israel;
texts.psa.78.60: So he gave up the habitation of Shiloh, The tent he had set up among Men;
texts.psa.78.61: Yea he gave up, into captivity, his strength, And his beauty into the hand of an adversary;
texts.psa.78.62: And delivered up, to the sword, his people, And, with his own inheritance, was he wroth;
texts.psa.78.63: His young men, were devoured by fire, And, his virgins, were not praised in song;
texts.psa.78.64: His priests, by the sword, did fall, And, his widows, were not able to bewail.
texts.psa.78.65: Then awoke, as one that had slept, Adonay, As a warrior exulting with wine!
texts.psa.78.66: So he smote his adversaries in the rear, Reproach age-abiding, laid he upon them.
texts.psa.78.67: Howbeit he rejected the tent of Joseph, And, the tribe of Ephraim, did not choose:
texts.psa.78.68: But made choice of the tribe of Judah, The mountain of Zion, which he loved;
texts.psa.78.69: And built, like the heights, his sanctuary, Like the earth, he founded it to times age-abiding.
texts.psa.78.70: And made choice of David his servant, And took him from among the folds of the sheep:
texts.psa.78.71: From after the sucking ewes, he brought him in,—To be shepherd to Jacob his people, And to Israel, his inheritance.
texts.psa.78.72: So he did shepherd them, according to the singleness of his heart, And, with the discernment of his hands, used he to guide them.
texts.psa.79.1: O God, nations, Have entered thine inheritance, Have profaned thy holy temple,—Have laid Jerusalem in heaps:
texts.psa.79.2: They have given, The dead bodies of thy servants, As food for the birds of the heavens, The flesh of thy men of lovingkindness, Unto the wild beast of the earth:
texts.psa.79.3: They have poured out their blood like water, Round about Jerusalem, With none to bury.
texts.psa.79.4: We have become, A reproach to our neighbours,—A mockery and a derision, to them who are round about us.
texts.psa.79.5: How long, O Yahweh, wilt thou be angry utterly? Shall thy jealousy, burn like fire?
texts.psa.79.6: Pour out thy wrath, Upon the nations that have not known thee—and, Upon the kingdoms that, on thy Name, have not called.
texts.psa.79.7: For he hath devoured Jacob,—And, his dwelling-place, have they laid waste.
texts.psa.79.8: Do not remember against us former iniquities,—Haste thee, let thy compassions, come to meet us, For we have been brought very low!
texts.psa.79.9: Help us, O God of our salvation, on account of the glory of thy Name,—Rescue us then, and put a propitiatory-covering over our sins, For the sake of thy Name.
texts.psa.79.10: Wherefore should the nations say—Where is their God? Let him be known among the nations before our eyes! [Yea! By] the avenging of the blood of thy servants which hath been shed!
texts.psa.79.11: Let the groaning of the prisoner, come in before thee,—According to the greatness of thine arm, Set free them who are appointed to death.
texts.psa.79.12: Return, therefore, unto our neighbours—Sevenfold, into their own bosom, The reproach wherewith they have reproached thee, O Adonay!
texts.psa.79.13: So, we, thy people, and the sheep of thy pasture, will give thanks unto thee, to times age-abiding,—To generation after generation, will we recount thy praise.
texts.psa.80.1: O Shepherd of Israel, give ear, Thou who leddest forth Joseph like a rock, Thou who art throned on the cherubim, appear!
texts.psa.80.2: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up thy strength, And come! to our salvation.
texts.psa.80.3: O God, bring us back, And light up thy face, That we may be saved.
texts.psa.80.4: O Yahweh, God of hosts! How long hast thou been wroth with the prayer of thy people?
texts.psa.80.5: Thou hast fed them with the food of tears, And hast caused them to drink the water of weeping in threefold abundance.
texts.psa.80.6: Thou dost make us an object of contention to our neighbours, And, our foes, find mockery for themselves.
texts.psa.80.7: O God of hosts, bring us back, And light up thy face, That we may be saved.
texts.psa.80.8: A vine out of Egypt, thou didst remove, Thou didst cast out nations, and plant it;
texts.psa.80.9: Thou didst make a clear space before it, So it rooted well its roots, and filled up the land;
texts.psa.80.10: Covered were the mountains with its shade, And, with its boughs, the mighty cedars.
texts.psa.80.11: It thrust forth its branches as far as the sea,—And, unto the River, its shoots.
texts.psa.80.12: Wherefore hast thou broken down its fences, So that all who pass along the way, pluck its fruit?
texts.psa.80.13: The boar out of the forest, browseth upon it, And, the wild beast of the field, pastureth thereon.
texts.psa.80.14: O God of hosts, return, we pray thee,—Look down out of the heavens, and see, And inspect this vine:
texts.psa.80.15: Yea the stock which thy right hand planted, Even upon the son thou didst secure for thyself.
texts.psa.80.16: To be burned with fire, it is cut down,—At the rebuke of thy countenance, they will perish.
texts.psa.80.17: Let thy hand be, Upon the Man of thy right hand, Upon the Son of Man thou didst secure for thyself;
texts.psa.80.18: So will we not draw back from thee, Thou wilt bring us to life, And, on thy Name, will we call.
texts.psa.80.19: O Yahweh, God of hosts! bring us back, Light up thy face, That we may be saved.
texts.psa.81.1: Shout ye for joy, unto God our strength, Sound the note of triumph, to the God of Jacob;
texts.psa.81.2: Raise a melody, and strike the timbrel, The lyre so sweet, with the harp:
texts.psa.81.3: Blow, at the new moon, the horn, At the full moon, for the day of our sacred festival:
texts.psa.81.4: For, a statute to Israel, it is, A regulation, by the God of Jacob;
texts.psa.81.5: A testimony in Joseph, he appointed it, When he went forth over the land of Egypt: A language I liked not, used I to hear;
texts.psa.81.6: I took away, from the burden, his shoulder, his hands, from the clay, were set free.
texts.psa.81.7: In distress, thou didst cry, and I delivered thee,—I answered thee, within a hiding-place of thunder, I proved thee by the waters of Meribah. [Selah.]
texts.psa.81.8: Hear, O my people, and I will adjure thee, O Israel, if thou wilt hearken unto me!
texts.psa.81.9: There shall not be, within thee, a foreign GOD,—Neither shalt thou bow down to a strange GOD:
texts.psa.81.10: I, Yahweh, am thy God, Who brought thee up out of the land of Egypt,—Open wide thy mouth, that I may fill it.
texts.psa.81.11: But my people, hearkened not, unto my voice, Even, Israel, inclined not unto me.
texts.psa.81.12: So then I let them go on in the stubbornness of their own heart,[—] They might walk in their own counsels!
texts.psa.81.13: If, my people, were hearkening unto me, [If,] Israel, in my ways, would walk,
texts.psa.81.14: Right soon, their foes, would I subdue, And, against their adversaries, would I turn my hand:
texts.psa.81.15: The haters of Yahweh, should come cringing unto him, Then let their own good time be age-abiding!
texts.psa.81.16: Then would he feed them from the marrow of the wheat, Yea, out of the rock—with honey, would I satisfy thee.
texts.psa.82.1: God, hath taken his place in the august assembly, In the midst of the gods, will he judge.
texts.psa.82.2: How long will ye judge perversely, And, the countenances of the lawless, uplift? [Selah.]
texts.psa.82.3: Vindicate the weak and the fatherless, The oppressed and the poor, see righted;
texts.psa.82.4: Deliver the weak and the needy, Out of the hand of the lawless, make rescue.
texts.psa.82.5: They know not, neither can they perceive, In darkness, they wander, All the foundations of the earth do shake.
texts.psa.82.6: I, said, Gods, ye are, Yea, sons of the Highest, are ye all;
texts.psa.82.7: But indeed, like the earth-born, shall ye die! And, like one of the princes, shall ye fall!
texts.psa.82.8: Arise! O God, judge thou the earth, For, thou, wilt inherit all the nations.
texts.psa.83.1: O God, Do not keep quiet, Do not hold thy peace, Neither be thou still, O GOD!
texts.psa.83.2: For lo! thine enemies, are tumultuous, And, they who hate thee, have lifted up the head;
texts.psa.83.3: Against thy people, they craftily devise a secret plot, And conspire against thy treasured ones.
texts.psa.83.4: They have said—Come, and let us wipe them out from being a nation, That the name of Israel may be remembered no more.
texts.psa.83.5: For they have taken counsel with one heart, Against thee—a covenant, would they solemnize—
texts.psa.83.6: The tents of Edom, and the Ishmaelites, of Moab and the Hagarenes;
texts.psa.83.7: Gebal and Ammon, and Amalek, The Philistines, with the dwellers in Tyre;
texts.psa.83.8: Even Assyria hath joined herself with them, They have become an arm to the sons of Lot. [Selah.]
texts.psa.83.9: Make them like Midian, like Sisera, like Jabin, by the torrent of Kishon;
texts.psa.83.10: They perished at En-dor, They become manure for the soil!
texts.psa.83.11: Make them—their nobles—like Oreb and like Zeeb, And, like Zebah and like Zalmunna, all their princes:
texts.psa.83.12: Who said—Let us take a possession for ourselves, The pastures of God!
texts.psa.83.13: O my God, make them, As whirling [dust], As chaff before a wind;
texts.psa.83.14: As a fire burneth a forest,—And as a flame setteth mountains ablaze,
texts.psa.83.15: So, wilt thou pursue them with thy tempest,—And, with thy storm-wind, wilt terrify them:
texts.psa.83.16: Fill thou their faces with dishonour, That men may seek thy Name, O Yahweh;
texts.psa.83.17: Let them turn pale, and be terrified to futurity, Yea let them blush, and perish:
texts.psa.83.18: That men may know that, thou, Whose Name alone is Yahweh, Art Most High over all the earth.
texts.psa.84.1: How lovely are thy habitations, O Yahweh of hosts!
texts.psa.84.2: My soul, longeth—yea even languisheth—for the courts of Yahweh,—My heart and my flesh, shout aloud for a Living GOD.
texts.psa.84.3: Even the sparrow, hath found a home, And, the swallow, a nest for herself, where she hath laid her young, Thine altars, O Yahweh of hosts, My king and my God!
texts.psa.84.4: How happy are they who abide in thy house,—Still are they praising thee. [Selah.]
texts.psa.84.5: How happy the men whose strength is in thee, Festive processions are in their heart.
texts.psa.84.6: Passing through the balsam-vale, A place of fountains, they make it, Yea, with blessings, is it covered by the early rain.
texts.psa.84.7: They go from strength to strength, Each one appeareth before God in Zion.
texts.psa.84.8: O Yahweh, God of hosts, hear thou my prayer,—Give hear, thou God of Jacob. [Selah.]
texts.psa.84.9: Our Shield, behold thou, O God, And look upon the face of thine Anointed One.
texts.psa.84.10: For better is a day in thy courts, than a thousand, I choose rather to stand at the threshold in the house of my God, Than to dwell in the tents of lawlessness.
texts.psa.84.11: For, a sun and shield, is Yahweh God,—Grace and glory, will Yahweh give, He will not withhold what is good, from them who walk without blame.
texts.psa.84.12: O Yahweh of hosts! How happy the man who trusteth in thee!
texts.psa.85.1: Thou hast accepted, O Yahweh, thy land, Thou hast brought back the captives of Jacob;
texts.psa.85.2: Thou hast taken away, the iniquity of thy people, Thou hast covered, all their sin. [Selah.]
texts.psa.85.3: Thou hast withdrawn all thine indignation, Thou hast ceased from the glow of thine anger.
texts.psa.85.4: Restore us, O God of our salvation, And take away thy vexation towards us.
texts.psa.85.5: To times age-abiding, wilt thou be angry with us? Wilt thou prolong thine anger, from generation to generation?
texts.psa.85.6: Wilt not, thou thyself, again give us life, That, thy people, may rejoice in thee.
texts.psa.85.7: Show us, O Yahweh, thy lovingkindness, And, thy salvation, wilt thou grant us.
texts.psa.85.8: I will hear, what GOD—Yahweh—will speak,—For he will bespeak prosperity to his people, And to his men of lovingkindness, And to them who return with their heart unto him.
texts.psa.85.9: Surely, near unto them who revere him, is his salvation, That the Glory, may settle down, in our land.
texts.psa.85.10: Lovingkindness and faithfulness, have met together, Righteousness and prosperity, have kissed each other;
texts.psa.85.11: Faithfulness, out of the earth, doth spring forth, And, righteousness, out of the heavens, hath looked down.
texts.psa.85.12: Yahweh himself too, will give us the blessing, And, our land, shall yield her increase.
texts.psa.85.13: Righteousness, before him, shall march long,—That he may make, into a way, the steps of its feet.
texts.psa.86.1: Bow down, O Yahweh, thine ear—answer me, For, oppressed and needy, am I;
texts.psa.86.2: O guard my life, For, a man of lovingkindness, am I,—Save thy servant, O thou my God, [Thy servant] who trusteth in thee;
texts.psa.86.3: Show me favour, O My Lord, For, unto thee, do I cry, all the day;
texts.psa.86.4: Rejoice the soul of thy servant, For, unto thee, O My Lord, my soul, do I lift.
texts.psa.86.5: For, thou, O My Lord, art good and forgiving, And abundant in lovingkindness, to all who call upon thee.
texts.psa.86.6: Give ear, O Yahweh, unto my prayer, And attend unto the voice of my supplications.
texts.psa.86.7: In the day of my distress, will I call upon thee, For thou wilt answer me.
texts.psa.86.8: There is none like unto thee, among the gods, O My Lord, And nothing like thy works.
texts.psa.86.9: All nations whom thou hast made, Shall come in and bow down before thee, O My Lord, That they may glorify thy Name.
texts.psa.86.10: For great thou art, and doest wondrous things, Thou, O God, of thyself alone.
texts.psa.86.11: Point out to me, O Yahweh, thy way, I will walk steadfastly in thy truth, My heart will rejoice to revere thy Name.
texts.psa.86.12: I will give thee thanks, Adonay, my God, with all my heart, And will glorify thy Name unto times age-abiding.
texts.psa.86.13: For, thy lovingkindness, is great towards me, And thou hast rescued my soul from Hades beneath.
texts.psa.86.14: O God, the insolent, have arisen against me, And, the assembly of tyrants, have sought my life, And have not set thee before them.
texts.psa.86.15: But, thou, O My Lord, art, A God of compassion and favour, Slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness a faithfulness.
texts.psa.86.16: Turn thou unto me, and show me favour,—Give thy strength to thy servant, And save the son of thy handmaid.
texts.psa.86.17: Perform with me a token for good,—That they who hate me may see and be ashamed, In that, thou, Yahweh, hast helped me and comforted me.
texts.psa.87.1: His foundation, is in the holy mountains:
texts.psa.87.2: Yahweh loveth the gates of Zion, More than all the dwellings of Jacob.
texts.psa.87.3: Glorious things, are to be spoken of thee, O city of God. [Selah.]
texts.psa.87.4: I will mention Rahab and Babylon, to them who know me—Lo! Philistia and Tyre with Ethiopia, This one was born there.
texts.psa.87.5: But, of Zion, it shall be said—This man and that were born in her, And the Highest himself shall establish her.
texts.psa.87.6: Yahweh, will record, when he enrolleth the peoples, This one was born there. [Selah.]
texts.psa.87.7: As well the singers as the flute-players [are saying],—All my springs, are in thee!
texts.psa.88.1: O Yahweh, God of my salvation, By day, have I made outcry, In the night, [also] before thee.
texts.psa.88.2: Let my prayer, come into thy presence, Bow down thine ear to my loud cry.
texts.psa.88.3: For my soul, is sated with misfortunes, And, my life—unto Hades, hath drawn near;
texts.psa.88.4: I am counted with them who descend into the pit, I have become as a man that is without help;
texts.psa.88.5: Among the dead, is my couch,—Like the slain that lie in the grave, Where thou rememberest them no more, Yea, they, from thy hand, are cut off;
texts.psa.88.6: Thou hast laid me, In the lowest pit, In dark places, In the deeps:
texts.psa.88.7: Upon me, hath rested thine indignation, And, with all thy breakers, hast thou caused affliction. [Selah.]
texts.psa.88.8: Thou hast far removed mine acquaintances from me,—Thou hast made me an abomination unto them, Shut up, and I cannot go forth!
texts.psa.88.9: Mine eye, hath dimmed through affliction; I have called upon thee, O Yahweh, all day long, I have spread out, unto thee, my hands.
texts.psa.88.10: For the dead, wilt thou perform a wonder? Or shall, the shades, arising, give thee thanks? [Selah.]
texts.psa.88.11: Shall Thy lovingkindness be recounted in the grave? Thy faithfulness, in destruction?
texts.psa.88.12: Shall any wonder of thine, be known in the dark? Or, thy righteousness, in the land of forgetfulness?
texts.psa.88.13: But, I, unto thee, O Yahweh, have cried for help, And, in the morning, my prayer will confront thee!
texts.psa.88.14: Wherefore, O Yahweh, shouldst thou reject my soul? shouldst thou hide thy face from me?
texts.psa.88.15: Afflicted have I been, and dying, from youth, I have borne the terror of thee—I shall be distracted!
texts.psa.88.16: Over me, have passed thy bursts of burning anger, The alarms of thee have put an end to me;
texts.psa.88.17: They have surrounded me like waters, all the day, They have come circling against me together:
texts.psa.88.18: Thou hast far removed from me, lover and friend, Mine acquaintances, are in darkness.
texts.psa.89.1: The lovingkindnesses of Yahweh, age-abidingly will I sing, To generation after generation, will I make known thy faithfulness with my mouth.
texts.psa.89.2: For I said, To times age-abiding, shall lovingkindness be built up, As for the heavens, thou wilt establish thy faithfulness therein.
texts.psa.89.3: I have solemnised a covenant, for my chosen one, I have sworn unto David my servant:
texts.psa.89.4: Unto times age-abiding, will I establish thy seed, And will build up, unto generation after generation, thy throne. [Selah.]
texts.psa.89.5: So shall the heavens praise thy wondrousness, O Yahweh,—Yea, thy faithfulness, in the convocation of holy ones.
texts.psa.89.6: For whom, in the skies, can one compare unto Yahweh? [Or] can one liken unto Yahweh, among the sons of the mighty?
texts.psa.89.7: A GOD inspiring awe in the circle of the holy ones, exceedingly, And to be reverenced above all who are round about him.
texts.psa.89.8: O Yahweh, God of hosts! Who, like thee, is mighty, O Yah! With thy faithfulness round about thee:
texts.psa.89.9: Thou, rulest over the swelling of the sea, When the rolling waves thereof lift themselves, Thou, dost bid them be still:
texts.psa.89.10: Thou, hast crushed—as one slain—Rahab, With thy strong arm, hast thou scattered thy foes.
texts.psa.89.11: Thine, are the heavens, Yea, thine, the earth, The world and the fulness thereof, Thou, didst found them;
texts.psa.89.12: The north and the south, Thou, didst create them,—Tabor and Hermon, with thy Name, shall shout for joy:
texts.psa.89.13: Thine is an arm with might, Strong is thy hand, High is thy right hand;
texts.psa.89.14: Righteousness and justice, are the establishing of thy throne, Lovingkindness and faithfulness, go before thy face.
texts.psa.89.15: How happy are the people who know the joyful sound! O Yahweh! in the light of thy countenance, shall they firmly march along;
texts.psa.89.16: In thy Name, shall they exult all the day, And, in thy righteousness, shall they be exalted.
texts.psa.89.17: For, the beauty of their strength, thou art, And, in thine acceptance, shall our horns be exalted.
texts.psa.89.18: For, to Yahweh, belongeth our Shield, And, to the Holy One of Israel, belongeth our King.
texts.psa.89.19: Then spakest thou in vision of thy men of lovingkindness, and saidst—I have laid help upon a mighty one, I have exalted one chosen from among the people;
texts.psa.89.20: I have found David my servant, With mine own holy oil, have I anointed him;
texts.psa.89.21: With whom my hand shall be firm, Yea, mine arm, shall strengthen him;
texts.psa.89.22: No foe shall make exactions on him, Nor shall, a son of perversity, humiliate him;
texts.psa.89.23: And I will shatter, from before him, his adversaries, And, them who hate him, will I smite;
texts.psa.89.24: And, my faithfulness and my lovingkindness, shall be with him, And, in my Name, exalted shall be his horn;
texts.psa.89.25: And I will set, in the sea, his hand, And, in the rivers, his right hand;
texts.psa.89.26: He, shall cry out unto me, My Father, thou art, My GOD, and my Rock of Salvation!
texts.psa.89.27: Yea, I, will appoint him, firstborn, Most High to the kings of the earth!
texts.psa.89.28: Age-abidingly, will I keep for him my lovingkindness, And, my covenant, hath been made steadfast for him;
texts.psa.89.29: Therefore will I appoint, to futurity, his seed, And his throne as the days of the heavens.
texts.psa.89.30: If his sons forsake my law, And, in my regulations, do not walk;
texts.psa.89.31: If, my statutes, they profane, And, my commandments, do not keep:
texts.psa.89.32: Then will I punish, with a rod, their transgression; And, with stripes, their iniquity:
texts.psa.89.33: But, my lovingkindness, will I not frustrate from them, Neither will I falsify my faithfulness;
texts.psa.89.34: I will not violate my covenant, And that which hath proceeded out of my lips, will I not alter:
texts.psa.89.35: One thing, have I sworn by my holiness, Verily, to David, will I not lie;
texts.psa.89.36: His seed, age-abidingly, shall remain, And, his throne, be like the sun before me;
texts.psa.89.37: Like the moon, shall it be established unto times age-abiding, And, a witness, in the skies, hath been made sure. [Selah.]
texts.psa.89.38: Yet, thou thyself, hast cast off, and rejected, Thou hast been wroth with thine Anointed One!
texts.psa.89.39: Thou hast cast down the covenant of thy Servant, Thou hast profaned, to the earth, his crown;
texts.psa.89.40: Thou hast broken down all his defenses, Thou hast laid his fortresses in ruins;
texts.psa.89.41: All the passers by the way, have plundered him, He hath become a reproach to his neighbours;
texts.psa.89.42: Thou hast raised the right hand of his adversaries, Thou hast gladdened all his enemies;
texts.psa.89.43: Yea thou hast turned the edge of his sword, Neither hast thou caused him to stand in the battle;
texts.psa.89.44: Thou hast brought to an end his splendour, And, his throne—to the ground, hast thou hurled;
texts.psa.89.45: Thou hast shortened the days of his youths,—Thou hast covered him with shame. [Selah.]
texts.psa.89.46: How long, O Yahweh, Wilt thou hide thyself utterly? Shall thine indignation, burn like fire?
texts.psa.89.47: Remember how short-lived, I, am, Wherefore, in vain, hast thou created all the sons of Adam?
texts.psa.89.48: Who is the man that shall live, and not see death? That can deliver his soul from the hand of hades. [Selah.]
texts.psa.89.49: Where are thy former lovingkindnesses, O My Lord? Thou didst swear unto David, in thy faithfulness!
texts.psa.89.50: Remember, O My Lord, the reproach of thy servants, I have carried in my bosom the insult of the peoples:
texts.psa.89.51: In that thy foes have reproached, O Yahweh, In that they have reproached the footsteps of thine Anointed One!
texts.psa.89.52: Blessed be Yahweh to times age-abiding, Amen, and Amen!
texts.psa.90.1: Lord! a dwelling-place, hast, thou, become to us, From generation to generation:
texts.psa.90.2: Before, the mountains, were born, Or thou hadst brought forth the earth and the world, Even, from age to age, thou, [wast] GOD.
texts.psa.90.3: Thou causest man to return unto dust, And hast said—Return, ye sons of Adam!
texts.psa.90.4: For, a thousand years, in thine eyes, [are], As yesterday, in that it passed away, Or [as] a watch in the night.
texts.psa.90.5: Thou hast snatched them away, A sleep, do they become, In the morning, [they are] like grass that shooteth up,
texts.psa.90.6: In the morning, it sprouteth and shooteth up, By the evening, it is cut down and withered.
texts.psa.90.7: For we are consumed in thine anger, And, in thy wrath, are we dismayed;
texts.psa.90.8: Thou hast set, Our iniquities before thee, Our secret near the luminary of thy face.
texts.psa.90.9: For, all our days, decline in thy wrath,—We end our years like a sigh.
texts.psa.90.10: The days of our years, have, in them, three score years and ten, And, if, by reason of strength, they have fourscore years, Yet, their boast, is labour and sorrow, For it hath passed quickly, and we have flown away.
texts.psa.90.11: Who knoweth the strength of thine anger? Even, according to the fear of thee, is thy wrath!
texts.psa.90.12: How to number our days, so grant us to know, That we may win us a heart that hath wisdom.
texts.psa.90.13: Return, Yahweh, oh how long? And have compassion upon thy servants;
texts.psa.90.14: Satisfy us, in the morning, with thy lovingkindness, That we may shout aloud and be glad, Throughout all our days.
texts.psa.90.15: Make us glad, according to, The days thou hast humbled us, The years we have seen misfortune:
texts.psa.90.16: Let thy work, appear unto thy servants, And, thy majesty, upon their children;
texts.psa.90.17: And let the delightfulness of Adonay our God be upon us,—And, the work of our hands, establish thou upon us, Yea, the work of our hands, establish thou it.
texts.psa.91.1: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the Most High, Under the shadow of the Almighty, will tarry,
texts.psa.91.2: Saying of Yahweh—My refuge and my fortress, My God, in whom I will trust.
texts.psa.91.3: For, he, will rescue thee, From the snare of the fowler, From the destructive pestilence.
texts.psa.91.4: With his pinion, will he cover thee, And, under his wings, shalt thou seek refuge, A shield and buckler, is his faithfulness.
texts.psa.91.5: Thou shalt not be afraid, Of the dread of the night, Of the arrow that flieth by day;
texts.psa.91.6: Of the pestilence that, in darkness, doth walk, Of the plague that layeth waste at noonday.
texts.psa.91.7: There shall fall, at thy side, a thousand, Yea, myriads, at thy right hand, Unto thee, shall it not come nigh;
texts.psa.91.8: Save only, with thine own eyes, shalt thou discern, And, the recompense of the lawless, shalt thou see.
texts.psa.91.9: Because, thou, [hast made] Yahweh, my refuge,—The Most High, thou hast made thy dwelling-place,
texts.psa.91.10: There shall not be sent unto thee misfortune, Nor shall, plague, come near into thy tent;
texts.psa.91.11: For, his messengers, will he charge concerning thee, To keep thee, in all thy ways;
texts.psa.91.12: On hands, will they bear thee up, Lest thou strike, against a stone, thy foot;
texts.psa.91.13: On the lion and adder, shalt thou tread, Shalt trample on young lion and crocodile.
texts.psa.91.14: Because, on me, he hath set firm his love, Therefore will I deliver him, I will set him on high, Because he hath known my Name;
texts.psa.91.15: He shall call me, and I will answer him, With him, will, I, be, in distress, I will rescue him, and will honour him;
texts.psa.91.16: With length of days, will I satisfy him, And will show him my salvation.
texts.psa.92.1: It is good to give thanks to Yahweh, And to sing praises unto thy Name, O Most High;
texts.psa.92.2: To declare, in the morning, thy lovingkindness, And thy faithfulness at night;
texts.psa.92.3: Upon an instrument of ten strings, and upon a harp, With resounding music on the lyre.
texts.psa.92.4: For thou hast made me glad, O Yahweh, in thy doing, In the works of thy hands, will I shout for joy.
texts.psa.92.5: How great have grown thy works, Yahweh, [How] very deep are laid thy plans!
texts.psa.92.6: A man that is brutish, cannot know, And, a dullard, cannot discern this:—
texts.psa.92.7: When the lawless do thrive like grass, And all the workers of iniquity have blossomed, It is that they may be destroyed for ever.
texts.psa.92.8: But, thou, shalt be on high age-abidingly, O Yahweh.
texts.psa.92.9: For lo! thine enemies, Yahweh, For lo! thine enemies, shall perish, They shall be scattered—all the workers of iniquity;
texts.psa.92.10: But thou wilt exalt, as [those of] the buffalo, my horn, I have been anointed, with fresh oil.
texts.psa.92.11: So hath mine eye descried them who were lying in wait for me,—Of my wicked assailants, mine ears, shall hear.
texts.psa.92.12: The righteous, like the palm-tree, shall thrive, Like the cedar in Lebanon, shall he grow;
texts.psa.92.13: They who are planted in the house of Yahweh, In the courts of our God, shall flourish;
texts.psa.92.14: Still shall they bear fruit in old age, Vigorous and fresh, shall they be:
texts.psa.92.15: To declare that upright is Yahweh, My Rock, and no perversity in him.
texts.psa.93.1: Yahweh, hath become king, With majesty, is he clothed,—Clothed is Yahweh, With strength, hath he girded himself, Surely he hath fixed the world, It shall not be shaken.
texts.psa.93.2: Established hath been thy throne from of old, From age-past times, thou art.
texts.psa.93.3: The floods have lifted up, O Yahweh, The floods have lifted up—their voice, The floods have lifted up—their dashing waves.
texts.psa.93.4: With the sounds of many waters, Majestic are the breakers of the sea, Majestic on high, is Yahweh.
texts.psa.93.5: Thy testimonies, are strongly confirmed, To thy house, befitting is holiness, O Yahweh—to length of days.
texts.psa.94.1: O GOD of avenging—Yahweh, GOD of avenging, shine forth:
texts.psa.94.2: Lift up thyself, O judge of the earth, Render a recompense unto the proud.
texts.psa.94.3: How long shall the lawless, O Yahweh, How long shall the lawless exult?
texts.psa.94.4: They pour forth [words], they speak arrogantly, All the workers of iniquity, do boast:
texts.psa.94.5: Thy people, O Yahweh, they will crush, And, thine inheritance, tread down;
texts.psa.94.6: The widow and sojourner, they will slay, And, the fatherless, murder.
texts.psa.94.7: Yet have they said—Yah, doth not see, The God of Jacob, doth not understand.
texts.psa.94.8: Understand, ye brutish among the people, And, ye dullards, when will ye show discretion?
texts.psa.94.9: He that planteth the ear, shall he not hear? Or, that fashioneth the eye, shall he not have power to see?
texts.psa.94.10: He that correcteth nations, shall he not reprove? He that teacheth man knowledge!
texts.psa.94.11: Yahweh, knoweth the plans of men, That, they, are a breath!
texts.psa.94.12: How happy the man whom thou correctest, O Yah! And whom, out of thy law, thou instructest!
texts.psa.94.13: That thou mayest give him rest from the days of misfortune, Until there be digged—for the lawless one—a pit.
texts.psa.94.14: For Yahweh, will not abandon, his people, And, his inheritance, will he not forsake;
texts.psa.94.15: For, unto righteousness, shall the judicial sentence return, Then shall follow it—all the upright in heart.
texts.psa.94.16: Who will rise up for me, against the evil-doers? Who will make a stand for me, against the workers of iniquity?
texts.psa.94.17: If, Yahweh, had not been a help to me, Soon had sunk into silence—my soul!
texts.psa.94.18: If I say, My foot, hath slipped, Thy lovingkindness, O Yahweh, supporteth me.
texts.psa.94.19: In the multitude of my cares within me, Thy consolations, delight my soul.
texts.psa.94.20: Shall the throne that inflicteth ruin, have fellowship with thee, That frameth oppression, by statute?
texts.psa.94.21: They make an attack on the life of the righteous one,—And, innocent blood, they condemn.
texts.psa.94.22: But, Yahweh, hath become for me a high tower, And my God, my rock of refuge.
texts.psa.94.23: Thus hath he brought back on them their iniquity, And, by their own wickedness, will he destroy them, Destroy them, will Yahweh our God.
texts.psa.95.1: Come, let us make a joyful noise to Yahweh, Let us shout in triumph, to the rock of our salvation!
texts.psa.95.2: O let us come before his face with thanksgiving, With the sounds of strings, let us shout aloud to him.
texts.psa.95.3: For, a great GOD, is Yahweh, And a great king, above all gods.
texts.psa.95.4: In whose hand, are the hidden recesses of the earth, And, the peaks of the mountains, are his;
texts.psa.95.5: Whose, is the sea, for, he, made it, And, the dry land, his hands, did form.
texts.psa.95.6: Enter! let us bow down, and bend low, Let us kneel, before Yahweh our maker;
texts.psa.95.7: For, he, is our God, And, we, are the people of his pasture, and the flock of his hand? To-day, if, to his voice, ye will hearken,
texts.psa.95.8: Do not harden your heart as at Meribah, As on the day of Massah, in the desert;
texts.psa.95.9: When your fathers, tested me, They proved me, yea they also saw what I could do.
texts.psa.95.10: Forty years, loathed I that generation, So I said—A people going astray in heart, they are, Even they, have not known my ways!
texts.psa.95.11: And I sware in mine anger,—Verily they shall not enter into my rest.
texts.psa.96.1: Sing to Yahweh, a song that is new, Sing to Yahweh, all the earth;
texts.psa.96.2: Sing to Yahweh, bless ye his Name,—Tell the tidings, from day to day, of his salvation:
texts.psa.96.3: Recount, Among the nations, his glory, Among all the peoples, his wonders.
texts.psa.96.4: For great is Yahweh, and worthy to be mightily praised, To be revered is he above all gods;
texts.psa.96.5: For, all the gods of the peoples, are things of nought—But, Yahweh, made, the heavens.
texts.psa.96.6: Praise and majesty, are before him, Strength and beauty, are in his sanctuary.
texts.psa.96.7: Give to Yahweh, ye families of the peoples, Give to Yahweh, glory and strength;
texts.psa.96.8: Give to Yahweh, the glory of his Name, Bring a present, and enter his courts;
texts.psa.96.9: Bow down to Yahweh, in the adornment of holiness, Be in anguish at his presence, all the earth!
texts.psa.96.10: Say among the nations, Yahweh, hath become King, Surely he hath fixed the world, it shall not be shaken, He will judge the peoples with equity.
texts.psa.96.11: Let the heavens rejoice, and the earth exult, Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof;
texts.psa.96.12: Let the field, leap for joy, and all that is therein, Then, shall all the trees of the forest, shout in triumph,
texts.psa.96.13: Before Yahweh, for he is coming, For he is coming to judge the earth,—He will judge the world, in righteousness, And the peoples, in his faithfulness.
texts.psa.97.1: Yahweh, hath become king, Let the earth exult, Let the multitude of coastlands rejoice.
texts.psa.97.2: Clouds and thick darkness, are round about him, Righteousness and justice, are the establishing of his throne.
texts.psa.97.3: Fire, before him, proceedeth, That it may consume, round about, his adversaries.
texts.psa.97.4: His lightnings, have illumined, the world, The earth, hath seen, and hath trembled;
texts.psa.97.5: The mountains, like wax, have melted, At the presence of Yahweh, At the presence, of the Lord of all the earth.
texts.psa.97.6: The heavens, have declared, his righteousness,—And all the peoples, have seen, his glory.
texts.psa.97.7: Let all who serve an image, be ashamed, They who boast themselves in things of nought, Bow down unto him, all ye gods.
texts.psa.97.8: Zion, hath heard and rejoiced, And the daughters of Judah, have exulted, Because of thy righteous decisions, O Yahweh:
texts.psa.97.9: For, thou, Yahweh, art Most High over all the earth, Greatly hast thou exalted thyself above all gods.
texts.psa.97.10: Ye lovers of Yahweh! be haters of wrong,—He preserveth the lives of his men of lovingkindness, From the hand of the lawless, will he rescue them.
texts.psa.97.11: Light, is sown for the righteous one, And, for the upright in heart, rejoicing:
texts.psa.97.12: Rejoice, ye righteous, in Yahweh, And give ye thanks, at the mention of his holiness.
texts.psa.98.1: Sing to Yahweh, a song that is new, For, wonderful things, hath he done, His own right hand and his holy arm, have brought him salvation.
texts.psa.98.2: Yahweh, hath made known, his salvation, Before the eyes of the nations, hath he revealed his righteousness;
texts.psa.98.3: He hath remembered his lovingkindness and his faithfulness towards the house of Israel,—All the ends of the earth, have seen, the salvation of our God.
texts.psa.98.4: Shout aloud to Yahweh, all the earth, Break forth and make a joyful noise and sweep the strings;
texts.psa.98.5: Sweep the strings to Yahweh, With the lyre, With the lyre, and the voice of melody;
texts.psa.98.6: With trumpets and the sound of a horn, Shout aloud, before the king—Yahweh.
texts.psa.98.7: Let the sea, roar, and the fulness thereof, The world, and they who dwell therein;
texts.psa.98.8: Let, the floods, clap their hands, Together, let, the mountains, make a joyful noise,
texts.psa.98.9: Before Yahweh, for he is coming—to judge the earth,—He will judge the world, in righteousness, And the peoples, with equity.
texts.psa.99.1: Yahweh, hath become king, Let the peoples, tremble, He is enthroned on the cherubim, Let the earth, shake.
texts.psa.99.2: Yahweh, in Zion, is great, And, high, is he over all the peoples.
texts.psa.99.3: Let them thank his Name—great and reverend, Holy, is he!
texts.psa.99.4: Yea, with the strength of a king—justice, he loveth,—Thou, hast established equity, Justice and righteousness in Jacob, thou, hast wrought.
texts.psa.99.5: Exalt Yahweh our God, And bow down at his footstool, Holy, is he!
texts.psa.99.6: Moses and Aaron, [were] among his priests, And, Samuel, [was] among them who were calling upon his Name, Who were calling upon Yahweh, and, he, used to answer them:
texts.psa.99.7: In the pillar of cloud, used he to speak unto them, They kept his testimonies, and the statute he gave them.
texts.psa.99.8: O Yahweh our God! thou, answeredst them,—A pardoning GOD, thou becamest to them, Yet one bringing vengeance on their deeds.
texts.psa.99.9: Exalt Yahweh our God, And bow down towards his holy mountain, For, holy, is Yahweh our God.
texts.psa.100.1: Make a joyful noise to Yahweh, all the earth:
texts.psa.100.2: Serve Yahweh with rejoicing, Enter before him, with shouts of triumph.
texts.psa.100.3: Know that, Yahweh, he, is God,—He, made us, and not, we ourselves, His people, and the flock of his pasture.
texts.psa.100.4: Enter ye his gates, with thanksgiving, his courts, with praise, Give ye thanks to him, bless ye his Name;
texts.psa.100.5: For good is Yahweh, Age-abiding is his lovingkindness, And, unto generation after generation, his faithfulness.
texts.psa.101.1: Of lovingkindness and of justice, will I sing! Unto thee, O Yahweh, will I touch the strings!
texts.psa.101.2: I will behave myself wisely in a blameless way, When wilt thou come in unto me? I will walk to and fro in the blamelessness of my heart,—in the midst of my house:
texts.psa.101.3: I will not set before mine eyes, a vile thing,—The doing of them who fall away, I hate, It shall not cleave unto me;
texts.psa.101.4: A perverse heart, shall depart from me, A maker of mischief, will I not acknowledge;
texts.psa.101.5: He that uttereth slander in secret against his friend, him, will I root out; One of lofty eyes, and of an ambitious heart, him shall I not be able to endure.
texts.psa.101.6: Mine eyes, shall be upon the faithful of the land, That they may dwell with me,—he that walketh in a blameless way, he, shall attend me.
texts.psa.101.7: There shall not dwell in the midst of my house, One who worketh deceit,—he that speaketh falsehoods, shall not be established before mine eyes;
texts.psa.101.8: Morning by morning, will I uproot, All the lawless ones of the land, That I may cut off, out of the city of Yahweh—All the workers of iniquity.
texts.psa.102.1: O Yahweh, hear thou my prayer, and let, my cry for help, unto thee, enter in.
texts.psa.102.2: Do not hide thy face from me, In the day when I am in distress,—Bend down unto me thine ear, In the day when I call, speedily answer me.
texts.psa.102.3: For, consumed in smoke, are my days, And, my bones, like a burning mass, are scorched through;
texts.psa.102.4: Smitten like herbage, so is my heart dried up, For I have forgotten to eat my food.
texts.psa.102.5: At the noise of my groaning, my bone, hath cleaved, to my flesh:
texts.psa.102.6: I am like the pelican of the desert, I have become as an owl among ruins.
texts.psa.102.7: I have watched and am become, Like a bird sitting alone upon a housetop.
texts.psa.102.8: All the day, have mine enemies, reproached me, And, they who are mad against me, by me, have sworn.
texts.psa.102.9: For, ashes—like bread, have I eaten, And, my drink—with my tears, have I mingled;
texts.psa.102.10: Because of thine indignation and thy wrath, For thou hast lifted me up, and cast me down.
texts.psa.102.11: My days, are like a shadow extended, And, I, as green herbage, do wither.
texts.psa.102.12: But, thou, O Yahweh, age-abidingly wilt remain, And the memorial of thee, to generation after generation.
texts.psa.102.13: Thou, wilt arise, wilt have compassion upon Zion, Surely it is time to favour her, Surely the time appointed, hath come;
texts.psa.102.14: Seeing that thy servants, take pleasure, in her stones, And, her dust, they favour:
texts.psa.102.15: That the nations may revere thy Name, O Yahweh, And all the kings of the earth, thy glory.
texts.psa.102.16: When Yahweh, hath built up, Zion, Hath appeared in his glory;
texts.psa.102.17: Hath turned towards the prayer of the destitute, And not despised their prayer,
texts.psa.102.18: This, shall be written, for a later generation, And, a people to be created, will give praise unto Yah:—
texts.psa.102.19: That he looked down, out of his holy height, Yahweh, from the heavens unto the earth, directed his gaze;—
texts.psa.102.20: To hear the groaning of the prisoner, To set free, them who were appointed to death.
texts.psa.102.21: To the end the Name of Yahweh, might be celebrated in Zion, And his praise in Jerusalem:
texts.psa.102.22: When the peoples, gather themselves together, And the kingdoms, to serve Yahweh.
texts.psa.102.23: He hath prostrated, in the way, my strength,—He hath shortened my days.
texts.psa.102.24: I said, O my GOD, do not remove me in the midst of my days, Throughout the generation of generations, are thy years;
texts.psa.102.25: Of old—the earth, thou didst found, And, the work of thy hands, are the heavens;
texts.psa.102.26: They, shall perish, But, thou, wilt abide; And, they all, like a garment, shall fall in pieces, As a vesture, wilt thou change them and they shall vanish;
texts.psa.102.27: But, thou, art, the same,—And, thy years, shall have no end:
texts.psa.102.28: The children of thy servants, shall continue,—And, their seed, before thee, be established.
texts.psa.103.1: Bless, O my soul, Yahweh,—And all that is within me, his holy Name;
texts.psa.103.2: Bless, O my soul, Yahweh, And forget not all his dealings:—
texts.psa.103.3: Who forgiveth all thine iniquity, Who healeth all thy diseases;
texts.psa.103.4: Who redeemeth, from destruction, thy life, Who crowneth thee, with lovingkindness and compassion:
texts.psa.103.5: Who satisfieth, with good, thine age, Thy youth, reneweth itself like an eagle.
texts.psa.103.6: Yahweh is one, who executeth righteousness, Yea vindication for all the oppressed.
texts.psa.103.7: Who made known his ways unto Moses, unto the sons of Israel, his doings.
texts.psa.103.8: Compassionate and gracious, is Yahweh,—Slow to anger and abundant in lovingkindness.
texts.psa.103.9: Not perpetually, will he contend, Nor age-abidingly, retain anger;
texts.psa.103.10: Not according to our sins, hath he dealt with us, Nor according to our iniquities, hath he treated us.
texts.psa.103.11: For, as the heavens are exalted over the earth, His lovingkindness hath prevailed over them who revere him;
texts.psa.103.12: As far as East from West, Hath he put far from us, our transgressions;
texts.psa.103.13: Like the compassion of a father for his children, Is, the compassion of Yahweh, for them who revere him;
texts.psa.103.14: For, he, knoweth how we are formed, He is mindful that, dust, we are.
texts.psa.103.15: As for man, like grass, are his days, Like the blossom of the field, so, doth he blossom;
texts.psa.103.16: For, a wind, hath passed over it, and it is gone, And its own place is acquainted with it no more.
texts.psa.103.17: But, the lovingkindness of Yahweh, is from one age even to another, Upon them who revere him, And his righteousness, to children’s children:—
texts.psa.103.18: To such as keep his covenant, And remember his precepts, to do them.
texts.psa.103.19: Yahweh, in the heavens, hath established his throne, And, his kingdom, over all, hath dominion.
texts.psa.103.20: Bless Yahweh, ye messengers of his,—Heroes of vigour, doing his word, To hearken [again] to the voice of his word;
texts.psa.103.21: Bless Yahweh, all ye his hosts, Attendants of his, doing his pleasure;
texts.psa.103.22: Bless Yahweh, all ye his works, In all places of his dominion, Bless, O my soul, Yahweh.
texts.psa.104.1: Bless, O my soul, Yahweh,—Yahweh, my God, thou art exceedingly great, With honour and majesty, hast thou clothed thyself,
texts.psa.104.2: Putting on light, as a robe, Stretching out the heavens, as a curtain;
texts.psa.104.3: Building, in the waters, his upper chambers,—Who maketh clouds his chariot, Who passeth along on the wings of the wind;
texts.psa.104.4: Making His messengers, winds, His attendants, a flaming fire;
texts.psa.104.5: He hath fixed the earth on its foundations, It is not to be shaken, to times age-abiding and beyond.
texts.psa.104.6: With the resounding deep—as a garment, hast thou covered it, Above the mountains, stand the waters;
texts.psa.104.7: At thy rebuke, they flee, At the voice of thy thunder, they hurry away;
texts.psa.104.8: Mountains rise, Valleys sink, Unto the place which thou hast fixed for them;
texts.psa.104.9: Bounds, hast thou set, which they are not to pass over, They are not to return to cover the earth.
texts.psa.104.10: Who hast sent forth springs, through the torrent-beds, Between the mountains, they flow along;
texts.psa.104.11: They give drink, to every wild beast of the field, The wild asses do break their thirst.
texts.psa.104.12: Over them, the bird of the heavens settleth down, From amidst the foliage, they utter a voice.
texts.psa.104.13: Who watereth the mountains out of his upper chambers, Out of the fruit of thy works, thou satisfiest the earth.
texts.psa.104.14: Who causeth the grass to shoot forth for the cattle, And the herb, for the service of man, That he may bring forth food out of the earth;
texts.psa.104.15: And, wine, may rejoice the heart of man, Making radiant his well-nourished face,—And, food, may, the heart of man, sustain.
texts.psa.104.16: Satisfied are, The trees of Yahweh, The cedars of Lebanon, which he hath planted;
texts.psa.104.17: Where the birds build their nests, The stork, in the fir-trees, hath her house;
texts.psa.104.18: The high mountains, are for the chamois, The crags, are a refuge for the conies.
texts.psa.104.19: He hath made the moon for seasons, And, the sun, knoweth his place for entering in.
texts.psa.104.20: Thou causest darkness, and it becometh night, Therein, creepeth forth, Every wild beast of the forest;
texts.psa.104.21: The young lions, roaring for prey, And seeking, from GOD, their food.
texts.psa.104.22: The sun ariseth, they withdraw themselves, And, in their lairs, lay them down.
texts.psa.104.23: Man goeth forth to his work, And to his labour, until evening.
texts.psa.104.24: How thy works abound, O Yahweh! All of them—in wisdom, hast thou made, The earth is full of thy possession:—
texts.psa.104.25: This sea here, is great and broad on both hands,—Wherein are creeping things, even without number, Living things, small with great;
texts.psa.104.26: There, ships, sail along, This sea-monster, thou hast formed to sport therein;
texts.psa.104.27: All of them, for thee, do wait, That thou mayest give them their food in its season;
texts.psa.104.28: Thou givest unto them, they gather, Thou openest thy hand, they are satisfied with good.
texts.psa.104.29: Thou hidest thy face, they are dismayed, Thou withdrawest their spirit, They cease to breathe, And, unto their own dust, do they return:
texts.psa.104.30: Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created, And thou renewest the face of the ground.
texts.psa.104.31: Be thy glory, O Yahweh, to times age-abiding, Let Yahweh rejoice in his own works:
texts.psa.104.32: Who looketh at the earth, and it trembleth, He toucheth the mountains, and they smoke.
texts.psa.104.33: I will sing to Yahweh, as long as I live! Yea I will touch the strings to my God, while I continue;
texts.psa.104.34: Pleasing unto him, be my meditation, I, will rejoice in Yahweh.
texts.psa.104.35: Sinners shall be consumed out of the earth And, the lawless, no more, shall exist,—Bless, O my soul, Yahweh, Praise ye Yah!
texts.psa.105.1: Give ye thanks to Yahweh, Call upon his Name, Make known, among the peoples, his doings;
texts.psa.105.2: Sing ye to him, Make ye music to him, Speak ye of all his wonders.
texts.psa.105.3: Make your boast in his holy Name, Joyful be the heart of them who are seeking Yahweh.
texts.psa.105.4: Search out Yahweh and his strength, Seek diligently his face at all times.
texts.psa.105.5: Remember his wonders which he hath done, His portents, and the just decisions of his mouth.
texts.psa.105.6: O ye Seed of Abraham—his servants, Sons of Jacob—his chosen ones:
texts.psa.105.7: Yahweh himself, is our God, Through all the land, are his just decision.
texts.psa.105.8: He hath remembered, unto times age-abiding, his covenant, The word he commanded, to a thousand generations;
texts.psa.105.9: Which he solemnised with Abraham, and his oath, to Isaac;
texts.psa.105.10: And confirmed it unto Jacob for a statute, To Israel, as a covenant age-abiding;
texts.psa.105.11: Saying, To thee, will I give the land of Canaan, As your inherited portion;
texts.psa.105.12: While as yet they were men easily counted,—A very few, and sojourners therein;
texts.psa.105.13: And they wandered from nation to nation, From a kingdom, to another people.
texts.psa.105.14: He suffered no son of earth to oppress them, And reproved—for their sakes—[even] kings!
texts.psa.105.15: Ye may not touch mine Anointed ones, And, to my Prophets, may ye do no wrong.
texts.psa.105.16: Then called he a famine over the land, All the staff of bread, he brake;
texts.psa.105.17: He sent before them a man, For a slave, was he sold—[even] Joseph;
texts.psa.105.18: They forced, into a fetter, his foot, Into the iron, entered his soul;
texts.psa.105.19: Until the time when his word came to pass, Speech of Yahweh, proved him;
texts.psa.105.20: The king sent, and set him free, One having dominion over peoples, yet loosed he his bonds;
texts.psa.105.21: He appointed him lord to his household, And one having dominion over all he possessed;
texts.psa.105.22: That he might bind his rulers as he pleased, And, his elders, he might embue with wisdom.
texts.psa.105.23: So Israel came into Egypt, And, Jacob, sojourned in the land of Ham;
texts.psa.105.24: And he made his people exceeding fruitful,—And caused them to become stronger than their adversaries.
texts.psa.105.25: He let them turn their heart—To hate his people, To deal treacherously with his servants;
texts.psa.105.26: He sent Moses his servant, Aaron, whom he had chosen.
texts.psa.105.27: He set among them his threatening signs, And his wonders, in the land of Ham;
texts.psa.105.28: He sent darkness, and made it dark, But they rebelled against his words;
texts.psa.105.29: He turned their waters into blood, And so caused their fish to die;
texts.psa.105.30: Their land swarmed with frogs, In the chambers of their kings!
texts.psa.105.31: He spake, and there came in the gad-fly, Gnats, in all their bounds;
texts.psa.105.32: He made their showers—hail, A fire flaming throughout their land;
texts.psa.105.33: And he smote their vines, and their fig-trees, And brake in pieces the trees of their bounds;
texts.psa.105.34: He spake—then came the swarming locust,—The devouring locust, and that without number;
texts.psa.105.35: And devoured all the herbage in their land, And devoured the fruit of their ground.
texts.psa.105.36: Then smote he every firstborn in their land, The beginning of all their strength;
texts.psa.105.37: Thus brought he them forth, with silver and gold, Nor was there, throughout his tribes, one that faltered;
texts.psa.105.38: Egypt rejoiced when they went out, For the dread of them had fallen upon them.
texts.psa.105.39: He spread out a cloud as a covering, And fire, to give light by night,
texts.psa.105.40: They asked, and he brought in the quail,—And, with the bread of the heavens, he satisfied them;
texts.psa.105.41: He opened the rock, and there gushed forth waters, They flowed along, through parched places, as a river;
texts.psa.105.42: For he remembered his holy word, With Abraham his servant.
texts.psa.105.43: Thus brought he forth his people with gladness,—With shouts of triumph, his chosen ones;
texts.psa.105.44: And gave them, the lands of the nations, And, of the toil of the peoples, took they possession:
texts.psa.105.45: In order that they might observe his statutes, And, over his laws, might keep watch, Praise ye Yah.
texts.psa.106.1: Praise ye Yah, Give ye thanks to Yahweh—For he is good, For age-abiding, is his lovingkindness.
texts.psa.106.2: Who can relate the mighty deeds of Yahweh? can cause to be heard, all his praise?
texts.psa.106.3: How happy! They who observe justice, He that executeth righteousness at all times.
texts.psa.106.4: Remember me, O Yahweh, when thou acceptest thy people, Visit me, with thy salvation;
texts.psa.106.5: That I may look upon the welfare of thy chosen ones, That I may rejoice in the joy of thy nation, That I may glory, with thine inheritance.
texts.psa.106.6: We have sinned—with our fathers, We have acted perversely, we have committed lawlessness;
texts.psa.106.7: Our fathers, in Egypt, understood not thy wonders, They remembered not the abounding of thy lovingkindnesses, but rebelled by the sea—at the Red Sea.
texts.psa.106.8: Yet he saved them, for the sake of his Name, to make known his mighty power;
texts.psa.106.9: So he rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up, And he led them through deeps, as pasture-land;
texts.psa.106.10: And saved them from the hand of one full of hatred, And redeemed them out of the hand of the foe;
texts.psa.106.11: So the waters covered their adversaries, Not one from among them, was left.
texts.psa.106.12: They believed therefore in his words, They sang his praise.
texts.psa.106.13: Soon forgat they his works,—They waited not for his counsel;
texts.psa.106.14: But lusted a lust in the desert, and tested GOD in the waste.
texts.psa.106.15: So he gave them their request, but sent leanness into their soul.
texts.psa.106.16: And they became jealous of Moses in the camp,—of Aaron the holy one of Yahweh;
texts.psa.106.17: The earth opened and engulfed Dathan, and covered up the assembly of Abiram;
texts.psa.106.18: Then was kindled a fire in their assembly,—a flame, consumed the lawless ones.
texts.psa.106.19: They made a calf in Horeb,—and bowed down to a molten image;
texts.psa.106.20: Thus changed they my glory, for the similitude of an ox that eateth grass.
texts.psa.106.21: They forgat GOD their saviour, who had done great things in Egypt:
texts.psa.106.22: Wonders in the land of Ham, Terrible things by the Red Sea.
texts.psa.106.23: Then would he have bidden to destroy them,—had not Moses his chosen, stood in the breach before him, To turn back his wrath from destroying.
texts.psa.106.24: And they refused the delightful land, They believed not his word;
texts.psa.106.25: But murmured in their tents,—They hearkened not unto the voice of Yahweh.
texts.psa.106.26: So he lifted up his hand unto them, that he would let them fall in the desert;
texts.psa.106.27: And would disperse their seed among the nations, and would scatter them throughout the lands.
texts.psa.106.28: Yet they let themselves be bound to Baal-peor,—and did eat sacrifices to the dead:
texts.psa.106.29: So they provoked to anger by their doings, and a plague, made a breach among them.
texts.psa.106.30: Then stood up Phinehas, and interposed, and stayed was the plague:
texts.psa.106.31: So it was counted unto him, for righteousness, To generation after generation, unto times age abiding.
texts.psa.106.32: And they provoked by the waters of Meribah,—And it fared ill with Moses, for their sakes;
texts.psa.106.33: For they embittered his spirit, and he spake rashly with his lips.
texts.psa.106.34: They destroyed not the peoples of which Yahweh had spoken to them;
texts.psa.106.35: But had fellowship with the nations, and learned their doings;
texts.psa.106.36: Yea they served their idols, and they became to them a snare:
texts.psa.106.37: Yea they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to mischievous demons;
texts.psa.106.38: And poured out innocent blood, the blood of their sons and their daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan, And the land was polluted with blood-shed;
texts.psa.106.39: And they became unclean by their works, and became unchaste in their doings.
texts.psa.106.40: Then was kindled the anger of Yahweh with his people, and he abhorred his own inheritance.
texts.psa.106.41: So he delivered them up into the hand of the nations, And they who hated them, had dominion over them;
texts.psa.106.42: And their enemies oppressed them, And they were bowed down under their hand.
texts.psa.106.43: Many times, did he rescue them,—But, they, rebelled by their counsel, and sank low in their iniquity.
texts.psa.106.44: Then looked he on the distress which befell them,—when he heard their loud cry;
texts.psa.106.45: Then remembered he, for them, his covenant, and was moved to pity, according to the abounding of his lovingkindnesses;
texts.psa.106.46: And granted them compassion before all their captors.
texts.psa.106.47: Save us, O Yahweh our God, and gather us from among the nations, That we may give thanks unto thy holy Name, That we may triumph aloud in thy praise.
texts.psa.106.48: Blessed be Yahweh, God of Israel, from one age even unto another, And all the people, shall say, Amen! Praise ye Yah!
texts.psa.107.1: O give thanks to Yahweh—For he is good, For, age-abiding, is his lovingkindness.
texts.psa.107.2: Let the redeemed of Yahweh say, Whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the adversary;
texts.psa.107.3: And, out of the lands, hath gathered them—From the east and from the west, From the north and from the south.
texts.psa.107.4: They wandered about in the desert—in a waste, Way to a city to dwell in, found they none;
texts.psa.107.5: Hungry—yea thirsty, their soul, within them, fainted:
texts.psa.107.6: Then made they outcry to Yahweh, in their peril, Out of their distresses, he rescued them;
texts.psa.107.7: And led them by a straight road, That they might journey to a city to dwell in.
texts.psa.107.8: Let them give thanks to Yahweh for his lovingkindness, and for his wonderful dealings with the sons of men;
texts.psa.107.9: For he hath satisfied the longing soul, and, the famished soul, hath he filled with good.
texts.psa.107.10: The dwellers in darkness and death-shade, bound with oppression and iron;
texts.psa.107.11: Because they had rebelled against the sayings of GOD,—and, the counsel of the Most High, they had spurned;
texts.psa.107.12: And he bowed down, with labour, their heart, They staggered, with no one to help,
texts.psa.107.13: Then made they outcry to Yahweh in their peril, Out of their distresses, he saved them;
texts.psa.107.14: He brought them forth out of darkness and death-shade, and, their fetters, he tare off.
texts.psa.107.15: Let them give thanks to Yahweh for his lovingkindness, and for his wonderful dealings with the sons of men!
texts.psa.107.16: For he brake in pieces the doors of bronze, And, the bars of iron, he hewed asunder.
texts.psa.107.17: The perverse, by reason of their transgression, and on account of their iniquities, are afflicted;
texts.psa.107.18: All manner of food, their soul abhorreth, and so they draw near unto the gates of death,
texts.psa.107.19: Then make they outcry to Yahweh in their peril, and, out of their distresses, he saveth them.
texts.psa.107.20: He sendeth his word, and healeth them, and delivereth them from their graves.
texts.psa.107.21: Let them give thanks to Yahweh for his lovingkindness, and for his wonderful dealings with the sons of men!
texts.psa.107.22: Yea let them sacrifice the sacrifices of thanksgiving, and recount his works with a shout.
texts.psa.107.23: Men who go down to the sea, in ships, doing business through mighty waters;
texts.psa.107.24: They, see the works of Yahweh, and his wonders in the deep;
texts.psa.107.25: And he speaketh, and there ariseth a tempestuous wind, which lifteth on high its rolling waves;
texts.psa.107.26: They mount the heavens, they descend the roaring deeps, their soul, by trouble, dissolveth;
texts.psa.107.27: They reel and stagger, like a drunken man, and, all their wisdom, is engulfed,
